title: The Bengals are the only AFC team Trevor Lawrence has never beaten
summary: Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence has faced the Bengals three times in his NFL career and none of those contests has ended with a Jacksonville victory.
full_text: ''' Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence has faced the Bengals three times in his NFL career and none of those contests has ended with a Jacksonville victory. The Bengals won at home by a field goal in Lawrence's rookie season in a game best remembered as the one that was followed by then-coach Urban Meyer staying behind to have a little fun at a local bar rather than travel home with his team. The Bengals won in overtime behind Jake Browning in 2023 and Browning came in to rally them to a win again after Joe Burrow was injured late in last season's game in Cincinnati. Those results make the Bengals the only AFC team that Lawrence has not beaten since he entered the league as the first overall pick in 2021 and he acknowledged that's something he's aware of during a Wednesday press conference. “We gotta make it turn. We gotta go win it ," Lawrence said. "It’s definitely something that, when you’re going into the game, you think about. You’re not sitting there thinking about it every second of the day and all week, but I’ve thought about it. It’s a team that we haven’t beat. We lost a tough one there early in the season last year and that's one that we definitely we want back. All those things you think about and you move on. You have to put your energy toward something that actually does something for you, which is preparing and getting ready to go." Both teams are 2-1 heading into Sunday's game, so it's an opportunity for the Jags to get an early leg up in the AFC playoff race in addition to getting Lawrence a clean sweep of the conference.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jalon Daniels aims to be "the thermostat" in his first NFL start
summary: There were 10 quarterbacks selected in the 2026 draft, but the first rookie quarterback to start a game during the 2026 season will not be part of that group.
full_text: There were 10 quarterbacks selected in the 2026 draft, but the first rookie quarterback to start a game during the 2026 season will not be part of that group. Baker Mayfield's dislocated thumb has put Jalon Daniels in line to start for the Buccaneers against the Packers on Sunday. Daniels was not selected after spending six years and appearing in 49 games at Kansas, but he beat out Jake Browning for the backup job this summer and will now get a chance to run an NFL offense before any of his peers. On Wednesday, Daniels said Mayfield advised him to "just stay composed, play as yourself, don't try to be anybody else besides yourself" once he is out on the field and Daniels said his time at Kansas has taught him that he has to be proactive rather than reactive. "I think that one thing I learned in college was, you can't be the thermometer, you have to be the thermostat," Daniels said, via a transcript from the team. "You have to be someone who comes in and is able to set the temperature of the room, not test the room and try to be able to blend in with it. If a team is low, I have to be able to pick it up to be able to make sure that they're even. If we're high, then I have to be able to be low to be able to make sure that we're even. I try to be as even-keel as possible. I think that being able to go out there and have that even-keeled feel, the team around you feels that." An 0-3 start has led to a lot of talk about hot seats in Tampa, so the best thing Daniels could do in his first start is cool things down by helping the team win a game. That's a big ask, but so is going from undrafted to starting a game a month into your rookie season and Daniels has already pulled that off.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cowboys send Steelers 2027 sixth-round pick and 2028 second-round pick for Joey Porter Jr.
summary: One of the NFL's best young cornerbacks is heading to Dallas, and Pittsburgh is getting two picks.
full_text: The Cowboys are sending the Steelers two draft picks in the trade that brings cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to Dallas. The Steelers will get a 2027 sixth-round pick and 2028 second-round pick, according to multiple reports. The 2027 sixth-round pick is the Steelers' own sixth-rounder, which they had previously traded to the Cowboys as part of the George Pickens deal. For the Cowboys, it's a move that's about bolstering the defense immediately with a player who's in the final year of his contract, whereas for the Steelers it's about acquiring future draft capital for a player who clearly wanted more money than the Steelers were going to be willing to pay. Whether the Cowboys pay that money remains to be seen. It would be unusual to trade for a player in the last year of his contract and not give him an extension, but the Cowboys could also be thinking that they'll get the rest of this season out of Porter and then evaluate whether to sign him to a long-term deal or let him walk in free agency. The Cowboys could be calculating that getting one good season out of Porter this year and then letting him leave for a lucrative contract with another team wouldn't be the worst thing, as that would likely bring them a third-round compensatory pick in 2028. Essentially, they'd be renting Porter for one season and only paying him the $3.924 million salary on the final year of his contract, at the price of moving down from the second to the third round in 2028. For the Steelers, they're losing one of their most talented players, but it had become clear that things weren't going to work out for Porter in Pittsburgh. He was unhappy with his contract and still hasn't played this season, officially because of a back injury — a back injury that the Steelers may have calculated was not going to heal until they gave him the contract he wanted. Whether Porter gets that contract in Dallas this year, in Dallas next offseason, or with some other team next offseason, he's now a Cowboy, and the Steelers have acquired two draft picks for a player who wanted out.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Steelers trade Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys
summary: Contract impasse ends with Porter being sent to a new team.
full_text: ' Last year, once the Cowboys realized that linebacker Micah Parsons wasn't going to play without a new contract, Dallas traded him. This year, the Steelers apparently have realized that cornerback Joey Porter Jr. wouldn't be playing without a new contract. And so they're trading him. Per multiple reports, the Steelers are sending Porter to the Cowboys. The full terms have yet to emerge. The separate question will be whether the Cowboys will give Porter the contract he couldn't get in Pittsburgh. Dallas could decide to ride it out in 2026, with Porter making $3.924 million. Then, they could apply the franchise tag in 2027. It's hard to imagine the Cowboys tradining for a player who apparently doesn't intend to play until he gets a new deal. The common link between Porter, a second-round pick in 2023, and Parsons is that both are represented by David Mulugheta of Athletes First. Mulugheta also represents receiver George Pickens, who was traded by the Steelers to the Cowboys in May 2025. The Cowboys haven't given Pickens a new deal. For 2026, they tagged him. For receivers, the franchise tender is well below market value. It is for cornerbacks, too. Much will be revealed in the coming hours. For now, the most important point is that the impasse between the Steelers and Porter has ended with Porter being sent to a new team.
author: Mike Florio

title: 3-0 Vikings are a game away from a dubious record
summary: The Vikings have scratched and clawed their way to a 3-0 record.
full_text: The Vikings have scratched and clawed their way to a 3-0 record. Dating back to last year, Minnesota has won eight in a row. They've done it with defense and special teams. Their offense, to date, has not been good enough. Via NBC Sports research, the Vikings could become the first team in the Super Bowl era to win four straight games without gaining 250 or more yards. Currently, the Vikings have the worst offense in the NFL, with an average output of 238.3 yards per game. (The Titans rank 31st, with 249.3.) Yes, the Vikings are prevailing in the only stat that matters: points scored vs. points allowed, one game at a time. The offense nevertheless needs to improve. If/when it does, the Vikings could emerge as a true contender. For now, wins happening without a high-powered offense become money in the bank for January. If they can ever pull the cord on the Kevin O'Connell lawnmower, Minnesota will be able to play with — and to beat — anyone.
author: Mike Florio

title: Five Rams missed practice on Wednesday
summary: The Rams are banged up in advance of Sunday's key game at the Eagles.
full_text: ''' The Rams are banged up in advance of Sunday's key game at the Eagles. Five players didn't practice on Wednesday. Defensive tackle Aaron Donald skipped the session with a back issue. Cornerback Jaylen Watson's Week 3 shoulder injury caused him to miss practice on Wednesday. Tight ends Colby Parkinson (knee/shoulder) and Terrance Ferguson (ankle) also didn't practice. Receiver Davante Adams took the day off, with the team dubbing it "rest." At the end of a long catch and run against Denver, he seemed to pull up. Still, there was no calf or hamstring injury disclosed. (Adams missed the final three games of the 2025 season with a hamstring injury.) Receiver Puka Nacua was officially limited with what continues to officially be called a hip injury. In reports, it's often called a groin problem. The 1-2 Rams, after playing the 2-1 Eagles, host the 3-0 Bill on Monday night to cap Week 5.
author: Mike Florio

title: Ted Cruz claims the reaction to his appearance on College GameDay was "overwhelmingly positive"
summary: Earlier this month, ESPN gave Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) an extended platform on its marquee college football show, College GameDay.
full_text: Earlier this month, ESPN gave Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) an extended platform on its marquee college football show, College GameDay . It did not go well. But Cruz, exercising the kind of fact-defying delusion that only politicians can, claims it went incredibly well. “ The response was overwhelmingly positive ,” Cruz told Front Office Sports , via Drew Lerner of Awful Announcing . “And the critics were mostly partisans who were just engaged in partisan games. It’s a little ridiculous to say, ‘Gosh, College GameDay should not talk about college sports,’ which is what we were talking about, and the rules that govern college sports and bringing — saving college sports. That’s what the whole show is about.” The response, Ted, was overwhelmingly negative. Both in person, where he was booed and subjected to a "Ted you suck" chant, and among those who were perplexed to see a football pregame show morph into a one-sided episode of Face The Nation . No one wanted to hear from Cruz in the hours before a full slate of college football games, and it was shameful for ESPN to let Cruz push for the passage of the bill without giving equal time to the opposition. And, yes, it's easy for Cruz to dismiss the negativity as "partisan." But this is, as Cruz likes to point out, a bipartisan bill. The opposition is bipartisan, too. As is the public's general disdain for Cruz, who keeps getting elected only because he's a Republican in a blood-red state.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kirk Cousins has seven consecutive victories as a starter
summary: Kirk Cousins is still a bridge quarterback for the Raiders, holding down the starting job until No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is ready.
full_text: Kirk Cousins is still a bridge quarterback for the Raiders, holding down the starting job until No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is ready. Alex Smith did that for Patrick Mahomes for one season, and Aaron Rodgers held off Jordan Love for three seasons. Cousins has already served in that role once, starting 14 games for the Falcons in 2024 before they turned to first-round rookie Michael Penix. (Cousins ended up starting eight games last season when Penix was injured.) With the Raiders off to a 3-0 start, though, no one is calling for Mendoza. “We’re just worried about playing the next game, and [Cousins is] playing this next game,” Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said, via Mark Anderson of the Associated Press. “Fernando’s ready to go when called upon .” Cousins has won seven games in a row, the league's longest active streak. He can become the first quarterback since the 1970 merger to win four consecutive games for two teams in the same streak. Cousins has thrown nine touchdown passes and three interceptions and his passer rating of 107.2 ranks eighth. “That’s the great part about this league is you’ve got to go out every single week and prove it to yourself, prove it to everyone else,” Cousins said. “So I’ve never really felt like anything was going to be handed to me or given to me. You've got to go out and play at that level, and I think the opportunity was what I was more interested in, was just having an opportunity to go see. But you've got to go do it.”
author: Charean Williams

title: Jalen Carter has a hairline fracture in his wrist
summary: Officially, Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter fully participated in practice with a wrist injury.
full_text: Officially, Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter fully participated in practice with a wrist injury. Unofficially, Carter has a hairline fracture in his wrist. That's the word from Jeff McLane of the Philadelphia Inquirer. Per the report, the injury happened in Week 1. Carter has played the last two games with a soft case. McLane adds that Carter's playing time has decreased. Carter had 66 snaps (94 percent) in Week 1 against the Commanders. In Week 2 at Tennessee, he was on the field for 41 snaps (77 percent). On Monday night at the Bears, Carter took part in 51 snaps (71 percent). Carter has appeared on all injury reports since Week 1, with the wrist issue disclosed. His participation has increased from limited to full. Asked on Wednesday whether the injury has been an issue for Carter, Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said, "There's no way it can't be, but to be honest with you, he's done better than I thought he would with it." They'll need him on Sunday against a Rams team that is surely desperate to avoid falling to 1-3.
author: Mike Florio

title: Seahawks S Julian Love returns to limited practice
summary: Seahawks safety Julian Love returned to practice on Wednesday.
full_text: Seahawks safety Julian Love returned to practice on Wednesday. He was a limited participant. Love strained a calf muscle at Thursday's practice and missed Sunday's loss to the Commanders. He has two interceptions in two games. The Seahawks practiced without safety Ty Okada (hamstring). Running back George Holani (rib), running back Jadarian Price (chest), defensive tackle Jarran Reed (foot), defensive tackle Leonard Williams (rest) and guard Grey Zabel (groin) were limited. author: Charean Williams

title: Mike Macdonald on Rashid Shaheed's limited production: "The ball will find him"
summary: In June, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said he was "excited to see" what receiver Rashid Shaheed would do in the offense, given the benefit of having the full offseason and training camp to prepare for his first full year with the team.
full_text: In June, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said he was " excited to see " what receiver Rashid Shaheed would do in the offense, given the benefit of having the full offseason and training camp to prepare for his first full year with the team. Through three games, Shaheed's offensive production has been limited to six catches for 53 yards. On Wednesday, Macdonald was asked about Shaheed's numbers. “I don’t know what exactly his numbers are," Macdonald said. "I know the ball's finding [Jaxon Smith-Njigba] a lot right now. Sheed’s doing a great job. Because of the question, I'm assuming you're thinking the ball's not finding him as much, but it will. I think we’ve just got to stick to our process. There’s always something that maybe we want to improve in our game, but we’ve just got to keep attacking it, stick with it, make some tweaks in how we approach everything and trust that the ball goes in the right direction and it'll find him, but he's doing a good job.” In contrast, Smith-Njigba has 27 catches for 405 yards and six touchdowns. And Cooper Kupp has eight catches for 101 yards and a touchdown. Shaheed also contributes on special teams, with seven punt returns for 67 yards and seven kickoff returns for 190. Still, the full contribution seems to be falling short of the $17 million per year in compensation that Shaheed is receiving.
author: Mike Florio

title: Marvin Mims, Jaylen Waddle had full participation Wednesday
summary: Broncos wide receiver Marvin Mims returned to full participation at Wednesday's practice.
full_text: Broncos wide receiver Marvin Mims returned to full participation at Wednesday's practice. Mims has not played since Week 1 due to a foot injury. He had limited practices all of last week and was questionable to play against the Rams but was inactive. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (foot) and running back J.K. Dobbins (hip) also were full participants Wednesday. Coach Sean Payton said Waddle is "doing great." Outside linebacker Dondrea Tillman (hamstring) was the only Denver player not to practice.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jim Harbaugh, to no surprise, spoke to John Harbaugh before J.J. McCarthy trade
summary: Before the 2024 draft, former Michigan coach Jim Harbaugh had plenty of glowing things to say about former Michigan quarterback J.J.
full_text: Before the 2024 draft, former Michigan coach Jim Harbaugh had plenty of glowing things to say about former Michigan quarterback J.J. McCarthy. So it's no surprise that Jim Harbaugh had many positive things to say about McCarthy to Harbaugh's brother, John, before John's Giants traded for McCarthy. "I mean, John called me and asked me ," Harbaugh told reporters on Wednesday. "I said, you know, John, I love you. I love J.J. I think you guys would be . . .' so, really, I'm telling you the same thing that I told my brother." For whatever reason, things didn't work for McCarthy in Minnesota. But they worked for McCarthy in Michigan. Maybe McCarthy responds better to the Harbaugh rah-rah style. Maybe McCarthy's second act with the Giants will go better than his first NFL stint. However it goes, McCarthy needed a fresh start. And playing for Jim Harbaugh's brother may be the next best thing to playing for Jim Harbaugh.
author: Mike Florio

title: Zack Baun, DeVonta Smith miss practice for Eagles
summary: The Eagles were missing several players at Wednesday's practice, including linebacker Zack Baun.
full_text: The Eagles were missing several players at Wednesday's practice, including linebacker Zack Baun. Baun missed practice with a concussion. title: Aaron Donald misses practice with a sore back
summary: The Rams got wide receiver Puka Nacua back on the practice field Wednesday, but they were missing an important part of their defense.
full_text: ''' The Rams got wide receiver Puka Nacua back on the practice field Wednesday, but they were missing an important part of their defense. Head coach Sean McVay said that defensive tackle Aaron Donald would sit out their first practice ahead of Sunday's game against the Eagles. McVay declined to speculate about whether Donald is at any risk of missing the game in Philadelphia. "Just taking it a day at a time," McVay said, via Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com. "I wouldn't want to say anything of that nature yet, but I think the back's a little bit sore. And he's as tough as it gets, and so I'll continue to have updates as the week goes." Donald did not play in Week 1 as he was still ramping up after deciding to come out of retirement late in the summer. He had four tackles, a tackle for loss and a quarterback hit in the last two games.
author: Josh Alper

title: Drake Maye: I love playing for Mike Vrabel, that's not going to change
summary: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel dismissed a report that he has issues with quarterback Drake Maye during a Wednesday press conference by saying that coaching Maye is the reason he's in New England and Maye got his chance to comment on it later in the day.
full_text: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel dismissed a report that he has issues with quarterback Drake Maye during a Wednesday press conference by saying that coaching Maye is the reason he's in New England and Maye got his chance to comment on it later in the day. While Vrabel said he didn't "have much to add to that about a comment from an unnamed source," Maye's response avoided discussion of where the report came from and focused on how much he likes playing for the coach. "Coach Vrabel’s been one of the best football coaches I’ve had in my life," Maye said, via a transcript from the team. "I think Coach Vrabel’s been one of the biggest things as to why this has been so enjoyable for me is playing for Coach. I think we all feel that way in the locker room. He pushes us hard. I’ve loved playing for him, and it’s not going to change. It hasn’t changed, and it won’t change. The way he pushes me, and he coaches the quarterbacks in a way that I really respect, and I’m looking forward to getting going, proving to Coach that I can lead this football team and play good football." Maye also fielded questions about whether an injury to his shoulder is contributing to his poor play so far this season and there will continue to be questions about what's bothering a player who finished second in MVP voting last year until he starts playing at that level again.
author: Josh Alper

title: Keon Coleman out of practice for Bills, Deone Walker limited

title: Cowboys practice without CBs Shavon Revel, Cobie Durant
summary: With Nico Collins returning to practice for the Texans, the Cowboys could use cornerback Shavon Revel this week.
full_text: With Nico Collins returning to practice for the Texans, the Cowboys could use cornerback Shavon Revel this week. They already likely will play another week without Cobie Durant (hamstring). Revel was at practice for the portion open to media, but he officially did not practice. He was listed with right knee and right ankle injuries. Revel appeared to hyperextend his knee as he flew out of bounds while chasing Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers. Ameer Speed and Caelen Carson replaced Revel. Durant and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) also did not practice Wednesday. Safety Malik Hooker (fractured forearm) was limited in his return to practice. Outside linebacker James Houston (shoulder) was a full participant.
author: Charean Williams

title: Falcons DT Gervon Dexter agrees to four-year extension
summary: Defensive tackle Gervon Dexter has made a good impression on the Falcons in his first three games as a member of the team.
full_text: '' Defensive tackle Gervon Dexter has made a good impression on the Falcons in his first three games as a member of the team. Agents Drew and Jason Rosenhaus told ESPN that Dexter has agreed to a four-year contract extension with the team. The deal is worth $78 million $78 million and includes $46.5 million in guaranteed money. Dexter joined the Falcons in a trade with the Bears on August 30. He was a 2023 second-round pick in Chicago and the Falcons sent defensive back Clark Phillips and a fifth-round pick to the Bears in the deal. Dexter has seven tackles, a half-sack and a pass defensed through the first three weeks of the season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Derrick Henry: Facing the Titans will be "a crazy moment"
summary: Ravens running back Derrick Henry will do something he's never done before this weekend.
full_text: Ravens running back Derrick Henry will do something he's never done before this weekend. Henry will play against the Titans for the first time. He was a 2016 second-round pick in Tennessee and won the 2020 offensive player of the year award during his eight seasons with the team, but the Ravens did not play his former team in his first two seasons with Baltimore. Henry joked on Wednesday that "it's a whole different logo" when asked about the emotions involved in facing his first NFL team, but then admitted that there will be a little extra feeling come Sunday. "It's going to be a crazy moment to be playing against the team that I came in the league playing for," Henry said. "But I ain't trying to make too much of it, though. . . . It's still like family there. So it's always love, but it ain't going to be much love on Sunday." Henry called his departure from the Titans "bittersweet" because they didn't make an effort to keep him. That may be a decision they regret as Henry has run for 3,817 yards and scored 40 touchdowns for the Ravens and they'll regret it even more if he runs wild again on Sunday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Sean McVay says NFL told him pass interference should not have been called on Josh Wallace
summary: The call negated what appeared to be a game-sealing interception for the Rams and set up the Broncos' game-winning touchdown.
full_text: '' The game-changing pass interference call on Rams cornerback Josh Wallace was a bad call, according to Rams head coach Sean McVay. McVay said today that the league office told him pass interference should not have been called on Wallace. The penalty was huge, as it negated what would have been Wallace's interception with 1:09 remaining in the game and the Rams leading 26-23. Instead of the Rams getting the ball back and almost certainly winning, the penalty gave the Broncos first-and-goal, setting up a touchdown and a 30-26 Broncos win. Wallace did make contact with Broncos wide receiver Pat Bryant, although it was the kind of contact that frequently goes un-called, and Bryant also made contact with Wallace and could have been flagged for offensive pass interference. Bryant acknowledged that he flopped to sell the call . The controversial call was one of the biggest penalties of this NFL season. And, according to McVay, the NFL now says it was a flag that should not have been thrown.
author: Michael David Smith

title: CB Christian Gonzalez, QB Drake Maye have shoulder injuries, but Maye says he's fine
summary: Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez did not practice on Wednesday because of a shoulder injury.
full_text: Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez did not practice on Wednesday because of a shoulder injury. In three games, he has eight tackles and five passes defensed. Defensive tackle Christian Barmore (shoulder) and offensive tackle Morgan Moses (foot) also didn't practice. Quarterback Drake Maye has a right shoulder injury, but he was a full participant Wednesday. It's the first time he's been on the report this season. Maye, who has one touchdown and six interceptions, said the shoulder is not factor in his struggles. "No, it hasn’t," Maye said, via a transcript from the team. "I don’t think it impacts my decision-making, and that’s what makes and breaks play for quarterbacks. I don’t feel like we’re struggling to move the ball. I think we’re turning the football over, doing things that are preventing us from scoring touchdowns, and I think that’s one of the biggest things for me. I think we’ve had a history of good football when we don’t turn the football over, playing good football and finding ourselves on the right side of games. So, that’s the biggest thing, and I’m looking forward to another good week of practice. I felt good out there today." The Patriots list linebacker Christian Elliss (chest), fullback Reggie Gilliam (knee), linebacker Dre'Mont Jones (shoulder), tight end Eli Raridon (thigh), safety Brenden Schooler (back) and safety Craig Woodson (shoulder) were limited. Schooler begins his return to play off the non-football injury list, but is not eligible to play this week.
author: Charean Williams

title: Rams expect Puka Nacua to play in Week 4
summary: It looks like wide receiver Puka Nacua will be back in the Rams' lineup this week.
full_text: ''' It looks like wide receiver Puka Nacua will be back in the Rams' lineup this week. Nacua has missed the last two games and the last two weeks of practice with what's been referred to as both a hip and a groin injury, but head coach Sean McVay said at a press conference that he will take part in Wednesday's practice on a limited basis. McVay also said that he expects Nacua to play against the Eagles in Philadelphia on Sunday. That will be a welcome development for the Rams as they try to even their record at 2-2. Konata Mumpfield had four catches for 93 yards and a touchdown against the Broncos in Week 3, but Davante Adams has carried a heavy load with Nacua out and the Rams' overall offensive capabilities will be raised if they have both of the wideouts on the field this weekend.
author: Josh Alper

title: Tony Pollard, Tyjae Spears did not practice for Titans on Wednesday
summary: The Titans did not have either of their top two running backs on the field for Wednesday’s practice.
full_text: The Titans did not have either of their top two running backs on the field for Wednesday’s practice. But they may still be OK for this week’s game against the Ravens. Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears did not participate to start the practice week. But head coach Robert Saleh told reporters earlier in the day that he’s “ not overly concerned about Sunday ” for both players. Pollard has a foot injury while Spears is dealing with an ankle injury. Pollard has taken 38 carries for 173 yards with six receptions for 22 yards. Spears has 58 yards on 13 carries along with four receptions for 41 yards. Additionally, defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers (back) did not participate on Wednesday. Saleh similarly told reporters that he’s not too concerned about Franklin-Myers’ availability for Sunday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: John Harbaugh on releasing OBJ: "It just wasn't working for us"
summary: On Tuesday, the Giants released receiver Odell Beckham Jr.
full_text: '' On Tuesday, the Giants released receiver Odell Beckham Jr. On Wednesday, Giants coach John Harbaugh addressed the decision to pull the plug on OBJ 2.0. "I had, you know, a great conversation with Odell, and, you know, it's tough," Harbaugh told reporters. "But we just weren't getting enough, you know? It just wasn’t working for us . And like I told him, I wanted to be able to get more. I wanted him to be able to do more. I wanted to get him on the field more. We just, whatever reason, we weren't able to do it. Put it on us. We weren't able to get it done. But at this point in time, that's kind of where we were. And we needed to move on." Harbaugh was reminded of last week's comments regarding the possibility of Beckham getting more chances in the offense. "Well, I think I said I hoped he would get more chances," Harbaugh said, "That's what I said. So nothing changed. I did hope he would get more chances. And he didn't. You know, and that's where we stood. So I felt like, that being the case, we're not gonna be able to get it done. Roster spot-wise, we need more out of that spot, and that's what we're gonna do. Nothing about Odell. Nothing that he could do, in that sense. It's just we weren't able to get it done, make it fit, make it work, whatever you want to call it. And I was hoping we could, and we didn't." (And, yes, Harbaugh did say he hoped it would happen on Sunday.) The problem is that Beckham was too deep on the depth chart to not play special teams. They needed someone who, when only getting limited snaps on offense, could do more in the third phase — like Braxton Berrios and Charlie Jones will. The injuries made it necessary to tweak the roster to ensure that the guys at the back end were able to contribute, in some fashion. Through three games, OBJ had become forgotten. And it's unlikely he'll return. His number, 13, already has been re-issued to quarterback Jake Haener, whose prior number (18) was claimed by new backup quarterback J.J. McCarthy.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cowboys place S Jalen Thompson, DT Jonathan Bullard on IR
summary: The Cowboys placed safety Jalen Thompson and defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard on injured reserve, the team announced Wednesday.
full_text: The Cowboys placed safety Jalen Thompson and defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard on injured reserve, the team announced Wednesday. Both players must miss at least four games. Thompson's hamstring injury could keep him out even longer than that. Bullard, who missed much of training camp with a groin/abdominal injury, has a calf injury that will sideline him. Thompson's injury is the latest hit the Cowboys have taken at the position. Malik Hooker (fractured forearm) has missed the past two games, and P.J. Locke (foot) is on injured reserve. Cornerbacks Shavon Revel (knee/ankle) and Cobie Durant (hamstring) are also injured. The Cowboys announced that they have signed defensive tackle Elijah Garcia to the active roster from the practice squad. They also signed defensive backs Alex Austin, Tyrek Funderburk and Juanyeh Thomas to the practice squad.
author: Charean Williams

title: Why the Cowboys traded for CB Joey Porter Jr. from the Steelers and where his contract stands
summary: Dallas scooped up the Steelers' disgruntled top cornerback late Wednesday night before Week 4
full_text:
Dallas Cowboys owner/general manager Jerry Jones teased making a major move after the team's 37-20 Week 2 win over the Washington Commanders . Jones made good on his word late Wednesday night by acquiring cornerback Joey Porter Jr . from the Pittsburgh Steelers for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick, a team source confirmed. The news was first reported by The Ringer .
Porter Jr. did not suit up for the Steelers in the first three weeks because he was in a staredown with Pittsburgh to secure a long-term contract extension. The 26-year-old, the first pick of the second round in the 2023 NFL Draft , enters the final year of his rookie deal this season and reportedly sought more than $30 million per year on a new deal.
Six cornerbacks in the entire league have such a contract, and Pittsburgh maintains a tradition of not negotiating multi-year extensions during a season. Porter Jr. held himself out of play with what the team officially listed as both back and condition issues, and he will now be a Cowboy.
Porter Jr. has a solid argument for a substantial raise despite no Pro Bowl selections and just three career interceptions in three seasons — one each year. He led the NFL in passer rating against as the primary defender in coverage in 2025, among 128 players with at least 60 pass attempts thrown their way, with a 49.1 passer rating allowed. No other corner allowed a sub-50 passer rating against, so Porter can claim he was in a different stratosphere as a cover corner than the rest of the league the last time he took the field.
Porter Jr. ranked ahead of other All-Pro and Pro Bowl cornerbacks who have received big paydays in recent years, like Patrick Surtain II (four years, $96 million), Derek Stingley Jr . (three years, $90 million) and Christian Gonzalez (four years, $135 million). Gonzalez's $33.75 million average per-year salary is the highest among all NFL corners. Porter Jr.'s 48.1% career completion percentage allowed ranks as the fourth-lowest in the NFL since he entered the league in 2023 among those with at least 150 passes thrown their way, per CBS Sports Research.
Porter Jr. is currently set to become a free agent next offseason, but the Cowboys could franchise tag him if they fail to come to an agreement on a new deal before the start of the 2027 league year. The 2027 offseason will be a tricky one for Dallas, with Pro Bowl wide receiver George Pickens also set to become a free agent. Dallas could tag him for a second year in a row if the two sides fail to reach a new long-term agreement with the 25-year-old wideout.
Dallas currently possesses $20.8 million in cap space in 2026, the eighth-most in the NFL per OverTheCap.com. Whatever the Cowboys don't use this year can be rolled over to their 2027 cap ledger, which currently sits at -$13.1 million. Simply rolling over this year's surplus would get the Cowboys into the green from a team cap sheet perspective.
Additional contract restructures for cornerback DaRon Bland , tight end Jake Ferguson and tight end Kenny Clark , all of whom restructured in the 2026 offseason, could free up additional room. The same goes for defensive tackle Quinnen Williams', quarterback Dak Prescott's and wide receiver CeeDee Lamb's existing, multi-year deals.
So yes, there is a world where the Cowboys could extend one or both of Pickens and Porter Jr., or extend one and tag the other next spring. How both of these negotiations go will be worth pulling out the popcorn and following closely. Both Pickens and Porter Jr. are represented by agent David Mulugheta and his Athletes First firm. That's the same representation All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons had when negotiations between him and the Cowboys broke down and ultimately ended with him being traded to the Green Bay Packers a week before the 2025 season began.
Mulugheta, Jerry, and Stephen Jones mended the fence when Pickens signed his franchise tag tender and showed up for mandatory minicamp this offseason. If Porter Jr. were to depart in free agency on a top-of-the-line contract, Dallas could receive a 2028 third-round compensatory pick back. That would mean they would have moved back roughly 20ish spots in the draft to rent Porter Jr. for the 2026 season in that scenario.
The why behind the Cowboys trading for Porter Jr. entering Week 4 is pretty simple. Jones will turn 84 years old on Oct. 13, and he's desperate to make a significant push for a fourth Super Bowl ring while he still can. Through three weeks, Dallas is 1-2 with the NFL's No. 7 scoring offense (29.3 points per game) and the No. 25 scoring defense (27.3 points per game allowed).
Since trading Parsons at the start of the 2025 season, the Cowboys are allowing the most points per game (29.7), the second-most total yards per game (378.5) and the third-most passing yards per game (244.9). They've hauled in the second-fewest interceptions (6) in that span.
This season, the 2026 Cowboys defense has become the third team since 1963 (when team sacks became an officially tracked stat) to allow 375-plus total yards per game (387.0, third-worst in the NFL), have two or fewer sacks (2, third-fewest in the NFL) and no interceptions (tied for last in the NFL) through a season's first three games. Per CBS Sports Research, the other two such teams are the 1976 New York Jets and the 2022 Arizona Cardinals . Neither of those teams hit the five-win mark when their defenses started off this worrisome through the first three games.
* Team sacks became an officially tracked statistic in 1963
The trade for Porter Jr. marks another key move in Dallas' roster churn to provide first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker the personnel he needs to turn the Cowboys' sagging defense around. A whopping 83% of Dallas' defensive snaps this season have come by players in either their first or second year with the Cowboys, the second-highest rate in the NFL behind only the New York Jets (85%) per CBS Sports Research.
Jones has invested 11 draft picks on defense, picks made in the draft or as trade compensation for current players, from the 2026 to 2028 drafts, with five of those picks coming from either the first or second round. Since trading Parsons in 2025, the Cowboys' record is 8-11-1, which ranks 21st out of the league's 32 teams.

Draft (92nd overall in 2026)
Draft (11th overall in 2026)
The Cowboys claimed to have all the confidence in the world in 2023 first-team All-Pro cornerback DaRon Bland and 2025 third-round pick corner Shavon Revel. But Dallas decided their team's CB1 wasn't in the building and went out to grab Porter Jr. to change that.
It will be interesting to see how the high-end man-coverage cornerback who prefers to go one-on-one against opposing receivers will fit in Parker's zone-coverage-based scheme with plenty of disguise looks. Dallas has run man coverage on 20.2% of their defensive snaps this season, the 12th-highest rate in the league. So there will be opportunities for Porter Jr. to do what he enjoys most while lining up as an outside corner in zone coverage as well. His presence could allow Parker to be even more creative schematically with hybrid looks that possess a mixture of man and zone coverage.
Injuries have ravaged Dallas' secondary early on this season, so the teammates Parker lines up with when he first hits the field, most likely on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 5 when Dallas hosts the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , may not be who he plays next to all year. Porter Jr.'s presence could also push Bland back to the slot where he lined up as a rookie in 2022 and intercepted five passes. Such a switch could also have a ripple effect of moving Downs from his hybrid nickel/linebacker lite role to deep safety. Perhaps veteran Cobie Durant's starting spot could come into question with Bland and Porter Jr. as mainstays for Dallas' defense.
What is clear is that Dallas' cornerback position is at its deepest since 2023, when 2019 NFL Defensive Player…
author: Garrett Podell

title: Joey Porter Jr. trade grades: Steelers win trade after getting coveted high pick from Cowboys
summary: Dallas will now have to pay up for Porter's extension
full_text:
Once again, the Steelers and Cowboys have pulled off a significant trade. The latest trade between the two iconic franchises took place late Wednesday night, when the Steelers traded cornerback Joey Porter Jr . to Dallas in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick.
The trade was a byproduct of Porter and the Steelers being unable to come to terms on a contract extension this summer. Porter -- who was entering the final year of his rookie contract -- did not practice during the summer and was inactive for each of Pittsburgh's first three games. Just hours prior to the trade, the Steelers had ruled Porter out of Thursday night's game against the Browns with a back injury.
Assuming Porter is healthy, the Cowboys are getting a quality starting cornerback who can immediately improve the backend of the defense. Dallas' defense could use some help, as they are currently 25th in the NFL in points allowed, 32nd in third-down efficiency, and 21st in red-zone efficiency.
The Steelers will move forward with veterans Asante Samuel Jr . and Jamel Dean as starting cornerbacks, with rookie Daylen Everette behind them.
Which team won this trade? Let's find out.
It's hard to give the Steelers a much higher grade. While Porter reportedly drove a hard bargain, it's safe to say that the Steelers could have avoided this mess if they had handled the situation with more urgency during the offseason. Ideally, the Steelers would have signed Porter before several other cornerbacks (most notably Christian Gonzalez ) received big paydays. Once that happened, it undoubtedly made extending Porter much more difficult.
In the end, the Steelers couldn't bring themselves to give Porter what he wanted, which is valid. As good as Porter is, he doesn't have elite ball skills (he has three career interceptions in three seasons), is known for being handsy with receivers (which has often led to holding and pass interference penalties) and has had injury issues. He also isn't a great tackler.
In addition to Porter's likely contract demands, teams were also reportedly scared off by the Steelers' demands. The Steelers probably wanted more than they got, but in the end, they secured 2027 draft capital in addition to a future second-round pick.
From a performance standpoint, losing Porter makes the Steelers a weaker team. But after the two sides couldn't agree to terms before Week 1, Porter essentially forced their hand. The Steelers had no choice but to trade him.
There are three big positives for the Steelers. They avoided overpaying Porter, have a promising cornerback on the roster in Everette, and have rid themselves of what was a massive distraction.
Outside of the fact that Jerry Jones loves making splashy trades, it's easy to see why the Cowboys made this happen. Dallas needs reinforcements in the secondary, and they were able to get a player who can address that issue now.
The Cowboys are a better team now than they were 24 hours ago. While Porter has his weaknesses, he is a very good player who -- at 26 years old -- should just be entering his prime. Specifically, Porter has excelled in man coverage. Having him in the fold should make a significant impact for a Cowboys team that is looking to bounce back after losing two of their first three games.
Dallas also deserves credit for not giving up a high draft pick in the 2027 draft. The Steelers likely weren't going to budge off a second-round pick, so the Cowboys made the best of a less-than-ideal situation by giving up a 2028 second-rounder.
Money is the biggest reason why the Cowboys lost this trade. Dallas already has some expensive players on payroll (including on the defensive side of the ball in Quinnen Williams , DaRon Bland and Kenny Clark ), and now, they're about to shell out even more money for a player who has never been selected to a Pro Bowl. Dallas also still has the pending George Pickens contract to address.
If Porter excels in Dallas and he can help the Cowboys make several deep playoff runs (including this year), Jones' latest gamble would have been well worth it. But if Porter fails to live up to his expected contract, this trade will be remembered as another situation where Jones bit off more than he can chew.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Steelers trading Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys for 2028 second-round pick and 2027 sixth-rounder
summary: Porter is getting a fresh start after a tumultuous ending in Pittsburgh
full_text:
Joey Porter Jr. , after months of speculation, has finally been traded. The Steelers are sending the veteran cornerback to the Cowboys , as first reported by The Ringer and confirmed by CBS Sports NFL writer Garrett Podell. Dallas will be sending a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick to Pittsburgh.
Porter is heading to a Cowboys team that is currently dealing with injuries to starting cornerback Cobie Durant. Durant is dealing with a hamstring strain and is not expected to face the Texans in Week 4. Dallas' defense is currently ranked 25th in the NFL in points allowed, 32nd in third-down efficiency, and 21st in red-zone efficiency.
This marks the third notable trade between the Cowboys and Steelers in recent seasons. The Steelers traded offensive tackle and former first-round pick Broderick Jones to Dallas this summer. In May of 2005, Pittsburgh traded wideout George Pickens to Dallas for third- and fifth-round picks.
The trade ends what has been a tumultuous several months for the Steelers and Porter, who reportedly turned down an offer from the Steelers this offseason that would have paid him slightly over $27 million for 2026. Porter's situation with the Steelers brought to mind Le'Veon Bell's infamous holdout, which ultimately led to him missing the entire 2018 season before signing with the Jets as a free agent in 2019. This time around, the Steelers were able to get something in exchange for their disgruntled player.
Porter and the Steelers couldn't agree on a long-term contract before Week 1, Pittsburgh's unofficial deadline to negotiate contracts. Porter held in during training camp and was inactive during the team's first three games, citing a back injury. The Steelers reportedly cleared Porter of the injury prior to Week 2, which fueled speculation about the real reason for Porter's absence on game days.
A Pittsburgh native, Porter is the son of Joey Porter, the former Pro Bowl pass rusher who played for the Steelers from 1999-2006. Porter Jr. starred at Penn State and was selected by the Steelers with the first pick of the second round in the 2023 NFL Draft .
Porter's reputation for being handsy with receivers was undoubtedly one of the reasons why he was still available at the start of the second round. And while he has had his share of holding/pass interference calls (especially during his rookie season), Porter has improved that area of his game.
Porter, who broke into the starting lineup as a rookie, was often tasked with guarding the opposition's best receiver during his time with the Steelers. And while he didn't make a ton of splash plays (he has just three career interceptions), Porter more often than not held his own in his respective matchups with some of the league's premier receivers, including Ja'Marr Chase , Tee Higgins , Zay Flowers, and Jerry Jeudy .
The Steelers will move forward at cornerback with Jalen Ramsey , Jamel Dean , Asante Samuel Jr. , Brandin Echols , and rookie third-round pick Daylen Everette , who shadowed Chase during the final series of Pittsburgh's Week 3 win over Cincinnati.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Russell Wilson explains why Giants' controversial J.J. McCarthy trade could be a 'great' fit
summary: The former Giants quarterback says New York needs McCarthy just as much as the former first-round pick needs a reset
full_text:
Adding J.J. McCarthy is not a move everyone agrees with , but this week on CBS Sports' "Set Hut," Super Bowl champion and former Giants quarterback Russell Wilson and Pro Bowler Kyle Long explained why the trade between New York and the Minnesota Vikings fits. The move comes after starting quarterback Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending knee injury that required surgery.
Wilson called the trade "interesting" and said it could be a "great" situation for McCarthy to restart his career. The job belongs to Dart when he returns from injury, but for now, McCarthy gets to learn under starter Jameis Winston and perhaps step into an on-field role. Winston and Wilson were teammates on the 2025 Giants.
Long says the understanding and messaging from the team needs to be clear to McCarthy that Winston is the starter and when "the guy with the diamonds," aka Dart, is back, he will be the starter.
"I think this will help J.J., too. I'm sure Jameis is going to give some of that advice and thoughts," Wilson said.
In college, McCarthy won a title under Jim Harbaugh at Michigan.
"I like it for coach (John) Harbaugh, too," Wilson said. "He's got a guy that he knows is a competitor, a high draft pick as a backup just in case."
McCarthy's rookie season ended before it could begin, suffering a season-ending knee injury before the regular season. In 2025, after Sam Darnold went to the Seattle Seahawks , McCarthy was named the starter in Minnesota. In Week 2, suffered another injury, this time a high ankle sprain that sidelined him for five games and later in the season a concussion and a hand injury caused more missed time.
In 10 games, he went 6-4 with a 57.6% completion rate, 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions. He did not play in 2026, losing the starting job to Kyler Murray .
And injuries are now what bring McCarthy to New York, beefing up a room that lost Dart to season-ending knee surgery.
"Look, they need him, and he needs them, so I think it's a good situation for him," Long said.

title: John Harbaugh explains Odell Beckham Jr. release: 'It just wasn't working for us'
summary: Beckham played just 20 offensive snaps and failed to record a catch during his three-game return to New York
full_text:
The New York Giants released one of their most popular players, parting ways with veteran wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr . OBJ returned to the franchise where he became a household name in the early 2010s, and while he made the final 53-man roster in August, he was on the field for just 20 offensive snaps through three games and didn't make a catch.
During New York's 12-7 victory over the Tennessee Titans , MetLife Stadium even erupted in "OBJ" chants. However, he played just six snaps and saw one target. Giants coach John Harbaugh addressed the decision to release the player who was once viewed as the best receiver in the NFL , saying it just "wasn't working for us."
"I had a great conversation with Odell, and it's tough," Harbaugh said, via SNY . "But we just weren't getting enough, you know? It just wasn't working for us. And like I told him, I wanted to be able to get more. I wanted him to be able to do more, I wanted to get him on the field more. Whatever reason, we weren't able to do it. Put it on us. We weren't able to get it done. But at this point in time, that's kind of where we were and we needed to move on."
Harbaugh previously indicated that Beckham could see more opportunities in the passing game. He was asked what had changed.
"Well, I think I said I hoped he would get more chances," Harbaugh said, "That's what I said. So nothing changed. I did hope he would get more chances. And he didn't. You know, and that's where we stood. So I felt like, that being the case, we're not gonna be able to get it done. Roster spot-wise, we need more out of that spot and that's what we're gonna do. Nothing about Odell. Nothing that he could do, in that sense. It's just we weren't able to get it done, make it fit, make it work, whatever you want to call it. And I was hoping we could, and we didn't."
There were some roster gymnastics to work through with Beckham's release. ESPN initially noted that the Giants had to make a decision on wide receiver and punt returner Braxton Berrios , who had quickly exhausted his practice-squad elevations. Sure enough, Berrios was signed to the active roster following OBJ's release, as was Charlie Jones . For some potential landing spots for Beckham, click here .
