title: Predicting NFL's first coaching change of 2026: Why Todd Bowles, Jim Harbaugh are in greatest danger
summary: Sluggish starts put these coaches in danger of becoming the first to lose their job
full_text:
The first head coach firing of the 2025 NFL season came on Oct. 13. The year before that, Oct. 8 was the first fateful day. With the calendar about to flip from September to October, history suggests at least one unfortunate coach will be out the door in the coming weeks, and there are a few candidates that may be in line for an in-season pink slip.
Some worked their way off scalding seats over the first three weeks of the 2026 season. Aaron Glenn (New York Jets) and Shane Steichen (Indianapolis Colts), for instance, both have a win under their belts and were competitive in their losses. They could be out the door by the end of the year, but the chances that these highly scrutinized leaders become the first casualties of the coaching carousel are slimmer than they appeared at the beginning of the month.
At the same time, surprisingly rough starts for a few teams placed new pressure on coaches to right the ship. The Chargers and Packers , for instance, have a combined one win despite opening the year as perceived postseason contenders.
Five of our NFL writers at CBS Sports convened for a roundtable discussion to determine which coaches are at the highest risk of becoming the first to lose their jobs in 2026. Here are the responses.
"The Buccaneers coach had arguably the hottest seat in the NFL coming into the season, and not much has changed. In fact, his seat is probably hotter. After going 8-9 and missing the playoffs last year, Bowles fired most of his staff, which is typically a last-ditch effort before the entire operation gets overhauled. The rearranging of the deck chairs hasn't done much to turn the tide in Tampa, with the Bucs stumbling to a 0-3 start to the season. Each of those losses has come in one-score games, and the organization just feels stale. With Baker Mayfield (thumb) dinged up, it may only get worse from here.
"I'd keep an eye on Week 5 when the Bucs travel to Dallas to face the Cowboys on 'Thursday Night Football' as a possible spot where a change could be made. If they fall to 0-5, that mini-bye after a Thursday night game — especially if the primetime loss is one-sided — has been a pocket where changes have been made in the past."
"Todd Bowles is a firing waiting to happen. Baker Mayfield is hurt, and he was playing poorly before that. The offensive line and the offensive ecosystem as a whole have regressed under new offensive coordinator Zac Robinson . Coaches can usually survive striking out on one coordinator who runs the other side of the ball — Bowles did after he hired and fired Josh Grizzard within the span of a year last season — but rarely can they do so two straight years without any postseason success.
"The defense has been largely good, which is a point in Bowles' favor, but let's see if it can hold up against improved competition in the coming weeks without Mayfield."
"The Chargers were supposed to have a team capable of winning the franchise's first playoff game since the Philip Rivers era. Instead, the Chargers are 0-3 and are employing an offense that looks like it came straight from 'The Longest Yard.' Justin Herbert has regressed, and it's quickly become apparent that Mike McDaniel and Jim Harbaugh are indeed an odd couple.
"The odds of Harbaugh being the first canned coach only increase when you consider the Chargers' upcoming four games are against the Seahawks , Broncos , Chiefs and Rams . It's possible the Chargers fire Harbaugh during their Week 7 bye if things don't improve by then. Would that lead to McDaniel becoming interim coach?"
"The Chargers are continuously the 'what if' team, with the league's top 'what if' quarterback in Justin Herbert. But 'what if' doesn't win football games. Los Angeles dropped to 0-3 after a 24-16 loss to the Buffalo Bills . Despite forcing five turnovers and sacking Josh Allen four times, L.A. couldn't win, and alarm bells are ringing. The Chargers have the sixth-worst completion percentage (59.1), are tied for the third-fewest passing touchdowns (3), and are tied for second in interceptions (4).
"The team is very concerning, and year after year, it seems they cannot reach, or even get close to, their ceiling. Jim Harbaugh took over as the head coach in 2024, and in the two seasons he's been there, the Chargers haven't made it past the wild card round, even when they had the talent to. If things keep going the way they are, Harbaugh will be looking for a new coaching job for 2027. Their schedule going forward isn't doing them any favors, and they could easily go 1-6, or worse, to start the season."
"The Packers committed to Matt LaFleur in the offseason with a multi-year contract extension, so moving on from him less than a year later would require team president Ed Policy to eat crow and likely leave the franchise on the hook for millions of dollars in guaranteed salary. But what about the start to this season suggests LaFleur belongs on the sideline? His only win came in overtime against the Jets , and he just sustained a Week 3 drubbing at the hands of the previously winless Falcons . The offense is a mess, the defense seems to have regressed and the path back to the playoffs is treacherous. There are three other legitimate contenders vying for the NFC North crown.
"LaFleur is the longest-tenured active coach without a Super Bowl appearance, and he only has one postseason win without Aaron Rodgers . Packers fans are losing confidence in his ability to turn the campaign around, and even if he did, the track record suggests there is nothing to be excited for in January. The last time the Packers made a coaching change, they fired Mike McCarthy in-season. LaFleur could be in for the same fate if this year continues its downward spiral."
author: Carter Bahns

title: What is with these funky NFL helmet decals?
summary: The NFL does a great job of making the game as safe as possible for its players. Concussion researchers have been brought on, making this a constant battle to keep athletes from experiencing head trauma. There are currently four helmet manufacturers that supply the league with headgear. They are Riddell and Schutt, plus newcomers Xenith […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - JANUARY 5: An Arizona Cardinals helmet is seen on the sidelines near the players bench during an NFL football game between the San Francisco 49ers and the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on January 5, 2025 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Bruce Yeung/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL does a great job of making the game as safe as possible for its players. Concussion researchers have been brought on, making this a constant battle to keep athletes from experiencing head trauma. There are currently four helmet manufacturers that supply the league with headgear. They are Riddell and Schutt, plus newcomers Xenith and VICIS. RELATED: CARDINALS HELMET CONCEPTS Ideas are essential in coming up with the latest gear, such as new materials. Today’s helmets are technological marvels compared to leather headgear or even the early plastic hats. The NFL has invested quite a bit in research on what is best for players to wear. Originally, the first headgear was actually a device to protect a player’s ears from getting torn off while another player was reaching from behind to make a tackle. From there, the “Morrill’s Nose Guard” was a contraption with a strap to protect a player from getting a broken nose. Crude helmets were made of leather, and as time wore on, more and more padding was installed. The Riddell Sporting Goods Company is credited with the invention of the first plastic helmets in 1939. However, there was a huge issue. The top of the helmet was flat, and when contact was made, the thin area below the ear hole would crack and break. More innovations would later come, and a very good, stable plastic helmet was the norm in 1952. The elimination of concussions was never the reason for a player to don a football lid. It simply made each impact less of a head-wrenching occurrence than worrying about eventual head trauma. Now helmets are tested using 3D digital imaging, which pushes the boundaries of technology. But each design has to include stability as well as comfort as a selling point. The NFL began to improve their helmet situation by starting the Head Health Challenge around 2013, co-sponsored by GE. Six companies were awarded $10 million each to study and diagnose the understanding of mild to moderate traumatic brain injury. Part of the study would be tp see how the brain reacts following these types of injuries and to identify which brain areas become disconnected after such injuries occur. Of course, the end game was to improve the safety of league players. Invasion of the new obstacles With innovations and components of these helmets, the landscape has altered the exterior of the pro football helmet, to say the least. What used to be two ear holes on each side plus four air holes drilled on the topside is now a series of specifically positioned air vents, creases, diamond-shaped ear holes, rear helmet ledge, Oakley logo tabs, duo chin strap snaps, extra facemask strap grommets, and flex panels. If you ever noticed the front of helmets today, they have this strange “tab” just above the visor that goes up towards the top of the headgear. This is a sensor pad called “insite analytics smart helmet technology,” which records and analyzes data that then gives reports to reduce head impact. This tab also has some give upon impact. But with all these new thingys on each helmet, it has caused some issues with adhering stripes and logos. What used to be a solid side area for any type of decal and fully unobstructed areas from front to back for stripes is now a complication of dodging various indents, holes, and that definitive “ledge” that runs across the back of each helmet designed as a stabilizer. Teams have had to shift their decals back more, or up more, or down towards the ear hole. Or a combination of all of the above. Some of these stickers even appear now to be installed at a bit of an angle. The proper placement is when a player’s head is staring straight ahead with his eyesight parallel with the ground. This makes the emblem level. Whether some teams have had to slightly downsize the decal circumference is not known. But “decal shifting” is a real thing now. Most NFL clubs have adjusted their decals and stripes Of course, this all depends on the emblem. Some teams haven’t had much of a decal movement. These include the Chicago Bears “C”, Green Bay’s “G” oval, the fleur-de-lis of New Orleans, San Francisco’s oval, the New York Football Giants “NY” design, the shield of Las Vegas, and, of course, Cleveland’s stickerless sides and the Steelers single blank left side. Other than that, all of these indents and added distractions have new issues to dodge. You may notice how Carolina’s panther design is now farther back on the helmet because one chin strap grommet plus two vent holes is now in the way. Or the dolphin logo for Miami is raised towards the top more in order to miss three different vent holes. The flying buffalo with the Buffalo Bills’ logo is a nightmare now, trying to miss three vent holes, one crease plus a chin strap grommet and a facemask strap. Houston’s longhorn trademark is pushed back really far in an attempt to miss the ear hole and assorted grommets plus two upper vents. With the Arizona helmets, the logo has been pushed back a smidge and has a very long air port to dodge plus an extended chin strap snap. The trick is to get the Cardinal head to appear level when on a player’s head, not sitting on a table. These same scenarios are continuous with the remainder of the league. Stripes are often cut when they travel over air vents to allow air to continue to flow in and out. Then the striping picks up and continues on. Many decals are also trimmed within the logo to allow these air access ports to proceed with their designed function when missing, as whichever hole is not an option. The main thing for a helmet is to protect the player. The equipment guy’s decal placement is his problem, instead of adding brain issues for the athlete.
author: Barry Shuck

title: Should the Cardinals bring in a seasoned cornerback?
summary: During training camp, there were several Arizona Cardinals cornerbacks who were on the mend from various injuries and ailments. But the consensus was that this position group was on the verge of being one of the league’s finest. Which was a huge requirement. Because Arizona resides in the most difficult division in the NFL, the […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - NOVEMBER 23: Garrett Williams #21 of the Arizona Cardinals celebrates after intercepting a pass in the end zone against the Jacksonville Jaguars during the NFL 2025 game at State Farm Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images) | Getty Images During training camp, there were several Arizona Cardinals cornerbacks who were on the mend from various injuries and ailments. But the consensus was that this position group was on the verge of being one of the league’s finest. Which was a huge requirement. Because Arizona resides in the most difficult division in the NFL, the NFC West, the defensive backfield is expected to be battle-tested each and every week. Great quarterbacks and even better receivers dot each roster in the division. RELATED: WHERE IS THE CARDINALS PASS RUSH? Will Johnson has shown that he can become one of the best cornerbacks in the division as well as in the league. Last year, Denzel Burke, proved his worth when he was thrust into the starting lineup; the experience of Garrett Williams was apparent, and Max Melton had games where he showed he belonged, although his play is more summed up as a roller coaster. However, in the Week 2 matchup against division foe Seattle Seahawks, Johnson suffered a neck injury in the loss and later was added to IR. It now looks like he could be gone for the remainder of the season. Which is a huge, huge loss to this defensive backfield. Burke has filled in for Johnson while Melton has been added to the starting lineup with Williams in the slot. Starling Thomas was brought up from the practice squad, and the team is now dependent on Kei’Trel Clark and Kalen King as key backups. But this cornerback group has shown anything but consistency in being able to stop an opposing offense’s passing attack. You might even say this group is in trouble. Part of the reason is not only the loss of Johnson, who was this defense’s best cornerback, but also having to shuffle guys around into different positions. Plus, it is a very young room. Williams has the most games played, with 36 NFL games and 27 starts. But all of the other corners have minimal game experience. Another issue is that the defensive front four is not getting a good pass rush, which means opposing quarterbacks are being given ample time to survey the field and wait for guys to complete their routes. The inability of the defensive line to collapse the pocket makes it harder for the cover guys to continue to shadow their guy, and opposing receivers have been open all day long in all three games. A connection we love to see 🙌 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/6CqyBmFama — San Francisco 49ers (@49ers) September 27, 2026 Not to mention, a guy like Burke should have been brought along gradually after being taken in the fifth round in last year’s NFL Draft. Instead, he was thrust into the starting lineup last year, which has carried over into 2026. In the above clip, Burke bit on the early wiggle by WR Mike Evans, but had the speed to catch up. However, he never even looked back at the ball. If he had looked back when Evans did, Burke could have swatted the ball away and possibly intercepted the pass. Instead, it was six for San Fran, which was the difference on the scoreboard at the final gun. After just three games, the Cardinals are allowing more yardage through the air with each contest. In Week 1 against the Los Angeles Chargers, QB Justin Herbert threw for 209 yards with a single touchdown and one interception by safety Andrew Wingard. Against the Seahawks, the backup quarterback, Drew Lock, threw for 235 yards and tossed three touchdowns against zero interceptions. After a 7-7 halftime score, Lock found receivers open all day long in the second half. In this past weekend’s division matchup against the San Francisco 49ers, QB Brock Purdy threw for 297 yards, connected on four touchdowns, again with zero interceptions. Lock talk 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/x8Z3Wg0tPO — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) September 21, 2026 That equates to seven touchdowns through the air in two straight games without any picks. Is anyone paying attention? This season will be over very soon if this is not addressed. Opposing quarterbacks are being given way too much time without a valid pass rush, and the defensive backs are not able to keep running with receivers who can change their routes, wave their arms, and be wide-ass open. Is anyone paying attention? So, what is the answer? Keep doing what they’re doing and expecting Burke, Williams, and Melton to take care of business? Or maybe sign a free agent? What about a trade? Johnson ain’t coming back this year, which means their best cornerback is gone. If the Cardinals truly want to salvage this year, they have got to bring in a seasoned veteran. Let’s start with the trade angle first. The Pittsburgh Steelers are in a contract dispute with their starting cornerback, Joey Porter Jr. (6’-2”, 193 pounds). He believes he is an elite corner and should be paid as such. Pittsburgh views him as just an above-average guy who hasn’t even sniffed a Pro Bowl. Porter has yet to suit up for the Steelers this year, even though he has been completely healthy each week. Porter was taken in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft and was named to the NFL “All-Rookie Team” after being a First Team All-Big 10 selection in his final year at Penn State. His father was an NFL player, so he’s got pedigree. Pittsburgh signed Porter to a four–year, $9.61 million deal that included $8.99 million guaranteed and a signing bonus of $3.99 million. Which means Porter is in his contract year. He had 43 total tackles as a rookie, 70 in his second season, and 52 last year. He has 3 career tackles for loss, 0 QB hits, 1 sack, 31 batted passes, 3 interceptions, 1 hurry, 2 pressures, and 17 missed tackles. Do any of these stats scream elite? What they do say is that Porter is an above-average cornerback who is aggressive, has speed, has no issue in the run-defense game, and is around the ball a lot, but his missed tackles are an issue. If the price is right, it is assumed that the Steelers would be all ears. They don’t believe he will suit up for them this year at all, period. He could step in that first week after arriving in the desert and take Johnson’s place. As Pittsburgh is preparing to face their second straight divisional game against the Cleveland Browns on Thursday Night Football, Porter Jr. was listed as a full participant on the Steelers’ injury report for the first time this season. The trade issue may be that the Steelers view Porter Jr., age 26, as more valuable than his production has been so far as an NFL player. If their wish list is a first-or second-round pick for the disgruntled cornerback, then they may just have to keep him. But perhaps a third-round pick may entice them to allow him to leave. As far as scouring the free agent market, the list has been picked over pretty well. Trevon Diggs (6’-1”, 203 pounds) leads the list. He is 29 years old so he has some years left in him. His last contract was for $19.4 million, but is currently on the Dallas Cowboys practice squad making $13,750 a week. Sean Murphy-Bunting (6’-0”, 195 pounds), age 29, has seven years of experience and was paid $4.45 million in his last gig with the Cardinals. He is on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers practice squad. Kader Kohou (5’-10”, 197 pounds) is the last of the top cornerback prospects who was paid $3.26 million. He currently resides on the practice squad of the Kansas City Chiefs. All practice squad players are available to every NFL club at all times. With all three of these candidates, all the Cardinals have to do is make a roster claim and then add him to the 53-man roster (after dropping a player). The current cornerback cast is struggling. Each game, the opposing QB increases his total passing yards and touchdown throws. The status quo is not an option.

title: Where is the @#?$%&0! Cardinals pass rush?
summary: Everyone who follows the Arizona Cardinals knows that this new offense, installed by head coach Mike LaFleur, will take time for the roster to get acclimated. Patience is assuredly needed. But the defense seems to be struggling in games so far this season. RELATED: SWEAT NAMED TO THE 2026 NFL TOP-100 One aspect that is […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - SEPTEMBER 27: Dante Stills #55 of the Arizona Cardinals enters the field before an NFL game against the San Francisco 49ers on September 27, 2026 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Everyone who follows the Arizona Cardinals knows that this new offense, installed by head coach Mike LaFleur, will take time for the roster to get acclimated. Patience is assuredly needed. But the defense seems to be struggling in games so far this season. RELATED: SWEAT NAMED TO THE 2026 NFL TOP-100 One aspect that is pretty glaring is the lack of a pass rush. Why? Part of the reason is the 3-4 formation. Oftentimes, their opponent is blocking five on three. This forces the defense to send an outside linebacker instead of using another defensive end, as is the norm in the 4-3. Yes, linebackers are speedier, but offensive linemen are employed along the front for a reason: they are huge. A guy like LB Baron Browning has good speed within his 255-pound frame, but how does he match up with a 325-pound offensive tackle when engaged? The use of the 3-4 also allows the other team to not have to keep their running back in to block. For a team like the San Francisco 49ers, being able to utilize RB Christian McCaffrey as an outlet receiver all game is gold. Five blockers can handle a rush, even when they send another defender, or even two. Their offensive line is never outmatched. Sweat had a critical penalty that could have swayed the game. We are not playing disciplined or inspired ball. — JamMasterJ (@Kosher_dude) September 28, 2026 First off the list is EDGE rusher Josh Sweat. Last year, this cat had 12 sacks, 17 QB hits, 13 tackles for loss, 9 hurries, 7 knockdowns, 2 batted passes, 540 snaps, and 28 pressures to go along with his 30 total tackles. This year so far? Three tackles, 0 sacks, 1 tackle for loss, 0 batted passes, 0 QB hits, 3 hurries, and 3 pressures. His Pro Football Focus (PFF) grade in a three-game sample is a lousy 42.3. In going back through film of the first three games, he just isn’t getting any type of penetration into the offensive backfield. He doesn’t have a good first step and absolutely no burst. What’s wrong with him? And he has played just 49% of all defensive plays, so it’s not like he is out there all game. Get this: Sweat is ranked 111th out of 112 EDGE rushers this year. Nose tackle Roy Lopez is the inside man. One thing he is doing is plugging his gap and being a good run stopper. So far, he has just eight tackles, four each against the Los Angeles Chargers and the Seattle Seahawks, but zero tackles in the San Fran contest. He is not a pass rusher, and never has been. He will stay home and patrol the “A” gap and is difficult to move. Offensive coordinators have to design runs to other gaps because Lopez ain’t moving. His stats this year: 8 total tackles, 0 tackles for loss, 0 batted passes, 0 sacks, 0 QB hits, 1 hurry, 1 pressure, and has played 62% of defensive snaps. Because other teams cannot run into his lane, his PFF grade is a respectable 71.4, which is 24 th among 125 qualified interior defensive linemen. His run-defense grade of 73.5 has him ranked 9th. DT Walter Nolen usually lines up on the left side. He is on a rotational basis, but he is getting his share of snaps with 110, which is 62%. The issue is that he isn’t getting much as far as penetration into the pocket. As far as run stopping, he is doing above average, but as a pass rusher? 2026 stats: Three starts, 4 total tackles, 0 sacks, 2 QB hits, 0 tackles for loss, 0 batted passes, 1 hurry, and 3 pressures. His PFF grade is just average at 52.4. His pass-rush grade of 63.1 is better than his run-stoppage rating, which ranks Nolen 52nd among 125 qualified interior defensive linemen. Wasn’t Nolen supposed to be this dominant pass-rushing defensive tackle? When does that begin? The other DT is Dante Stills . So far, minimal pass rush in his three starts. One sack, 9 total tackles, 1 QB hit, 1 batted pass, 1 tackle for loss, 3 hurries, and 5 pressures. Has played 58% of defensive snaps. PFF grade of 55.0. The backup to Stills is DE Darius Robinson . He has played on just 37% of defensive reps, so he is strictly a rotational guy. 8 total tackles, 1 tackle for loss, 0 sacks, 0 QB hits, 0 batted passes, 2 hurries, and 2 pressures. PFF grade of 60.7. DT L.J. Collier is the backup to Nolen and has played 39% of snaps. His issue is that he cannot disengage from offensive linemen, who then move him at will. His PFF grade of 49.5 is self-explanatory. Only three tackles in three games tell his story. 0 sacks, 0 tackles for loss, 0 batted passes, 0 QB hits, 2 hurries, and 2 pressures. Price fumbles, Zaven Collins recovers. Big turnover for #AZCardinals . — Darren Urban (@Cardschatter) September 20, 2026 LB Zaven Collins has not always been used to rush the passer. He drops back into coverage quite a bit and is utilized as a stand-up linebacker on most snaps, and his main job is run defense. And he is good at that. But he does take off into the backfield. 44% of snaps means he is playing less than half of each game, so there’s that. His stats: One start, 11 total tackles, 1 tackle for loss, 0 QB hits, 2 batted passes, 1 fumble recovery, 0 sacks, 1 hurry, and 1 pressure. PFF grade of 90.1. His run-defense grade of 90.5 is ranked 2 nd, while he grades out at 60.1 in pass rushing. LB Baron Browning will line up at times as an EDGE rusher and then attempt to get into the offensive backfield, but his main job is run defense at the second level. He has two starts, along with 4 total tackles, 1 tackle for loss, 0 sacks, 1 QB hit, 0 batted passes, 0 hurries, and 1 pressure. PFF grade of 66.3 with a pass-rush grade of 59.4, which is ranked 66th among 109 qualified edge defenders. As anyone can see, the Cardinals just aren’t getting any type of pass rush. In looking back at the first three games, the opposing quarterback was rarely flushed and had to escape the pocket. Versus the 49ers, QB Brock Purdy had plenty of time to survey the field on just about every passing down. What this does is vastly affect the defensive backfield, which now must shadow their man for much longer than the play was designed. The Cardinals’ defensive backs aren’t getting help by forcing the QB to throw early or go through just two progressions instead of four. This killed the defensive effort against San Francisco as Purdy picked and chose who to throw to all game without much hassle from the pass rush. What is wrong with Sweat? In looking at the game film, he rarely gets by his offensive tackle. Where is the pass rush from Nolen and Stills? In the offseason, positions such as offensive guard and tackle were addressed, as were running back and backup quarterback. But nothing changed with the defensive line other than the team lost its second-most productive sack master, DT Calais Campbell. Currently, Arizona is ranked 27 th in the league in sacks with four. One of those stud pass rushers with the third overall pick would have been nice, but that was then; this is now. Sign a good free agent? Gone are Za’Darius Smith, Jadeveon Clowney, A.J. Epenesa, and Von Miller. What can be done? The list of available free-agent EDGE rushers has been picked over pretty well. Haason Reddick (6’-1”, 240 pounds), age 32, previous salary: $14M Joey Bosa (6’-5”, 280 pounds), age 32, previous salary: $12.6M Leonard Floyd (6’-6”, 240 pounds), age 34, previous salary: $10M Denico Autry (6’-5”, 285 pounds), age 36, previous salary: $10M Yetur Gross-Matos (6’-5”, 265 pounds), age 28, previous salary: $9M Tyquan Lewis (6’-3”, 267 pounds), age 31, previous salary: $6M

title: Falcons sign Gervon Dexter to 4 year, $78 million deal
summary: The Atlanta Falcons traded for Gervon Dexter thinking he could be a force in their defensive front. Dexter was an on-again, off-again presence in the Chicago Bears defense, one who was intermittently useful against the run and more frequently a fearsome pass rusher. With Nate Ollie coaching him and in a scheme that would allow […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Gervon Dexter Sr. #95 of the Atlanta Falcons goes to the locker room at halftime of an NFL football game against the Carolina Panthers at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons traded for Gervon Dexter thinking he could be a force in their defensive front. Dexter was an on-again, off-again presence in the Chicago Bears defense, one who was intermittently useful against the run and more frequently a fearsome pass rusher. With Nate Ollie coaching him and in a scheme that would allow him to continuously and joyously pursue the quarterback, Atlanta’s trade suggested, Dexter could flirt with greatness. Through three weeks, that’s exactly what he’s done, as he’s piled up one of the highest pressure totals of any interior defensive lineman and has formed a devastating duo with Brandon Dorlus. The Falcons decided there was no point in waiting to lock him up in a contract year, signing him to a big money four year deal that continues a trend of Atlanta signing their stars to long-term deals under a new regime. #Falcons signing standout DT Gervon Dexter Sr. to a 4-year, $78M ($19.5M/yr) extension with $46.5M guaranteed. Dexter has been a force on a dominant Atlanta interior defensive line and is a leader in pressures among all IDL. Good on the team to do this now. — Kevin Knight (@FalcoholicKevin) September 30, 2026 Here’s what Ian Cunningham had to say about the deal, per the team’s website : “Gervon is a young, ascending talent whose power, disruption and impact along the defensive line are difficult to find,” Atlanta Falcons general manager Ian Cunningham said. “What’s been just as impressive is the growth he’s shown off the field as a man and a father. His passion for the game and commitment to his teammates are qualities we value highly, and we’re excited to keep him as an important part of our defense moving forward. I also want to thank Drew and Jason Rosenhaus for their communication and partnership throughout this process.” A fifth round pick and Clark Phillips are not prices you’d associate with a game-changing talent, but that’s what the Falcons paid to get Dexter back in August. Ian Cunningham played a role in drafting Dexter in Chicago as the team’s assistant general manager and clearly coveted him, but the Bears were also clearly wary of paying him big money given his inconsistency as a run defender and tackler in particular. The Falcons bought low on a player who they felt was an ideal fit for their attacking front alongside Dorlus, Maason Smith, and LaCale London, and thus far Dexter has been everything they hoped for. He’s been fine against the run, but the sheer havoc he’s wreaked as a pass rusher is what Atlanta’s paying for, and the early returns have been terrific. Dexter has 14 pressures already this year, per Pro Football Focus, which is about a third of a way to his 2025 total of 43 through just three games. Teams have struggled mightily to keep him and Dorlus from blasting past overmatched linemen, with the pair haunting Jordan Love’s dreams in particular for the foreseeable future. It’s a hefty price to pay for an interior defensive lineman, but if you believe this is Dexter’s new standard, it’s better to pay it now than at the end of the season when other teams would be clamoring for him and the price tag might go up substantially. This fits a larger trend, too. Ian Cunningham clearly wants to ensure the high-end core of this team—Bijan Robinson, Drake London, Kyle Pitts, Dexter, and (though he’s still proving it) Matthew Bergeron—stick around in 2027 and beyond when this team has substantial resources to improve the roster around them. Getting the defensive interior in particular squared away for at least this season and next with Dexter, Dorlus, and Smith gives Atlanta a formidable group that can provide the kind of interior pressure that wrecks games. They simply have to keep it up now. Congratulations to Dexter, and may this be just the beginning of his reign of terror in the NFC South.

It’s Robinson’s third time earning this honor since the 2025 season. Robinson was the NFC Offensive Player of the Week […]
full_text: by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images | Getty Images In news that should surprise absolutely no one, Bijan Robinson has earned NFC Offensive Player of the Week honors for absolutely going off against the Green Bay Packers on Thursday Night Football in Week 3. It’s Robinson’s third time earning this honor since the 2025 season. Robinson was the NFC Offensive Player of the Week in Week 6 vs. Buffalo (19 carries, 170 rushing yards, and a rushing touchdown, plus six catches for 68 yards) and Week 16 vs. the Rams last season (22 carries for 195 yards and a touchdown, plus five catches for 34 yards and a touchdown). Robinson had himself a day against the Packers, with 29 carries for 194 yards — 6.7 yards per carry — and two touchdowns. His 19 receiving yards put his total from scrimmage at 213 yards on the day. And he wasn’t the only player who went off. Drake London also put up 194 receiving yards on Thursday night in Lambeau. Bijan’s widely considered to be one of the best running backs in the league — and I don’t think it’s a stretch to think he’s THE best right now. GB Vs Atl rewatch: ATL 1. Bijan is leagues best back. Top 5 individual player. Don’t know if he has a historical comp. (LT, Arian Foster?) 2. Penix changed the math. Worked inside the numbers heavily, but outside the numbers & down the field was where he did big play damage.… — Ryan Clark (@Realrclark25) September 29, 2026 You might have noticed that Kirk Herbstreit had a lot to say about Bijan’s performance on Thursday night — but he also hyped up Robinson’s kindness, which is valid. I’ve covered a lot of players over the years, and Robinson isn’t just a god-tier athlete. He’s a good man with strong values and an incredible work ethic, and he leads by example. Bijan Robinson and the Atlanta Falcons have absolutely steamrolled the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. Al Michaels and Kirk Herbstreit have the TNF Prime Video call. 🏈💥🎙️ #NFL pic.twitter.com/pSMKDWhGmm — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) September 25, 2026 Congratulations to Bijan for the well deserved honor — and congratulations to Atlanta sports fans. Being a Falcons fan is generally not for the faint of heart, but we are so fortunate to have this generational talent in Atlanta.

summary: With Atlanta’s special teams off to a forgettable start to the 2026 season, they’ve added a veteran linebacker to hopefully help their coverage and return units. That would be former Viking and Bengal Brian Asamoah. Asamoah, 26, had a solid rookie season as a defender in limited opportunities but has been a complete non-factor on […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - DECEMBER 8: Linebacker Brian Asamoah II #6 of the Minnesota Vikings stands on the field prior to an NFL football game against the Atlanta Falcons, at U.S. Bank Stadium on December 8, 2024 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images With Atlanta’s special teams off to a forgettable start to the 2026 season, they’ve added a veteran linebacker to hopefully help their coverage and return units. That would be former Viking and Bengal Brian Asamoah. Sources: The #Falcons are signing former #Vikings LB Brian Asamoah II. A former 3rd-round pick out of Oklahoma, Asamoah recently worked out for Atlanta and will provide much-needed depth. pic.twitter.com/H3TydSgw9k — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) September 30, 2026 Asamoah, 26, had a solid rookie season as a defender in limited opportunities but has been a complete non-factor on that side of the ball in three seasons since, piling up just 70 total snaps on D from 2023 to 2025. Over that same span, he has nearly 600 special teams snaps and has been a solid tackler and useful blocker who was instrumental in paving the way for a 98 yard Charlie Jones kickoff return touchdown for the Bengals last year. He’ll likely be active on gameday for those attributes alone, as the Falcons are quite stacked at linebacker—Divine Deablo, Harold Perkins Jr., and Kendal Daniels are all off to strong starts, and Josh Woods is a capable reserve—and Asamoah has not played well there since 2022. It’s not difficult to figure out why the Falcons felt the need to make a move. While Brian Robinson is a capable kick returner and Zachariah Branch a potentially dynamic punt returner, both have had early miscues that overshadowed the inconsistent blocking they’ve gotten thus far. Things have been worrying in coverage, as well, as the Falcons have avoided any catastrophic mistakes but also have nine missed tackles through just three games, led by Mike Ford with three. While Asamoah never became the starting-caliber linebacker the Vikings were hoping to get when they drafted him in the third round, there’s little question he can be a sure tackler and blocker on teams. Give him a warm welcome, if you would, and we’ll see if he’s active for Monday Night Football.

summary: Welcome back to Loose Feathers, a regular round-up of the latest news and analysis about the Baltimore Ravens. Tyler Loop wins first award of […]
full_text: Sep 27, 2026; Rio De Janeiro, BRA; Baltimore Ravens kicker Tyler Loop (33) walks off the field after the game against the Dallas Cowboys at Maracana Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome back to Loose Feathers, a regular round-up of the latest news and analysis about the Baltimore Ravens. In today’s edition, we cover a career-first for Tyler Loop, a potential overreaction to his game-winning kick in Brazil, and Derrick Henry’s thoughts on playing his former team in Week 4. Tyler Loop wins first award of NFL career Long. Live. Loop. The Ravens’ second-year kicker was named the AFC Special Teams Player of the Week after his last-second game-winning field goal in Brazil to lift Baltimore over the Dallas Cowboys. Loop faced pressure this offseason after his season-ending miss against the Steelers in January, and his struggles in the preseason inspired the team to bring in some competition at the end of training camp. But the 2025 sixth-round pick hit all seven of his kicks in Week 1 including a career-long 57-yard field goal, quieting any talk of a benching. Sunday’s kick will likely lock Loop in for the foreseeable future. His fateful miss in Pittsburgh made it easy to overlook a solid rookie campaign that featured a 30-for-34 mark on field goals and 44 of 46 successful field goals. Despite talk of a big leg coming out of Arizona, he only went one-for-four from 50 yards or longer in 2025, but he has made both such attempts this year. Tyler Loop Named AFC Special Teams Player of the Week – Quentin Corpuel (BaltimoreRavens.com) Ravens kicker Tyler Loop became an international sensation on Sunday. Now, he has been named AFC Special Teams Player of the Week after a clutch performance against the Dallas Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro. After Lamar Jackson connected with Zay Flowers on a 27-yard gain that left one second on the clock in regulation, Loop drilled a game-winning 56-yard field goal to clinch a 34-31 win and celebrated with Christiano Ronaldo’s “SIUUU.” It was a career-long kick for Loop and his first game winner. It was also the Ravens’ first game-winning field goal in regulation since Justin Tucker made a 43-yarder at the buzzer against the Cincinnati Bengals in October 2022. Brock Bowers, Talanoa Hufanga & Tyler Loop Named Week 3 AFC Players of the Week – NFL Commmunications Loop converted both of his field goal attempts (27, 56) and all four of his point after attempts in the Ravens’ 34-31 win over Dallas. Loop’s 56-yard field goal came as time expired, giving Baltimore the win in the first-ever regular-season game in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. This is Loop’s first-career Player of the Week award. He becomes the third Ravens kicker to earn the honor, joining Justin Tucker (12-time winner) and Matt Stover (six), and the first since 2021. Loop becomes the second former Arizona kicker to win a Special Teams Player of the Week award, joining Nick Folk (10-time winner). Are the Ravens over their late-game woes? NFL Week 3 overreactions: Pats officially have a Drake Maye problem, Ravens can finally win big games again – Zachary Pereles (CBS Sports) Lamar Jackson, Tyler Loop delivered the Ravens their biggest regular-season win in recent memory Lamar Jackson, Tyler Loop delivered the Ravens their biggest regular-season win in recent memory Overreaction or reality: Reality Over the past five years, the Ravens have blown 10 double-digit, second-half leads. It’s the most in the NFL by far. And it sure looked like No. 11 was on the way… One week after melting down against the Saints , Jackson simply said: “Not again.” He threw for 186 yards (on just 20 attempts) and two scores. He ran for another 50 yards. When the Ravens needed it most, he delivered, again and again. The Ravens have had statement wins. They’ve had blowout wins. But this is more important than any of them: a demon-exorcising win. It won’t be soon forgotten. Derrick Henry prepares for first career game against former Team Ravens’ Henry: ‘Always love’ for Titans, but not much this Sunday – Jamison Hensley (ESPN) “It’s going to be a crazy moment to be playing against the team that I came in the league playing for,” Henry said. “But I ain’t trying to make too much of it, though. Henry joined the Ravens in March 2024, signing a two-year, $16 million contract. Before Henry reached an agreement with Baltimore, the Titans had signed running back Tony Pollard to a three-year, $21.75 million deal. On Wednesday, Henry said Tennessee made no attempt to keep him in free agency. “They shipped me out,” Henry initially said, before adding, “I don’t want to say it like that. It’s always love.” How did it make Henry feel to not receive an offer from the Titans? “It was bittersweet,” Henry said. “I think I knew the writing was on the wall throughout that season and they were ready to move on. Good things don’t last forever. So it was time for me to find a new home and I knew what that home I wanted it to be and it was here.”

title: Ravens center Jovaughn Gwyn could miss 2-3 months with fractured fibula
summary: Baltimore Ravens center Jovaughn Gwyn could miss two to three months with a fractured fibula suffered in Sunday’s win over the Dallas Cowboys in Brazil. The injury will “likely require surgery,” according to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler. Gwyn, 27, won the Ravens’ starting center job out of training camp after early favorite Danny Pinter went down […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Jovaughn Gwyn #54 of the Baltimore Ravens looks on against the New Orleans Saints during an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Baltimore Ravens center Jovaughn Gwyn could miss two to three months with a fractured fibula suffered in Sunday’s win over the Dallas Cowboys in Brazil. The injury will “likely require surgery,” according to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler . Gwyn, 27, won the Ravens’ starting center job out of training camp after early favorite Danny Pinter went down in August with a season-ending knee injury. He excelled as a run-blocker in his first three starts, but he has struggled in pass protection. Among starting centers, his 19.1 pass-blocking grade from Pro Football Focus ranks dead-last by a wide margin. His six pressures allowed, three penalties, and 96.2 pass-blocking efficiency are all bottom-four marks, too. This is a disappointing outcome for Gwyn, who got his first shot at a starting job after three years in a depth role in Atlanta. He came to Baltimore with former Falcons offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford this offseason and was seen as a dark horse in the competition for the center gig. He impressed in the preseason, creating some excitement that Ledford had developed him into a starting-caliber player, but the early results were disappointing, to say the least. The starting job may not be waiting for Gwyn if he returns later this season. Gwyn will likely be placed on injured reserve this week. Pocic is also out “long-term” with a knee injury, moving right guard Vega Ioane into the starting center job for the time being. Andrew Vorhees took his place on Sunday and will likely do so moving forward. The Ravens did sign veteran center Andre James to their practice squad on Wednesday. Once he gets integrated into Baltimore’s offense, he could be a potential starter who would move Ioane back to his natural position.
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: AFC North Week 3 recap: Back to an even playing field
summary: All four teams in the AFC North now sit at 2-1, making it the only division where all teams have a winning record through three weeks. Pittsburgh Steelers (2-1) The Steelers defeated the visiting Bengals on Sunday by a score of 30-27. Pittsburgh’s offense found life in Week 3 with 411 total yards after a […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Ben Skowronek #15 celebrates his touchdown with Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers during the first quarter against the Cincinnati Bengals at Acrisure Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images All four teams in the AFC North now sit at 2-1, making it the only division where all teams have a winning record through three weeks. Pittsburgh Steelers (2-1) The Steelers defeated the visiting Bengals on Sunday by a score of 30-27. Pittsburgh’s offense found life in Week 3 with 411 total yards after a slow start to the season. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers rebounded from his poor performance in Week 2, completing 19 of 34 passes for 292 yards, three touchdowns, and an interception. Rodgers’ leading receiver was tight end Darnell Washington, with three receptions for 67 yards, including a 47-yard reception that led to a Chris Boswell field goal to give the Steelers a three-point lead with just over two minutes remaining. Running back Jaylen Warren had a successful day on the ground, racking up 127 yards on 17 carries while adding another 49 yards through the air on three receptions. Wide receiver D.K. Metcalf found the end zone for the first time this season on a six-yard touchdown catch, while Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek caught Rodgers’ other two touchdowns. The Steelers’ defense found themselves against the wall with the game on the line as Cincinnati, down three, had the ball with a little over two minutes remaining in the game. As they have so many times before, Pittsburgh’s defense rose to the occasion as defensive tackle Derrick Harmon forced a fumble on a sack of Joe Burrow that was recovered by fellow DT Sebastian Joseph-Day to end the game. Harmon’s sack was the team’s only of the day, but it was all they needed in the end. Former Ravens linebacker Patrick Queen led the defense with 13 total tackles. Cincinnati Bengals (2-1) The Bengals dropped their first game of the season with a 30-27 loss on the road to the Steelers. QB Joe Burrow’s game-losing fumble at the end of the game put a damper on an otherwise strong day, as the star quarterback completed 28 of 37 pass attempts for 282 yards and three touchdowns. WR Ja’Marr Chase led the offense with 98 receiving yards and a touchdown, with his running mate Tee Higgins not far behind with six catches for 90 yards and a score as well. TE Mike Gesicki also caught a touchdown to go with 37 yards on three catches. RB Chase Brown was the leading rusher with 61 yards on 13 carries. Cincinnati’s defense came back down to Earth against Pittsburgh, allowing 411 total yards, after two strong games to start the season. LB Demetrius Knight was the leading tackler with 9, while DT Dexter Lawrence had the team’s two sacks against Rodgers to go with three tackles for loss. Jordan Battle came down with an interception on Rodgers while the team trailed 17-10, leading to a tied game near the end of the half as the offense scored on the ensuing possession. Mistakes on special teams proved costly as well, as Ke’Shawn Williams muffed a punt return that was recovered by the Steelers. The turnover came at a critical moment as the Bengals led 27-24 with a chance to extend their lead in the fourth quarter. Instead, Pittsburgh capitalized on the good field position with a 36-yard field goal to tie the game. Cleveland Browns (2-1) The Browns won their second straight game with a 21-18 home victory over the Carolina Panthers. QB Deshaun Watson carried the momentum from last week into another solid outing on Sunday, completing 16 of 30 pass attempts for 144 yards and two touchdowns while adding another 45 yards on 11 carries. Second-year TE Harold Fannin Jr. was the recipient of Watson’s two touchdowns while also leading the team with 51 receiving yards on seven catches. RB Quinshon Judkins led the ground attack with 70 yards on 18 carries. LB Quincy Williams led Cleveland’s defense with nine total tackles. The unit sacked Panthers QB Bryce Young three times on the day, with two sacks coming from DT Mason Graham and DE Isaiah McGuire, while safety Ronnie Hickman snagged an interception. Ex-Ravens WR Tylan Wallace exited the contest with a knee injury and is in danger of missing the team’s Thursday game against the Steelers. Baltimore Ravens (2-1) The Ravens rebounded from a disappointing Week 2 loss with a thrilling 34-31 win over the Dallas Cowboys in Brazil. QB Lamar Jackson’s strong start to the season continued against the Cowboys, completing 15 of 20 pass attempts for 186 yards and two touchdowns while rushing six times for 50 yards. The highlight of the game was Jackson’s 26-yard completion to WR Zay Flowers, who led the team with 84 receiving yards on five catches, with just seven seconds remaining in regulation. Jackson quickly called a timeout with one second remaining on the clock, leading to some long-awaited redemption for K Tyler Loop in the form of a walk-off 56-yard field goal. Derrick Henry was his usual self with 89 yards and two touchdowns on 26 carries. Baltimore’s offense now finds itself in a predicament, though, after losing both of their centers, Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic to long-term injuries during the game. Rookie first-round guard Vega Ioane took over center duties after Pocic left the game and is expected to remain there in Week 5. The Ravens’ late-game defensive struggles remained against Dallas as they allowed 18 points in the second half. The unit made the stop in the most critical moment of the game, however, holding the Cowboys to a field goal when a touchdown would’ve won the game. LB Roquan Smith led the way with nine total tackles while notching the team’s only sack on QB Dak Prescott. The biggest story entering the game for Baltimore’s defense was the return of DT Nnamdi Madubuike from a neck injury that ended his 2025 season after just two games.
author: Dustin Cox

title: Ravens Week 4 injury report: LT Ronnie Stanley returns to practice
summary: Baltimore Ravens left tackle Ronnie Stanley returned to practice on Wednesday after missing Sunday’s win over the Dallas Cowboys with a toe injury. He was listed as limited on the team’s first injury report of Week 4, along with seven other players, including star quarterback Lamar Jackson. Minter opened his press conference by announcing that […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Ronnie Stanley #79 of the Baltimore Ravens looks on against the New Orleans Saints during an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Baltimore Ravens left tackle Ronnie Stanley returned to practice on Wednesday after missing Sunday’s win over the Dallas Cowboys with a toe injury. He was listed as limited on the team’s first injury report of Week 4, along with seven other players, including star quarterback Lamar Jackson . Minter opened his press conference by announcing that Jackson was limited after previous reports that he was not on the field at the start of practice. “Hopefully, I can calm down the whole city of Baltimore and let you know that Lamar was at practice,” Minter said. “Limited role, just dealing with something small, so that was good. I had heard that maybe that was sheer pandemonium that he was not out there earlier, but he ended up being able to get some stuff done.” Stanley did not participate in practice at all last week, bringing second-year tackle Carson Vinson into the starting lineup for the first time in his career. Vinson played well, but with the Ravens re-shuffling their offensive line due to multiple center injuries , Stanley’s leadership and football I.Q. could be crucial to the offensive line’s success in the coming weeks. In addition to Jackson and Stanley, Baltimore reported nine other players with injuries on Wednesday. Here is the full report: Full participation TE Mark Andrews (hand) Limited participation WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) CB Marlon Humphrey (hamstring) QB Lamar Jackson (back) WR Chris Moore (ankle) LG John Simpson (groin) TE Durham Smythe (heel) LT Ronnie Stanley (toe) Did not participate DL Calais Campbell (non-injury related/rest) C Jovaughn Gwyn (ankle) OLB Trey Hendrickson (finger) C Ethan Pocic (knee) Flowers, Simpson, and Hendrickson have been dealing with their injuries for a few weeks. The rest are new, but none are particularly worrisome. Hendrickson missed the first practice of Weeks 2 and 3 but still played a full complement of snaps in both games without any drop in his production. Baltimore’s upcoming opponent, the Tennessee Titans, only listed three players on their first Week 4 injury report: Did not participate DL John Franklin-Myers (back) RB Tony Pollard (foot) RB Tyjae spears (ankle) Franklin-Myers is one-half of Tennessee’s fearsome defensive line duo along with All-Pro Jeffery Simmons. His potential absence would give the Ravens’ shuffled interior O-line an easier overall matchup and allow them to consistently double-team Simmons. The Titans’ running back injuries could be a major concern for their offense. Quarterback Cam Ward has averaged just 5.1 yards per passing attempt through three games, while Pollard and Spears have recorded 4.5 yards per carry. An absence from either will elevate Julius Chestnut and Michael Carter into game day roles. If both were to miss Sunday’s game, Tennessee would likely bring Kalel Mullings up from the practice squad.
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Ravens Week 3 film study: LT Carson Vinson makes encouraging first start
summary: The Baltimore Ravens’ thrilling win over the Dallas Cowboys in Brazil gave us an opportunity to take a closer look at a few different players this week. Carson Vinson made his first NFL start at left tackle, Zion Young became more involved against the run, and Calais Campbell reminded everyone that even in Year 19, […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Carson Vinson #76 of the Baltimore Ravens lines up against the New Orleans Saints during an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens’ thrilling win over the Dallas Cowboys in Brazil gave us an opportunity to take a closer look at a few different players this week. Carson Vinson made his first NFL start at left tackle, Zion Young became more involved against the run, and Calais Campbell reminded everyone that even in Year 19, ability doesn’t simply disappear. LT Carson Vinson 64 snaps | 28 pass blocking | 36 run blocking | 0 pressures allowed Vinson made his first NFL start at left tackle for the Ravens on Sunday, and while there was plenty to like, there were also some areas that showed where his development still needs to continue. As a run blocker, Vinson flashed his movement skills and ability to work through combination blocks. On one rep, he did a nice job bouncing off a defensive tackle, climbing to the linebacker and sealing the second-level defender to create a lane for the running back. On another, however, Cowboys DT Quinnen Williams was able to overpower Vinson at the point of attack, work into the backfield and record a tackle for loss. Carson Vinson vs the Cowboys Some good. Some not so good. Did a nice job climbing to level 2, good hand placement. Still need better grip strength and functional strength. Was able to redirect guys inside on a few reps, but also got beat inside on others. pic.twitter.com/MiyKzAMt7y — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) September 29, 2026 That sequence highlighted one of the biggest areas of improvement remaining in Vinson’s game: functional strength and consistently playing behind his pads. If he is eventually going to take the mantle from Ronnie Stanley at left tackle, that part of his game will have to continue developing. In pass protection, there were some encouraging signs. Vinson showed good range when handling stunts and twists and displayed sound kick-step technique with solid punch timing. His ability to keep a clean sheet and finish the game without allowing a pressure was certainly encouraging. There were still reps where the process wasn’t quite as clean as the result. On multiple snaps, Vinson was walked backward by edge rushers converting speed to power. On another, he landed a solid initial strike but lost his grip, allowing the defender to work back inside. Once again, those reps pointed toward grip strength and functional power as two important areas of development. Overall, it was not a bad first NFL start for the 2025 fifth-round pick. Vinson showed that he can provide capable tackle play when called upon. The bigger question is whether he showed enough to suggest he can eventually become the Ravens’ long-term answer at left tackle, and that remains to be seen. OLB Zion Young 26 snaps | 14 run defense | 12 pass rush | 1 pressure | 1 TFL Young’s statistics may not jump off the page, but he did a lot of impressive dirty work for the Ravens on Sunday while also showing development in some of the areas we questioned in his original scouting report . One of the biggest questions surrounding Young was his get-off and overall quick-twitch ability. Against Dallas we got a glimpse of improvement in that area. On one rep, the Cowboys tackle beat Young off the snap, but the rookie recovered quickly, reduced his surface area and slipped past the block to bring down the running back for a short gain. It was an encouraging example of improved reaction time and recovery speed. Zion Young had a great game vs the cowboys Stats may not reflect (1 pressure, 2 tackles, 1 tfl) but charged up hand usage and leveraging length at the POA. SOB vs the run Finally starting to show improved reaction time/ get off (watch rep 2). 50% win rate on true pass sets pic.twitter.com/Teqkmkfpw6 — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) September 28, 2026 Young’s physicality at the point of attack also continued to show up. On one snap, he engaged the tackle and rode him laterally down the line of scrimmage before working off the block to make the tackle. On another, he met a tight end sliding across the formation head-on, maintained his position and wrapped up the ball carrier. He also showed his ability to set a hard edge, creating another tackle for loss in the run game. While the second-round pick only recorded one pressure, he finished with a 50% win rate on true pass sets, an encouraging sign for a player whose early role has required him to do plenty of work that won’t necessarily appear on the stat sheet. Young’s power and physicality were not questions coming out of college. The important development will be whether he can continue adding quickness, reaction speed and counters to that foundation. Sunday provided some encouraging signs that those parts of his game are beginning to develop. DT Calais Campbell 32 snaps | 7 run defense | 24 pass rush | 1 coverage | 6 pressures In the first two games of the season, Calais Campbell made a solid impact on the field, but his play didn’t pop on tape. One of the things I appreciate most when evaluating defensive linemen is simply whether they are consistently hitting the quarterback. Sacks can fluctuate from week to week, but consistently getting the quarterback on the ground or forcing him to absorb contact is usually a good indication that a pass rusher is getting extremely close to finishing those opportunities. Campbell did exactly that against Dak Prescott, delivering two significant hits on the Cowboys quarterback. Calais Campbell lead the Ravens with 6 QB pressures Sunday Hands like a heavyweight boxer. Violent club and rip. Turns out he just needed a few preseason games to warm up! pic.twitter.com/58lAtZwZiq — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) September 28, 2026 Campbell’s club move still hits like a heavy-handed boxer. His combination of length, mass and upper-body strength gives him a natural advantage against offensive linemen, and we saw that translate into disruption throughout the game. On one rep, Campbell crashed into the center, created immediate displacement and then ripped through the block to penetrate the pocket. That combination of power and length has been the foundation of Campbell’s game for nearly two decades, and even in Year 19, it remains extremely difficult for offensive linemen to deal with when he is playing with proper leverage and timing. Given the uniqueness of Campbell’s offseason situation, it was always reasonable to expect that he might need a few weeks to ramp himself back up to the level of play we have become accustomed to seeing. His performance against Dallas looked much closer to that version of the six-time Pro Bowler. The Ravens are going to need that version of him later in the season. When the weather gets colder, games become more physical and Baltimore needs someone capable of creating disruption from the interior, Campbell’s combination of size, length and power can still be an important piece of this defensive front. Snap counts and advanced metrics via Pro Football Focus .

title: Ravens sign center Andre James, guard Kyle Hergel to practice squad
summary: The Baltimore Ravens signed center Andrew James and guard Kyle Hergel to their practice squad on Wednesday, per a team announcement, adding much-needed interior offensive line depth after injuries to centers Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic. In a corresponding move, the team promoted safety K’Von Wallace from the practice squad to the 53-man roster to […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - JANUARY 05: Andre James #68 of the Las Vegas Raiders high-fives fans as he takes the field during player introductions before a game against the Los Angeles Chargers at Allegiant Stadium on January 05, 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Chargers defeated the Raiders 34-20. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens signed center Andrew James and guard Kyle Hergel to their practice squad on Wednesday, per a team announcement , adding much-needed interior offensive line depth after injuries to centers Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic. In a corresponding move, the team promoted safety K’Von Wallace from the practice squad to the 53-man roster to create space for both signings. As a vested veteran, Wallace can be released and re-signed to the practice squad at any time. He was elevated for the Ravens’ Week 3 matchup in Brazil but did not play in the game. James, 29, is one of the most experienced centers available. He signed with the Raiders as an undrafted free agent in 2019 after four years at UCLA and appeared in 12 games as a rookie with one start at center. He remained in the backup job in 2020 before taking over as the full-time starter in 2021. Over the next four years, he started 59 games in Las Vegas, including a career-best 2023 with a 74.6 overall grade from Pro Football Focus (75.0 run-blocking, 71.2 pass blocking). The Raiders moved on from James in March 2025 despite signing him to a three-year, $24 million extension almost exactly one year prior. He signed with the Chargers and appeared in all 17 games, but made just one start despite the team’s offensive line woes. The seven-year veteran then joined the Titans this year, but was released during final roster cuts. His experience in Tennessee may give the Ravens some information about their upcoming matchup against the Titans. James certainly has the experience to step in as the Ravens’ starting center once he is up to speed in Declan Doyle’s offense. The team will evaluate him in practice, as well as rookie guard Vega Ioane, who is poised to start at center in Week 4. Doyle and offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford will have to determine their best center/right guard duo among their options. Hergel, 26, could factor into the picture, but he is more likely a depth addition for the time being. Like James, he entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent, signing with the Saints in 2024. He appeared in eight games as a rookie, but he only played 45 snaps on offense (all at left guard) as an injury replacement. The Saints waived Hergel during final roster cuts in 2025. He signed with the Bears’ practice squad a few months later and played under Doyle for a few months, giving him some knowledge of the Ravens’ new offense. That could help him get integrated into the unit quickly, but his lack of experience suggests he is a long-shot to contribute on game days in the immediate future. Hergel worked out in Baltimore on Tuesday along with Graham Glasgow and Kingsley Eguakun. The team will likely continue to keep tabs on available offensive linemen, though those ranks will continue to dwindle as the season drags on. Former Ravens guard Kevin Zeitler signed with the Packers on Tuesday – much to the dismay of fans in Baltimore – but a reunion was never in the cards. Zeitler was interested, according to Cole Jackson of Baltimore Film Breakdown , but the Ravens were not. The team originally let him leave in 2024 due to concerns about his knee; additionally, Baltimore would not have given Zeitler the $5 million contract he received from Green Bay.

title: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson limited in 1st practice of Week 4
summary: Update: Jackson was seen leaving the practice field in full uniform by ESPN’s Jamison Hensley, and head coach Jesse Minter confirmed that his star quarterback was a limited participant due to “something small.” Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson was absent for the media viewing portion of the team’s first practice of Week 4, according to […]
full_text: Sep 27, 2026; Rio De Janeiro, BRA; Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson (8) speaks to the media after the game at Maracana Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Update: Jackson was seen leaving the practice field in full uniform by ESPN’s Jamison Hensley , and head coach Jesse Minter confirmed that his star quarterback was a limited participant due to “something small.” Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson was absent for the media viewing portion of the team’s first practice of Week 4, according to multiple reports. The two-time MVP’s absence does not seem to be caused by injury. He spoke to reporters prior to practice and gave no indication he was dealing with any physical issue or that he was at risk of missing Sunday’s game against the Tennessee Titans. More likely, this is a result of of traveling to Brazil and back in the last week, a trip that including a tight, taxing, and thrilling win over the Dallas Cowboys. Jackson “looked and sounded either really tired or sick” in the locker room after the game, per Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic. Ravens left tackle Ronnie Stanley did return to practice after missing all of Week 3 due to a toe injury. His backup, 2025 fifth-round pick Carson Vinson, held up in his first career regular-season start, but with the team’s other issues along the offensive line, Stanley’s potential return in Week 4 should boost the entire unit. The Ravens will release the first full practice report of Week 4 later this afternoon, which will provide some clarity of Jackson’s status, Stanley’s likelihood of playing on Sunday, and any other injuries the team picked up in Brazil.
