title: Joe Burrow has 1 career comeback win when trailing with 8 minutes left, but that doesn’t tell the whole story
summary: There’s no question that Joe Burrow is among the top-ranked quarterbacks in the league. He’s totally transformed the entire Cincinnati Bengals franchise, brought them back to a Super Bowl, and will hopefully lead them back to the postseason in 2026. If he were going to have a major flaw, it’s likely his durability, as he’s […]
full_text: There’s no question that Joe Burrow is among the top-ranked quarterbacks in the league. He’s totally transformed the entire Cincinnati Bengals franchise, brought them back to a Super Bowl, and will hopefully lead them back to the postseason in 2026. If he were going to have a major flaw, it’s likely his durability, as he’s struggled to stay healthy throughout his career so far. Still, it’s surprising to learn that Burrow has come back to win a game just one time (out of 35 attempts) when the Bengals were trailing their opponent with eight minutes left in the fourth quarter. This isn’t exactly his fault, of course. Think how many times over the past few years Burrow, along with Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, and others, put on an offensive clinic, scoring 30 or more points, just to watch the opposing offense score even more. How many times has he been sacked or pressured during a key moment? Throughout his career, when the Bengals are trailing in the final five minutes of a game, Burrow has thrown a touchdown on 10.3% of his pass attempts. That’s roughly one touchdown every 10 passes, and it’s the highest touchdown rate for any NFL quarterback in that situation since at least 2000, among quarterbacks with a minimum of 30 attempts, according to Warren Sharp . So, while the Bengals may not have won many games when trailing late in the fourth quarter, it’s pretty difficult to pin that on Burrow. When he’s been given the opportunity to make something happen late, he’s been remarkably good at doing exactly that. Sunday’s game against the Steelers was another example. Burrow completed 28/37 passes for 282 yards and three touchdowns. He didn’t turn the ball over until the final drive and did everything he could to make sure the Bengals would go 3-0. Special teams had different ideas, though. The punt return team gave Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers a fresh set of downs after Cedric Johnson was called for a very obvious roughing-the-kicker penalty. That turned into seven points. Then, in the fourth quarter, Ke’Shawn Williams muffed a punt, which was recovered by the Steelers in the red zone. That fumble turned into three points. Could Burrow have played better? Sure—he wasn’t perfect—but it’s hard to win when special teams’ mistakes turn into 10 points. Winning on the road, especially in a division game, is hard. Spotting a team 10 points isn’t how you get it done. Since 2021 Joe Burrow's dropback EPA/play when trailing with less than 8 minutes in regulation is +0.33 That's T-4th in the NFL in that time, behind Josh Allen (+0.44, 9-24), Dak Prescott (+0.36, 7-28-1) and Lamar Jackson (+0.34, 10-21) His 107.7 passer rating ranks 1st My… https://t.co/wAR1flknET — Jake Liscow (@JakeLiscow) September 27, 2026 Joe Burrow had a 94th percentile Total EPA in a loss to the Steelers in Week 3 Burrow leads all quarterbacks with 5 losses in games where the QB produced a 90th+ percentile Total EPA since 2020, per @SumerSports . No other QB has more than 2 such losses — Shawn Syed (@SyedSchemes) September 27, 2026

title: Losing at Pittsburgh will not define the 2026 Cincinnati Bengals
summary: The goal for the 2026 Bengals was never to go undefeated. It was also not just to beat the Pittsburgh Steelers on the road. For the 2026 Bengals, there are bigger goals that are still very much in play even with the 30-27 loss to the Steelers on Sunday. First off, it is still disappointing […]
full_text: The goal for the 2026 Bengals was never to go undefeated. It was also not just to beat the Pittsburgh Steelers on the road. For the 2026 Bengals, there are bigger goals that are still very much in play even with the 30-27 loss to the Steelers on Sunday. First off, it is still disappointing that the Bengals couldn’t find a way to win at Pittsburgh on Sunday. They had two chances in the second half to break the game open, but they gave the ball right back to the Steelers both times. Joe Burrow and the Bengals’ offense went three-and-out and fumbled on their final drive, and the defense couldn’t get a stop on the Steelers’ game-winning drive, despite it starting inside their own 10-yard line. It was a step back for the Bengals’ defense and a terrible day for the Bengals’ special teams on Sunday. Pittsburgh running back Jaylen Warren and tight end Darnell Washington gashed and steamrolled the Bengals’ defense all afternoon, pushing them around and attacking their weak spots. Despite all that, my outlook for the 2026 Bengals hasn’t changed. We knew there would be a game where the defense couldn’t get pressure on the opposing quarterback and would give up a lot of yards and points. It’s unfortunate that it came in an AFC North game that felt very winnable, but this Bengals defense was never going to be the 2000 Ravens or the ‘85 Bears. Even without getting much pressure on Aaron Rodgers and getting gashed and steamrolled by Warren and Washington, the Bengals still had multiple chances to win the game or break it open. It’s a testament to the fact that the Bengals lost this game because of self-induced mistakes. They didn’t lose this game because of a lack of talent. Last year, when they were blown out by the Minnesota Vikings in Week 3 and the Denver Broncos in Week 4, there was a sense of hopelessness because the talent disparity between the Bengals and most other teams in the NFL was glaring. This year, it’s different. The Bengals have talent, and that’s been very evident through three weeks. Ja’Marr Chase and Dexter Lawrence, among others, were very adamant in the locker room Sunday that this is still a team that can be very good. Joe Burrow concurred at his postgame press conference, but he also said they can’t make the mistakes they made on Sunday. Last year, the Seattle Seahawks lost at home in Week 1 to the San Francisco 49ers and at the Los Angeles Rams in Week 11. In 2024, the Philadelphia Eagles lost in the last 10 seconds at the Washington Commanders in Week 16. In 2023, the Kansas City Chiefs lost at home to the Las Vegas Raiders on Christmas. Tom Brady and the 2020 Tampa Bay Buccaneers lost to the New Orleans Saints… twice… in the regular season. Brady and the New England Patriots lost to the Miami Dolphins on the Miami Miracle in Week 14 of the 2018 season. All of these teams went on to win the Super Bowl. Losing at Pittsburgh by three points in Week 3 of the regular season is not going to define this Bengals team. The goal wasn’t just to beat Pittsburgh on the road. The Bengals have bigger goals this season, and one of them is still beating Pittsburgh. The Bengals can do that in Week 10 when they host the Steelers on Sunday Night Football. As Joe Burrow famously said in 2021, “We have bigger aspirations than beating the Steelers.”

title: Bengals News: Joe Burrow happy for Mitchell Tinsley return
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals had a problem pop up the last two weeks at what is usually one of their deeper positions. Wide receiver became a little to thin with injuries to Andrei Iosivas and the rookie Colbie Young. Iosivas is on injured reserve, and Young has already been ruled out this week against the Jacksonville […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 29: Mitch Tinsley #82 of the Cincinnati Bengals warms up prior to the game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on September 29, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals had a problem pop up the last two weeks at what is usually one of their deeper positions. Wide receiver became a little to thin with injuries to Andrei Iosivas and the rookie Colbie Young. Iosivas is on injured reserve, and Young has already been ruled out this week against the Jacksonville Jaguars. This led Cincinnati to bring back a familiar face in Mitchell Tinsley. He had been cut after the preseason, but he opted to go to the Houston Texans practice squad, which is where he has been until the Bengals signed him to the active roster. It was a decision that got Joe Burrow excited. “I thought it was pretty much a no-brainer,” Burrow told reporters following Wednesday’s practice. “He played well for us last year and gave us some good reps. He made a lot of plays for us in his limited opportunities, so to take a guy like that back that we weren’t sure we were going to is good for the Bengals.” Tinsley is unique in a way that he is able to make those high point catches on the boundary, which allows the team to comfortably move Ja’Marr Chase into the slot, where he can be an absolute nightmare for defenses. Bengals News Quick Hits | Do-It-All Dax Hill Gets Another Call; Erick All Jr. Wants Ball/Win, Not Praise; Injury Update It looks like Dax Hill will be lining up as the slot corner, which is what he played most of Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Jalen Davis is out, which leaves no one else since Ja’Sir Taylor is also out. Hill has shown he can do this, but it does mean rookie Tacario Davis has to grow up a bit quicker than expected as he will probably be slotted into the boundary corner position. Bengals sign wideout, returner Ke’Shawn Williams back to practice squad It wasn’t surprising to see the team move him around playing the 53-man roster game. He could be elevated when Sunday rolls around, but he certainly hurt his chances by having a very poor kick return — where he inexplicably tried to reverse field — as well as the even worse muffed punt late in the game. Those are two big no no’s as a returner. Bengals’ injury report for Week 4 seems concerning The safety position could be an issue come Sunday. Kyle Dugger is already out and Bryan Cook and Jordan Battle were both limited on Wednesday. Cook left Sunday’s game a few times, clearly trying to give it a go after dealing with injury. A close eye will have to be kept on their progress. NFL News Steelers trading CB Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys in exchange for second-, sixth-round picks Talk about a poverty franchise. Another player the team couldn’t afford to pay getting offloaded to the Dallas Cowboys after they did the same with George Pickens last season. You have to wonder how this will impact morale seeing this front office refusing to budge on guaranteed money. NFL QB rankings, Week 4: Brock Purdy climbs to No. 1; Kirk Cousins enters top 10 The strip sack was an unfortunate mistake, but you have to see how badly Burrow has to play absolutely perfect or otherwise he is punished. He was lights out against that defense even when you could argue they were letting defensive backs get away with way too much contact. NFL Power Rankings, Week 4: 49ers claim No. 1 spot! Raiders, Vikings enter top 10; Patriots drop to 31 The Bengals remain in the Top 10. It was a rough loss for the defense, but it is even more unfortunate they are getting blamed for 10 points being created of easily avoided special teams’ miscues. It is a game Cincinnati was talented enough to win, but letting that Steelers offense go off sure hurt the perception of this team.

title: Bengals Film Room: Is it time for Cincinnati to bench Jordan Battle for Kyle Dugger?
summary: The Bengals were expecting Jordan Battle to take a major step forward this season with the addition of veteran Bryan Cook alongside him at safety. Instead, it looks like the same inconsistent player the Bengals have seen the last several years. Jordan Battle currently has a 38.1 coverage grade on the season. He also has […]
full_text: The Bengals were expecting Jordan Battle to take a major step forward this season with the addition of veteran Bryan Cook alongside him at safety. Instead, it looks like the same inconsistent player the Bengals have seen the last several years. Jordan Battle currently has a 38.1 coverage grade on the season. He also has a 15.0% missed tackle rate. That mark is 10th worst among 46 qualified safeties that have played 80% of their team’s snaps so far this season. More concerning than the missed tackles for me is just how often he takes poor angles and doesn’t even get there to officially get credited with a missed tackle. During the first week of the season against Tampa Bay, it felt like Battle was very inconsistent, at best. He made some plays, but he was also arguably the poorest-performing player of the starters on the defense that day. He missed tackles, he took poor angles to the football, and didn’t look like a player you could count on if you wanted to see a vastly improved defense for the entire season. Jordan Battle vs. Tampa Bay The Bengals will need a more consistent performance from Battle on Sunday, and I think we will see that. pic.twitter.com/XqTjVXtJnH — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 18, 2026 Battle was able to bounce back with a better performance in Houston. However, that was a game where the Bengals generated 41 pressures, mostly by the guys up front. A dominant performance like that can typically help to mask the deficiencies of someone in the secondary. Regardless, we will say that was a solid performance from Jordan Battle in Houston. Jordan Battle stepped up his game vs. Houston on Sunday. pic.twitter.com/1CL1WiPFee — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 23, 2026 On Sunday, I thought Battle was awful. The poor angles, the missed tackles, and just a general lack of effort at times to go and make a play all reared their ugly heads during this one. Meanwhile, Bryan Cook was battling injuries throughout the game. While I am sure that might not have helped Battle on the day, it is still his job to go out there and make plays. At minimum, you cannot have a lack of effort as we saw at times against the Steelers. This wasn’t even the worst effort in tackling Darnell Washington of the day pic.twitter.com/HCvvaFgwlw — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 This Bengals defense gave up way too many explosives. The usual suspects played a big part in that too. What are these angles and effort? pic.twitter.com/Pr84HmZCA6 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 Regardless of the angle you see it from, a lot of pathetic effort out there to go and make this play after the Darnell Washington catch. pic.twitter.com/9HKBpp1YMo — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 His day in coverage wasn’t any better on Sunday. Battle finished with a 40.3 coverage grade on Sunday. One play in particular was directly responsible for the Steelers’ second touchdown of the game. Battle came up and was beat by Ben Skowronek for a 23-yard touchdown pass. Cooked pic.twitter.com/mvy4XbHA4r — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 The player that I would like to see get a shot next to a healthy Bryan Cook would be Kyle Dugger. Dugger had to play quite a few snaps in place of the injured Cook for much of the game on Sunday, and I thought he looked pretty good out there. He also came out of the game dinged up, so the health of him and Cook will be something to watch this week. However, if both can play, I would have them as my two starters this week. Dugger finished the game with 8 tackles and a pass defense during the game. His physicality, effort, and ability to finish tackles in the open field were all a cut above what we are seeing from Jordan Battle this year. An open field tackle on a tight end before they get the first down. Refreshing to see. I thought Kyle Dugger played like a guy that needs to be on the field more often. Preferably alongside a healthy Bryan Cook. pic.twitter.com/TgWVjHJ0ol — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 Kyle Dugger just gets enough of Jaylen Warren to keep him out of the end zone pic.twitter.com/Apt7uIGM4W — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 Dugger unblocked off the edge, and Dexter Lawrence there to finish it off. Bengals hold the Steelers to a field goal after the Ke’Shawn Williams muffed punt. pic.twitter.com/VkgWco8XTl — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 28, 2026 I didn’t even realize this until just now while clipping up Kyle Dugger, but he could barely move out there, and still went and made the tackle on Darnell Washington. Meanwhile, a bunch of other guys weren’t even trying to get him down. pic.twitter.com/XNJZTsgdjI — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 29, 2026 When everyone is healthy, do you think Kyle Dugger should replace Jordan Battle in the starting lineup at safety? Sound off in the comments.

title: 3 bold reasons the Bengals will bounce back and beat the Jaguars
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals didn’t exactly get the result they wanted in Pittsburgh. After opening the season 2-0, Cincinnati let a winnable game slip away from them in Week 3, falling 30-27 to the Steelers. Now, they get a chance to put that one behind them with the Jacksonville Jaguars coming to Paycor Stadium on Sunday. […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals didn’t exactly get the result they wanted in Pittsburgh . After opening the season 2-0, Cincinnati let a winnable game slip away from them in Week 3, falling 30-27 to the Steelers. Now, they get a chance to put that one behind them with the Jacksonville Jaguars coming to Paycor Stadium on Sunday. And while Jacksonville is coming off a convincing 35-6 win over New England, there are plenty of reasons to believe the Bengals can get back in the win column. Here are three bold reasons why. 1. Bengals’ response will be very different from performance in Pittsburgh Let’s start with the obvious one: this team should be angry. Cincinnati had a chance to walk out of Pittsburgh at 3-0 and instead came away with a divisional loss in which the Bengals made enough self-inflicted mistakes to cost themselves the game. That’s the kind of loss that can either linger or serve as a wake-up call. I’m betting on the latter. The Bengals return home, where they’ll have a chance to correct those mistakes in front of their own fans. Zac Taylor and Joe Burrow have been around long enough to understand that one loss doesn’t define a season, but allowing the same mistakes to snowball would be a different story. The Jaguars aren’t the Steelers. And Cincinnati should come out playing with the urgency of a team that doesn’t want to start a losing streak. Bold prediction: Cincinnati scores first and never trails. 2. Jacksonville will struggle with Cincinnati’s passing game The Jaguars’ defense has been opportunistic early this season, but this is where having Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins becomes a pretty significant advantage. Through the first three games, Burrow has thrown for 743 yards and six touchdowns, while Higgins has 244 receiving yards and Chase has already established himself as the centerpiece of the offense. And don’t forget what happened the last time these teams played in Cincinnati. The Bengals beat Jacksonville 31-27 in 2025, with Cincinnati’s passing game making several big plays late. And that was with Jake Browning playing half of the game. This matchup has the potential to become another one of those games where Jacksonville simply has too many weapons to account for. The Jaguars can’t sell out to stop Chase because Higgins can hurt them. They can’t devote all of their attention to the receivers because Burrow is perfectly capable of picking apart favorable looks underneath. And if the Bengals’ offensive line can give Burrow time? That’s where things could get really interesting. Bold prediction: Chase goes over 100 receiving yards and finds the end zone. 3. Dexter Lawrence and defensive front will take over Here’s the one I’m most interested in. Cincinnati’s biggest offseason overhaul came up front, and the early returns have been encouraging. The Bengals enter Week 4 leading the NFL with ten sacks, according to the NFL’s game-center statistics. Now they get to face a Jacksonville offense that has been productive but hasn’t exactly been unstoppable through the air. The Jaguars are averaging 314 yards per game, while Cincinnati’s defense has already generated ten sacks and five takeaways through three games. And this is where Dexter Lawrence can make his presence felt. The Bengals brought Lawrence in to change the complexion of their defensive front. After recording two sacks against Aaron Rodgers in Pittsburgh, he now gets another opportunity to wreck an opposing quarterback’s afternoon. If Cincinnati can generate pressure without constantly blitzing, it allows the secondary to play more aggressively and puts Jacksonville in some uncomfortable down-and-distance situations. Bold prediction: Lawrence records another sack, while the Bengals finish with at least four as a team. The Prediction Look, this isn’t going to be a walk in the park. Jacksonville is coming off a 35-6 demolition of New England, and the Jaguars are 2-1 heading into Cincinnati. But this feels like a classic “prove it” game for the Bengals. And there is something about history. It tends to repeat itself. If the Steelers win games against Cincinnati in the ways/scenarios we saw on Sunday, Lawrence and the Jags have an uphill battle. Since being drafted No. 1 overall by Jacksonville in 2021, Lawrence has not beaten the Bengals. This includes a crazy Thursday Night affair in his rookie year, as well as a couple of other crazy Jake Browning games. On Monday Night Football in 2023, as well as in relief last year in Week 2, Browning led the Bengals to improbable wins in Burrow’s absence. The Bengals have already shown they can win a close one. They showed they can dominate on the road against Houston. Now they need to show they can take a tough loss and respond. The Bengals are back at Paycor Stadium. Burrow is healthy. Chase and Higgins give them matchup problems all over the field. And the revamped defensive front has already demonstrated that it can make life miserable for opposing quarterbacks. So, let’s go bold: Bengals 31, Jaguars 23. A bounce-back win, a 3-1 record, and a much better feeling heading into the next stretch of the schedule.
author: Anthony Cosenza

title: Tee Higgins has been elite at catching passes and blocking
summary: It feels like Tee Higgins has been a little overshadowed by everything else going on around the Bengals’ offense. That probably won’t last. Higgins has come out of the gate absolutely cooking in 2026, and the numbers through three games are a pretty good reminder of just how valuable the Bengals’ WR2 really is. Through […]
full_text: It feels like Tee Higgins has been a little overshadowed by everything else going on around the Bengals’ offense. That probably won’t last. Higgins has come out of the gate absolutely cooking in 2026, and the numbers through three games are a pretty good reminder of just how valuable the Bengals’ WR2 really is. Through three games, Higgins has 14 catches for 244 yards, averaging an eye-popping 17.4 yards per reception, with a touchdown. He’s also coming off back-to-back 90-plus-yard performances after posting 95 yards against Houston and 90 against Pittsburgh. And there’s another number from Bradley Locker’s post that really puts his start into perspective: Higgins is averaging 81.3 receiving yards per game, which would put him on pace for more than 1,380 yards over a 17-game season. NFL receiver blocking efficacy/receiving ability through Week 3 The #Packers have a stud in Matthew Golden Also, look at all those #Jaguars WRs! pic.twitter.com/FjMVMEBTm4 — Bradley Locker (@Bradley_Locker) September 29, 2026 That’s some serious production. Locker’s tweet also shows how Higgins is highly effective as a run blocker. Scoring over 80 in both receiving and run-blocking grades shows just how great a start No. 5 is off to, as well as how complete of a wide receiver he is. Higgins has also been doing it without needing a ridiculous number of targets. He’s averaging fewer than five receptions per game, meaning Cincinnati is getting big chunks of yardage whenever Joe Burrow looks his way. The 6-foot-4 receiver has always been capable of making plays down the field, but there’s something particularly encouraging about seeing him establish this kind of consistency early. And that’s before we even get to what his presence does for Ja’Marr Chase. Defenses simply can’t afford to sell out to stop Chase when Higgins is playing like this. The Bengals can move Higgins around, attack different matchups, and let Burrow take whichever favorable matchup the defense gives him. Higgins isn’t just having a good start. He’s making it increasingly difficult for defenses to pick their poison against Cincinnati’s passing game. After three weeks, that’s a pretty encouraging development for a Bengals offense that will need all of its weapons if this team is going to make a run in 2026.

Rasco (Photo by Erick W. Rasco/Sports Illustrated via Getty Images/Getty Images) (Set Number: X164775) The Cincinnati Bengals return to Paycor Stadium this Sunday to take on the tough Jaguars. Jacksonville has had a couple of impressive victories this season, but they will be facing a motivated Bengals team that suffered a tough loss last week in Pittsburgh. To help us preview the game, we tapped the knowledge of Gus Logue over at Big Cat Country. We talked about a myriad of topics before Sunday’s big game. AC: The Jaguars are off to a nice start at 2-1. What’s the pulse on the viability of this team, as they have two dominating wins against teams of questionable caliber, but with Jacksonville also showing clear signs of improvement in year two under Liam Coen? GL: Jacksonville has an 11-2 regular-season record since last year’s bye week. Though it hasn’t exactly been a gauntlet of a schedule — and they’ve yet to pass the ultimate test of winning playoff games — the Jaguars are legitimate. They’re a balanced team that can win in a variety of ways. Trevor Lawrence looks unstoppable. The run defense is historically dominant. Ventrell Miller and Bhayshul Tuten have been superb replacing Travis Etienne and Devin Lloyd. And we even saw Travis Hunter catch his first NFL interception last week! Beyond postseason experience, Jacksonville’s biggest concerns are generating a pass rush and going against top pass rushes, but they’ve generally been able to mask those flaws. AC: After an explosive rookie season, Brian Thomas Jr. seemed to regress steeply in year two, and only has seven catches for 88 yards through three games this year. What’s going on there? Is there hope he will begin to turn things around? GL: It’s looking pretty grim right now. Thomas Jr. had two brutal drops in Week 2 that were reminiscent of his drops against Cincy in Week 2 last year. The Jaguars stopped sending him over the middle of the field a long time ago, but the issue now is that they’re not even throwing deep to him. Instead, Thomas Jr. has become a part-time player, mostly just running wind sprints from the X receiver spot. Sixth-round rookie Josh Cameron has taken reps from him, including most high-leverage situations. Cameron already has 2 touchdowns this year thanks to designated targets in the red zone. I waved off trade rumors about Thomas Jr. last year, but at this point, a change of scenery probably makes sense. BT is too talented to be a WR3/4 in Jacksonville when he could be a WR2/3 elsewhere. His game-breaking speed is being wasted because the Jaguars don’t trust him enough to design shot plays for him. Might as well recoup some draft capital, especially with Cameron looking good and Travis Hunter being available as depth. AC: Trevor Lawrence has looked much more capable under Coen and is off to a hot start this year, making plays through the air and with his legs. Are these further signs of him progressing as he hits the peak of his career, an indication of excelling against some opposing teams that are struggling this season, or a little bit of both? GL: By the grace of the football gods, Jacksonville didn’t have to face Myles Garrett in the season opener, but they’ve still played some stout units. The Browns, Broncos, and Patriots were all top-nine defenses by EPA/pass allowed last year, and they all rank top-15 so far this year. Lawrence has faced quality opponents in every game this season, and he’s responded with great performances, matching the aggressiveness of pass rushes by needling tight-window throws before pressure arrives. He’s admittedly had more head-scratching plays than we’d like to see — his 5.3% turnover-worthy play rate ranks seventh-highest among 37 QBs, per PFF — but we’re finally seeing the best of Lawrence for full 60-minute stretches. He’s lettin’ it rip. AC: Which player(s) have surprised you the most this year, in terms of their improvement? GL: Bhayshul Tuten, without a doubt. I actually went into the season thinking that Chris Rodriguez Jr. could end up earning the Jaguars’ starting RB job, but boy, does that seem silly now. Jacksonville’s rushing game is the Tuten show. He looks massively improved as a between-the-tackles rusher compared to last season. Even with Lawrence and the passing game humming, fans are clamoring for Coen to give Tuten the ball more. I also need to shout out DaVon Hamilton, who has always been a great run-stuffing nose tackle for the Jaguars — but currently, “Ham” is playing like a first-team All-Pro. He is single-handedly blowing up plays as we’ve never seen from him before. AC: As of the beginning of the week, FanDuel has Cincinnati as 2.5-point favorites at home this week. What’s your feeling about that line, and how do you see this game going? GL: Cincinnati’s defense is sure to bounce back after allowing Pittsburgh’s Aaron Rodgers to look like Green Bay’s Aaron Rodgers. At the same time, the Steelers hanging 30 points on the Bengals last week gives me confidence that the Jaguars’ offense will continue to fire on all cylinders. On the other side of the ball, I’m definitely terrified of Ja’Marr Chase, who has 31 catches for 391 yards and 2 scores in JUST THREE GAMES against the Jaguars in his career. We’ll see if Travis Hunter is up for that tall of a task. So long as Chase is relatively contained, I expect the Jaguars to cover the spread and win outright in a game that far exceeds the projected total of 51.5 points. Our thanks to Gus Logie over at Big Cat Country for the insight and Week 4 preview! Go check out the other side of the conversation there, too!

title: Bengals News: Shaka Heyward leaves for Miami Dolphins
summary: The Bengals were brought down to earth on Sunday in Pittsburgh, and now they have the task of proving to everyone (possibly even to themselves) who they really are is the team that beat the Buccaneers and Texans in Weeks 1 and 2. They made a flurry of moves on Tuesday, including bringing Mitch Tinsley […]
full_text: The Bengals were brought down to earth on Sunday in Pittsburgh, and now they have the task of proving to everyone (possibly even to themselves) who they really are is the team that beat the Buccaneers and Texans in Weeks 1 and 2. They made a flurry of moves on Tuesday, including bringing Mitch Tinsley back from Houston’s practice squad. They weren’t the only team making roster moves. While Cincy brought Tinsley back to Cincinnati, the Miami Dolphins signed linebacker Shaka Heyward off the Bengals’ practice squad on Tuesday. In Week 4 the Bengals host the Jacksonville Jaguars, but they travel to Miami to play the Dolphins the following week where they could see Heyward on the field. Heyward a 2023 undrafted rookie out of Duke, logged 10 combined tackles in eight appearances. He is very much aware of the Bengals’ defensive inner workings and schemes, and Miami may be looking to take advantage. Here’s what else is going on: With Jalen Davis headed to IR with a hamstring issue, the most likely fix in the secondary is moving Dax Hill into the slot and calling on rookie third-round pick Tacario Davis to take over outside opposite DJ Turner . That’s what happened during the game in Pittsburgh. Hill is familiar with the nickel corner position, both with the Bengals and in college. Mark Duffner’s Nickname For Joe Burrow And Other Bengals-Jags Tidbits “I’m very excited about the Bengals continuing to improve the roster, and I’ll also say this,” Duffner says. “I hope like heck that this team can reach the heights that I hope they can and bring a championship to Mr. Brown. I’m very much pulling for that possibility to occur.” Solomon Wilcots lists several reasons the Bengals’ defense isn’t that much improved from where it was over the last couple seasons, the chief of which has been the team’s inability to tackle. He also points to the fact the Bengals’ defense has allowed 27 or more points in two of the team’s three games. The Bengals aren’t the only team making roster moves. While the Bengals brought Mitchell Tinsley back to Cincinnati from Houston’s practice squad, the Miami Dolphins signed linebacker Shaka Heyward off the Bengals’ practice squad. In Week 4 the Bengals host the Jacksonville Jaguars, but they travel to Miami to play the Dolphins the following week where they could see Heyward on the field. Bengals’ Tanner Hudson: Signed to Cincinnati’s active roster The Bengals signed Hudson off the practice squad to the active roster Tuesday. Hudson was elevated from the practice squad for two of the Bengals’ first three games of the regular season, accumulating three catches on as many targets for 17 yards. He’ll now be a part of the team’s 53-man roster moving forward and will contribute mostly on special teams and in a depth role on offense behind fellow tight ends Mike Gesicki, Drew Sample and Erick All.

The Steelers and Ravens have been the standard bearers […]
full_text: Normally, most AFC North drama revolves around the Cleveland Browns and, sometimes, the Cincinnati Bengals . This offseason and heading into the regular season, contract drama seemed likely for the Pittsburgh Steelers with CB Joey Porter Jr. and possible for the Baltimore Ravens with QB Lamar Jackson . The Steelers and Ravens have been the standard bearers in the AFC North for a long time; drama hasn’t always followed them. For Pittsburgh, Week 4’s matchup with the Cleveland Browns is for the division lead, but they had already ruled Porter out for the game because his back became a problem in Wednesday’s practice . The back wasn’t bad enough to stop the Steelers from dealing away their problem corner on Wednesday night, sending Porter to the Dallas Cowboys in exchange for a future second-round pick: More about the Steelers agreeing to trade Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder, via @bepryor and @toddarcher : https://t.co/NzIl0p16Ru — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 1, 2026 This is the third trade between the two teams where the Cowboys received a player the Steelers had selected high in previous NFL drafts. WR George Pickens and OT Broderick Jones were also acquired by Dallas. An interesting note for the Cowboys is that both Porter and Pickens are due for new contracts and are represented by agent David Mulugheta. Not only is Mulugheta responsible for the Browns contract with QB Deshaun Watson , but owner Jerry Jones’ standoff with the agent last year led to DE/LB Micah Parsons being traded away from Dallas. Porter was already ruled out for Thursday Night Football, and now he is off the team. Two other Steelers cornerbacks, Jalen Ramsey and Brandin Echols , are questionable for tonight’s game. In a twist no one saw coming, the winner of the game will be ensured to close out Week 4 in first place in the AFC North Division. The Browns are riding a two-game winning streak fueled by a dominant defense and an offense that can’t much right until the fourth quarter. Pittsburgh, meanwhile, took down the Bengals last week for their second win of the season, but have never won a road division game on a Thursday night, which bodes well for a Browns team that would be a perennial playoff team if they could only play on Thursday nights. It is the Browns vs. the Steelers in the 150th meeting of the AFC’s oldest rivalry. First place is on the line, and the stadium should be rocking. Here is everything to know about the game. First meeting: The Browns won the first meeting, 30-17, on October 7, 1950. All-time series: Pittsburgh leads the all-time series, 83-65-1, but the Browns have won four in a row and six of the last seven games played in Cleveland. News & Notes The Browns have won seven consecutive games overall on Thursday night, and nine consecutive home games on Thursday night. The Steelers are 0-9 all-time in divisional road games on Thursday night. Mason Graham is the first Cleveland defender to register a sack in the first three games of the season since Myles Garrett in 2019. Harold Fannin Jr. is leading the Browns in receptions (14), and his nine career touchdowns are tied for fifth among all tight ends since 2025. Cleveland’s defense has gone 48 consecutive games without allowing a 300-yard passer, the longest current streak in the NFL. Pittsburgh quarterback Aaron Rodgers last 300-yard passing game was in Week 14 of the 2024 season, a span of 23 consecutive games. Deshaun Watson has thrown for two touchdowns and no interceptions in each of Cleveland’s wins, joining Baker Mayfield, Derek Anderson, and Vinny Testaverde as the only Cleveland quarterbacks in the past 35 years to accomplish that in consecutive victories. Watson is the first Cleveland quarterback to throw a game-winning touchdown pass in the final four minutes of regulation in consecutive games since Brian Sipe in 1980. Denzel Boston leads all rookies with 195 receiving yards and is tied for first among rookies with two touchdown receptions. Andre Szmyt has made 20 consecutive field goals, tied for the fifth-longest streak in franchise history. The Browns are +16 in the final two minutes of the halves, the best total in the NFL. title: Steelers-Browns Thursday Night tilt to add next chapter to long-time rivalry
summary: If you were to tell me that the Cleveland Browns would enter Week 4 with a 2-1 record and the opportunity to be in first place in the AFC North in a rebuilding year, no one would believe you, especially after Week 1. However, it is true. Many experts (including myself) didn’t believe that the […]
full_text: If you were to tell me that the Cleveland Browns would enter Week 4 with a 2-1 record and the opportunity to be in first place in the AFC North in a rebuilding year, no one would believe you, especially after Week 1 . However, it is true. Many experts (including myself) didn’t believe that the Browns would have a winning record early on this season. The opening day loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars left fans thinking whether or not this team would win a single game but somehow, Cleveland was able to string together two straight victories over NFC South opponents in the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Carolina Panthers. Fast forward to this week and the Browns have a rare opportunity in front of them. If you were to ask Steelers fans or Browns fans if this game is important, you might get different answers. For Cleveland fans, this game is important. The players and the coaching staff also understand the importance of this game. To be honest, we don’t know if Pittsburgh is a good football team . Their wins over the Atlanta Falcons and Cincinnati Bengals weren’t overly impressive, and this team has flaws that can be exploited. As for the Browns, we thought we knew this team isn’t making the playoffs, but this team isn’t as bad as people thought they were, so everything is possible. Offensively, Cleveland has talent, but the limitations are due to the quarterback position. The offensive line appears to be ahead of schedule, and the skill position group is talented. Defensively, the Browns don’t have star defensive end Myles Garrett anymore, but defensive tackle Mason Graham is starting to emerge as a star, cornerback Denzel Ward is still playing at an elite level, and defensive end Jared Verse is finding his groove and making an impact. Collectively, this is a team that has talent but is unproven. Winning Thursday Night Football will not only be big for the team, but the team has an opportunity to send a statement. Cleveland may not be a playoff contender, but this early in the season, this game could change a lot of opinions. A win against a division rival on a national stage will get the national media’s attention. The Browns are on the right track in terms of their rebuild, but if you want to get people to start talking about you and take you somewhat seriously, Thursday night is the opportunity for it. Thursday’s night’s game against the Pittsburgh Steelers should be viewed as an opportunity for the Cleveland Browns to prove that they aren’t “the same old Browns.” A new chapter in an old rivalry. title: Browns defensive identity coming into focus
summary: After a tough start to the season in Week 1, the Cleveland Browns have really turned things around in Week 2 and Week 3. Both sides of the ball have made some major improvements, but the defense in particular is starting to find a good rhythm. In Week One, the defense allowed the Jacksonville Jaguars […]
full_text: After a tough start to the season in Week 1 , the Cleveland Browns have really turned things around in Week 2 and Week 3 . Both sides of the ball have made some major improvements, but the defense in particular is starting to find a good rhythm. In Week One, the defense allowed the Jacksonville Jaguars to score 34 points, and it really felt like the team never had a chance. Overall, they have allowed opposing offenses to score fewer points in the last two weeks, but how they have done it matters, too. They are making big stops in the fourth quarter and late in games, when things matter most. While it is still early in the season, multiple performances like this help build the team’s confidence going into the rest of the season. The pass rush was particularly effective against the Carolina Panthers, tallying three total sacks and eight quarterback hits on QB Bryce Young . DT Mason Graham , in particular, has been a disruptive force on the defensive line. As he continues to gain confidence and establish himself as a leader, his impact will only continue to grow. Moving from Jim Schwartz’s man coverage, few blitzes, to Mike Rutenberg’s more coverage-flexible, blitz-oriented scheme was going to take some time to gel. Week 4 will be another chance for Cleveland’s defense to establish its identity. Let me know what you think in the comments – Is the Browns’ defense starting to find its identity? title: Week 4 Browns NFL Power Rankings: Cleveland enters the Top 20
summary: It is Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Cleveland Browns rose another 5 spots this week, making that a total of 10+ spots they’ve improved after back-to-back wins. All teams in the AFC North are 2-1, but the Bengals’ stock took the biggest hit this week. Overall, the Browns went up by […]
full_text: It is Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Cleveland Browns rose another 5 spots this week, making that a total of 10+ spots they’ve improved after back-to-back wins. All teams in the AFC North are 2-1, but the Bengals’ stock took the biggest hit this week. Overall, the Browns went up by 5.1 spots from week-to-week to have an overall ranking of 20.7 . Here is a summary of how the Cleveland Browns are viewed across mainstream media outlets in NFL Power Rankings heading into Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season. CBS Sports – No. 25 (up 3 spots) Who had them going 2-1 to start, especially after the blowout loss to the Jaguars in Week 1? They are tied for first place in the AFC North. ESPN – No. 24 (up 5 spots) Fantasy surprise: QB Deshaun Watson Expectations were low for Watson, who had performed like one of the worst NFL quarterbacks since joining Cleveland in 2022 and was returning from two Achilles tears. His ADP had him ranked as the QB29, but he’s the QB10 so far this season. Watson’s passing numbers (587 yards, five touchdowns) are modest, but he has turned the ball over only once, and he’s using his legs well. His 105 rushing yards ranks fourth among quarterbacks. NFL.com – No. 17 (up 6 spots) The Browns’ defense is back and playing a cohesive brand that rivals the best units in the NFL over the last two weeks. Mason Graham is off to a fantastic start, Jared Verse has started to make an impact and Carson Schwesinger picked up right where he left off in last season’s Defensive Rookie of the Year campaign. Deshaun Watson also seems to have rediscovered a fourth-quarter clutch mode we haven’t seen from him since he was in Houston. Cleveland’s offense needs to be better, but the Browns have definitely looked competent and earned the last two wins. Sporting News – No. 21 (up 7 spots) Deshaun Watson is putting the Browns in good positions to win in close games. Getting the Buccaneers and Panthers back-to-back brings some needed good offensive vibes under Todd Monken. Don’t forget about Mason Graham living up to be a defensive game-changer. Yahoo Sports – No. 20 (up 4 spots) The Browns have two close wins against the Buccaneers and Panthers, who are a combined 1-5 this season with the only win between them coming against a Cooper Rush-led Falcons team. Cleveland was outgained 360-259 by the Panthers at home on Sunday and caught a nice break that Deshaun Watson’s late interception was nullified due to a questionable roughing the passer penalty. If you want to buy the Browns’ 2-1 start that’s fine, but there are not a lot of signs that this is sustainable going forward. If there is an argument to be made that the Browns can keep this going, it’s their defense. After a horrific Week 1 against the Jaguars, the defense has been sixth in the NFL in EPA allowed per play over the last two weeks. Mike Rutenberg took over defensive coordinator job from Jim Schwartz this past offseason and the opening game was concerning, but the group has settled in since then. Bleacher Report – No. 20 (up 8 spots) The Cleveland Browns are racking up wins against the NFC South, beating the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Carolina Panthers by close margins. Deshaun Watson only completed about half of his pass attempts in the previous outing, but he’s doing enough to lead the Browns to victories, throwing two touchdown passes without an interception in back-to-back games. We’ll see how Cleveland handles a little success in a division matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers coming up on a short week. USA Today – No. 18 (up 4 spots) An unanticipated Deshaun Watson breakout vaulted them back to a 2-1 record and a four-way tie atop (at the bottom?) of the AFC North. full_text: Photo by Randy Litzinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys haven’t had any luck when it comes to injuries in 2026, and multiple guys have been added to the injured reserve list. To counter that, Dallas has added several players in the secondary to their practice squad. Now it looks like they are going even further in adding to their injured secondary. Reports are that a trade for Joey Porter Jr. is happening. BREAKING: Cowboys trading with Steelers for CB Joey Porter Jr. – RJ Ochoa, BTB Jerry Jones wasn’t lying about being ready to trade to help the team. Word broke late Wednesday night that the Cowboys have executed yet another trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers, this one for cornerback Joey Porter Jr. Reports earlier on Wednesday (and Sunday) suggested that the Cowboys were interested in Porter. Clearly that wound up being accurate as they wound up pulling off a deal for him. From a source: the Cowboys are giving up a sixth-round pick in 2027 and a second rounder in 2028 for Porter. https://t.co/Zn4ojgSPPv — Todd Archer (@toddarcher) October 1, 2026 Injuries, moving parts forcing Cowboys to simplify defensive gameplan vs. Texans – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News The Cowboys have been ravaged by injuries in the first three weeks of the season. As a result, their approach defensively has been adjusted for the Texans. FRISCO — The Cowboys are dealing with injuries at all three levels of their defense . They’ve had 29 different players take snaps on defense this season. There’s the possibility for even more Sunday against the Houston Texans as the injuries continue to pile up. With so much change, should the Cowboys simplify what they do on defense this Sunday? Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said it’s likely. The Cowboys won’t admit it but, but LB Jaishawn Barham is forcing a big change on defense from which there’s no going back – Mauricio Rodriguez, AtoZ Sports Barham has had back-to-back excellent games for the Cowboys as the starting middle linebacker in place of DeMarvion Overshown. It’s clear he needs to stay there. Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Schottenheimer declined to say if he’s the starting middle linebacker yet. “We’re going to play that by ear,” Schottenheimer said . “Jaishawn is earning those opportunities right now with how he’s playing. [. . .] We’ll discuss that. We’ve got to be flexible because of the fact that multiple guys have to wear [the green dot].” Cowboys injury report: Cobie Durant, DeMarvion Overshown DNP – LP Cruz, Blogging The Boys Dallas is banged up, to say the least. The injury report after Wednesday’s practice still has then in an unfavorable spot in that regard. After suffering a heartbreaking last-second finish, the Dallas Cowboys are back in the building. Cowboys 2027 free agents stock report: Otito Ogbonnia emerging on run defense – Jess Haynie, The Landry Hat The Cowboys have quite a few free agents next season. Here’s a look at where they stand as of now. Here on a one-year deal to rotate with Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark, Ogbonnia is starting to rival these big-name defensive linemen on the field. He led all Cowboys with six stops against the Ravens , which was crucial against Derrick Henry and their power run game. title: Full details on Cowboys trade for CB Joey Porter Jr.
summary: The Dallas Cowboys struck a deal with the Pittsburgh Steelers on Wednesday night, something that is becoming a bit of a habit for them these days. full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys struck a deal with the Pittsburgh Steelers on Wednesday night, something that is becoming a bit of a habit for them these days. This particular deal was for veteran cornerback Joey Porter Jr. which is obviously very exciting. This was one of those reports where news of the trade happened and in the immediate aftermath the specific details weren’t available. It took about 20 minutes of real time for reporting on them to finally reach the surface. Serious credit to ESPN’s Todd Archer who got them. The Cowboys are sending a second-round pick and a sixth-round pick to the Steelers, but the years on them are important. The sixth is next year while the second isn’t until 2028. From a source: the Cowboys are giving up a sixth-round pick in 2027 and a second rounder in 2028 for Porter. https://t.co/Zn4ojgSPPv — Todd Archer (@toddarcher) October 1, 2026 It is a massive win that the Cowboys were able to hold on to their second-round pick in 2027, especially given that they are (we all assume) going to have to give Porter Jr. a new deal on top of the trade. They have a small amount of draft capital next year as a whole, so keeping the second is a big deal for the short-term window. Keep in mind that Pittsburgh now owns (as far as the 2027 NFL Draft) Dallas’ third- (Broderick Jones), fifth- (George Pickens), and now sixth-round (Joey Porter Jr.) selections. Although original reporting suggested that the sixth involved was conditional, Archer didn’t mention anything on that. As noted this is a bit of a fluid situation. How do you feel about the second being in 2028?

title: CeeDee Lamb has Dallas Cowboys history in his sights
summary: Earlier this season, CeeDee Lamb climbed the Dallas Cowboys record book. After the first week of the season Lamb passed Dez Bryant on the franchise’s all-time receiving list. Given that Lamb has yet to play 100 career games, it was highly impressive. Lamb has another member of Club 88 in his sights, though. In fact, […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images Earlier this season, CeeDee Lamb climbed the Dallas Cowboys record book. After the first week of the season Lamb passed Dez Bryant on the franchise’s all-time receiving list. Given that Lamb has yet to play 100 career games, it was highly impressive. Lamb has another member of Club 88 in his sights, though. In fact, he has the original member in his sights, Drew Pearson. Lamb needs 98 yards to pass Drew Pearson on the team’s all-time receiving list. It is obviously a matter of when and not if this is going to happen. It could happen on Sunday, for all we know. Lamb has a little bit more of a ways to go to pass the next person on the list in Tony Hill. He currently needs 264 to pass Hill, and when he does he will sit third all-time in franchise history in receiving yards. Both of these figure to happen this season given the math involved. If Lamb wants to pass Michael Irvin and/or Jason Witten, then he is going to need to continue this level of production with the Cowboys for the next handful of years at the very least. That is a conversation for a different day, though. Do you think CeeDee will get it done against Houston? Or will it require another game or more?

title: As injuries mount Cowboys young DTs must step up
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are banged up. Injuries continue to steadily mount across the defense, with the secondary taking the brunt of it. This has forced the team to bring in more resources from the outside to help stop the bleeding. One injury that isn’t drawing as much attention is defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard. The veteran […]
full_text: Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are banged up. Injuries continue to steadily mount across the defense, with the secondary taking the brunt of it. This has forced the team to bring in more resources from the outside to help stop the bleeding. One injury that isn’t drawing as much attention is defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard. The veteran suffered a calf strain against the Ravens on Sunday and is expected to be out for three to five weeks. Unlike the hits to the secondary, this one doesn’t seem as hurtful because the Cowboys still have a very strong interior defensive line unit led by Quinnen Williams, Kenny Clark, and Otito Ogbannia. That’s a little comforting as the big three had a better day versus the Ravens. Williams and Clark have drawn some heat early as they’re both attached to big contracts. Fans expect big things. Both looked sharper against the Ravens, as did the low-cost free agent acquisition Ogbannia, who continues to toss blockers aside and close down running lanes. Having these three means the starting unit remains intact. But the loss of Bullard isn’t as inconsequential as it may seem. The veteran has been the perfect signing for this defense. He’s a savvy defender with smarts and toughness, and adds more heavy hands to the rotation. He is coming off one of the biggest plays of the year for the defense with a huge fourth-down stop when he and fellow DT teammate Ogbannia didn’t give way to the Ravens’ offensive line, causing running back Derrick Henry to be tackled in the backfield and resulting in a turnover on downs. Bullard is an important part of this unit because defensive coordinator Christian Parker relies on a deep rotation of interior defenders. In Parker’s defense this group must hold gaps while battling double-teams. It’s been somewhat effective as teams are having less success running the ball inside on the Cowboys. Sure, the total rushing yards allowed aren’t great, but that’s because they’ve surrendered 50+ yards to each starting quarterback in all three games so far, but if you look at how they’ve contained the starting running backs, the rushing stats tell a different story. Week 1: Cam Skattebo = 4.5 yards per carry Week 2: Jacory Croskey-Merritt = 3.8 yards per carry Week 3: Derrick Henry = 3.4 yards per carry They’re improving. And it helps to have fresh guys always available so the group doesn’t miss a beat on any given series. Last week against the Ravens, the snap count distribution went as follows: 75% Quinnen Williams 70% Kenny Clark 62% Otito Ogbannia 36% Jonathan Bullard 23% LT Overton This means everyone is likely to take on a little more of the workload while Bullard is out, with the rookie fourth-round pick LT Overton being the most obvious beneficiary of playing time. Overton has excellent base strength with a never-ending motor to chase down ball carriers. He also has 33 1/4 inch arms, giving him added range to attack. Overton might not be the only guy getting more opportunities. Undrafted free agent rookie Tommy Dunn was a fan favorite in the preseason for continually making plays, to the point where some thought he could make the 53-man roster despite the team already being so deep at the position. He didn’t, but he cleared waivers and was stashed on the Cowboys’ practice squad. This 305-pound youngster has nice get-off, disciplined hands, and very good functional strength to shut down interior gaps. He’s a great depth piece, and we could see his debut really soon. Over the next month or so, the Cowboys will continue to be tested as they attempt to fill voids left from all their injuries. While handling the depleted secondary remains a daunting task, they are more equipped to handle the loss of Bullard. It just means more opportunities for their rookies, and if these young defensive tackles can replicate his blue-collar efficiency, the defense should be able to keep its interior defense strong.

title: Cowboys roundtable discussion: Christian Parker, the pass rush, and Houston Texans
summary: Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo, Dyllan Rivers, Tom Ryle and Sean Martin.  We’re now three games into the season. It’s time to get your opinion on Christian Parker so far? Mike – Three games […]
full_text: Tom Fox/The Dallas Morning News via Getty Images Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo , Dyllan Rivers , Tom Ryle and Sean Martin. We’re now three games into the season. It’s time to get your opinion on Christian Parker so far? Mike – Three games in, my opinion on Christian Parker is still incomplete, but it’s not blind confidence. You can see he wants the defense to be aggressive and built around disguise. The problem is that the execution has been too inconsistent to fully trust it yet. I like the structure more than last year, and I think the defense has looked better coached in stretches, but Parker still has to prove he can adjust quicker and keep this unit from giving up the back-breaking play at the worst possible time. Right now, I’d call it promising, but still under review. Tom – Clearly, there was a learning curve, but the way the defense performed shows major strides forward. I was convinced going into the game that Derrick Henry was going to run wild, but they stonewalled him repeatedly. The pass defense is not as far along as the run defense, but given how badly depleted the secondary was by the end of the Ravens game, that is harder to judge. Still, I feel much better about losing a game where the Cowboys just made one or two mistakes too many. Jorge – I’m not as optimistic as Tom. I’m not sure the defense has improved in any facet, third-down percentage in Week 3 aside, to make a difference, and in some instances it looks like they have gotten worse, e.g., the pass rush. The Ravens still ran for 192 yards, and when the defense needed stops the most, they were completely unable to stop Baltimore, including that disaster final play, which should never, ever happen. I feel like that was on Parker more than anything. Maybe he needs to be in the booth, but I just feel like he hasn’t brought the juice; this team’s defense just isn’t much better than last year’s horrible iteration, and that is very concerning, even if it is early. Sean – Really, all we know so far is last year the Cowboys had defensive lapses and breakdowns at a rate incompatible with winning games, and it lasted all year under one-and-done coordinator Matt Eberflus. Through three games in 2026, a lot of these lapses and breakdowns are still happening, but there’s a runway ahead to change it. Injuries are never a good enough excuse on their own, but there is significant talent on defense on the bench right now too. We’ve all wanted to see Parker find a way to make more of an immediate impact, but let’s be fair and ask ourselves when was the last time a Dallas defense was above average to great against mobile quarterbacks? I can’t even remember one, and so far they’ve been exposed the most by Jaxson Dart, Jayden Daniels, and Lamar Jackson. Let’s give it time. Dyllan – The defense has improved every week. In fact, I think the defense was actually the best unit on the field on Sunday when you consider the full context of the situations they were put in and the results. They still weren’t good enough, but I don’t think it’s unfair to be excited about their growth. The most worrisome part at this point in the season is the injuries. The Cowboys secondary is completely devastated. It’s tough to grow as a unit when players are being shuffled in and out of the lineup. We’ll see how that impacts them moving forward, but all things considered my optimism remains moderately-high for where the unit will be in the coming weeks. The Cowboys have only two sacks on the season. How concerned are you about the pass rush at this stage of the season? Mike – Best way to put it is concerned, but not completely panicking just yet. If Quinnen Williams, Kenny Clark, Rashan Gary and the edge rotation are at least forcing hurried throws, moving quarterbacks off their spot, and helping the coverage, then the sack numbers should eventually correct, or at least that’s my hope. For now, it is a warning and not a full-blown emergency, but I really want this Cowboys pass rush to show up soon. Tom – We have to be concerned, but I think that the focus for the Rio game was on shoring up the run defense. If they can continue to keep that going, then hopefully they can work more on getting to the QB. This is where Parker faces a big challenge. He has some good tools to work with, like Jaishawn Barham, but he definitely needs to figure out how to get more from the defensive line. We have to anticipate some more growing pains. But while Dallas has dug itself a little hole already, it is not too late to salvage the season, especially in a division where two starting quarterbacks are already lost for the year. It is still important to find a way to win this Sunday. Jorge – The pass rush is not only nonexistent, but the rush plans are unimaginative; when the rush does appear, it is undisciplined and wild. Lamar Jackson shifted and manipulated the pocket with ease and took what he wanted when the rush forced him out. The Cowboys also don’t have anybody who moves the needle in that phase of the game. There’s time, but a solid foundation clearly isn’t here at this point. Sean – This part of the defense is very concerning. There’s a reason top edge rushers keep flying up the board on how much of a team’s salary cap they can eat up, they can cover up for so many other holes and change a game in a flash. The Cowboys just don’t have that guy right now, in fact all they have is months of lip service about wanting such a pass rusher, but not getting one. There also has to be something more than just bad luck going on when it comes to how often the Cowboys have been near the quarterback this season but couldn’t bring him down, so that’s another concern. Jaishawn Barham is the awesome middle linebacker they need right now, but we’ve forgotten about how he’s supposed to also be a hybrid between this role and a pass rusher. There just aren’t many answers in this department right now. Dyllan – This is the major issue staring the Cowboys in the face. Sacks are just non-existent. Who lines up in the defensive backfield is inconsequential when the quarterback has all day to throw the ball. This defense is in dire need of a serviceable pass rusher that can consistently be around the quarterback and help other pass rushers get home. Unfortunately, as much as Jerry flirts with the idea of a big trade, the front office is in a tough spot to make that work when you look at anything further than the 2026 season. Parker believed he could scheme up pressures but we just haven’t seen it yet. And that’s why the defense’s potential this year could be capped at mediocre-at-best. This week the Cowboys face their state rival, the Houston Texans. What’s the biggest threat to victory for the Cowboys? Mike – The biggest threat is Dallas letting an 0-3 Texans team play desperate football. Houston has struggled badly to run the ball, ranking near the bottom of the league through three weeks, but C.J. Stroud is still capable of turning a game if the Cowboys give him clean pockets and easy throws. That is where Dallas has to be careful. The Cowboys should have the better roster, but if they bring sloppy discipline and a quiet pass rush into a road game against a desperate state rival, this becomes much harder than it needs to be. Tom – Health, especially in the secondary, and regression. We saw the running game come alive, and that has to continue. The defense has to find a way to not give up too many points while the offense has to cut way down on the mistakes in the red zone. Another continuing worry is the number of penalties on both sides of the ball, including Brandon Aubrey’s kickoffs. Against Baltimore, it is a valid argument that Dallas just shot itself in the foot too often. There is still a lot to clean up. Jorge – The coaching staff. This staff, led by Brian Schottenheimer, put together a…

title: Cowboys report card: Grading Week 3 vs. the Ravens
summary: The Dallas Cowboys came within a few coaching decisions of being 2-1 instead of 1-2. In the NFL, margins come down to a few plays and a couple of bounces of the ball. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer has had a historic start to his head coaching career from a scoring standpoint, but none of that […]
full_text: Dallas Cowboys' quarterback #04 Dak Prescott pass the ball during the NFL match between the Dallas Cowboys and the Baltimore Ravens at the Maracana Stadium in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on September 27, 2026. (Photo by MAURO PIMENTEL / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys came within a few coaching decisions of being 2-1 instead of 1-2. In the NFL, margins come down to a few plays and a couple of bounces of the ball. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer has had a historic start to his head coaching career from a scoring standpoint, but none of that matters if he can’t beat the good teams on the schedule. With the #Cowboys scoring 31 points tonight, it makes Brian Schottenheimer the 4th head coach in the Super Bowl era to score 30+ points in half of his first 20 games. He joins Mike Martz, Sean McVay and Chip Kelly, per NFL Pro. #DallasCowboys pic.twitter.com/uvyiMv6tEW — Brandon Loree (@Brandoniswrite) September 28, 2026 If the Cowboys scored on their final drive and went for the win instead of the tie, fans would be singing his praises and looking at the Ravens game as a defining moment of his tenure with Dallas. Now, it leaves questions about his ability to make the right calls in big moments. Despite the loss, a handful of players had strong performances that make you feel good about where the season can go if the team stays healthy long enough. Here is the Week 3 report card. A grades: Jaishawn Barham (A+): Over the last three weeks, no one has played better on defense than Jaishawn Barham. The rookie third-round pick has exceeded expectations since DeMarvion Overshown went down with his injury. To not only wear the green dot and command the defense, but also do that away from AT&T Stadium against Lamar Jackson was impressive. His two key fourth-down stops could have earned him an A-plus grade on their own. For years, the Cowboys defense would have buckled in that situation and would have been pushed back off the ball. Instead, Barham showed instincts of a long-time veteran at the position and did everything he could to get the offense the ball back. Impressive stuff from the young player. CeeDee Lamb (A+): When CeeDee Lamb dropped passes in training camp and had inconsistent days in Oxnard, questions started about what kind of year the star wideout would be in. It turns out there was nothing to worry about, and Lamb looks as good as ever. Lamb sits fourth in the NFL with 309 receiving yards and was outstanding against a Ravens secondary that was being pushed around. In the past, the Cowboys offense hasn’t fully capitalized on favorable outside matchups. That wasn’t the case against Malon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins. Lamb should be in line for another career year. Dak Prescott (A): When Dak Prescott was asked to make the big play on Sunday, he delivered more times than not. There were a few drives where he left things on the table to Lamb and George Pickens on the outside, which is why he gets an A instead of an A+. Yes, Prescott is a seasoned vet who deserves the chance to call his own plays at the goal line if he doesn’t agree with what the head coach is saying, but he’s never been like that—at least vocally. Rest assured, if the Cowboys have an opportunity to take the lead late in the fourth quarter five yards from the endzone, he’ll do the right thing and go for the kill shot instead of going for the tie. Caleb Downs (A): Second to Jaishawn Barham, Caleb Downs has probably been the defense’s second-best player on the field. His pass coverage is the only thing not yet on full display this season, but as a run defender, Downs has been everywhere. Both Downs and Barham each have 20 combined tackles in Weeks 1-3, tying Leighton Vander Esch for the most among rookie defenders in team history during that span, per Stathead. How active have #Cowboys Caleb Downs and Jaishawn Barham been on defense? Both rookies each have 20 combined tackles in Weeks 1-3, tying Leighton Vander Esch for the most among rookie defenders in team history during that span. Playmakers making plays. #DallasCowboys pic.twitter.com/ZsKRbVLpQI — Brandon Loree (@Brandoniswrite) September 30, 2026 Downs’ aggressive, no-fear approach has really helped improve Dallas’ run defense this year, and it showed up against a formidable running back in Derrick Henry. Javonte Williams (A-): The Cowboys offensive line got a ton of push in the run game, which led to Javonte Williams having his best outing of the season on the ground. Starting with the opening drive, Williams looked unstoppable. Even though the Cowboys didn’t run the ball as often, their bell cow looked like his old self. On a fourth-down run call at midfield in the second quarter, Williams had the chance to bounce the ball to the outside for a first down and a big gain, but instead fumbled the ball and fell short of the line to gain. It would have given Dallas’ offense the momentum needed to score points after Baltimore had scored 14 unanswered. B grades: George Pickens (B+): After back-to-back weeks of limited involvement in the offense, George Pickens had a nice day, catching seven passes for 82 yards. His grade would have been even higher if the critical third-down catch had held up in the third quarter, when Dallas was down 17-13. A Terence Steele penalty moved the Cowboys offense back, and the drive ended with a blocked field goal. Pickens feels on the verge of a breakout game after a solid outing against the Baltimore secondary. He’ll need it this week as the Cowboys face a Houston Texans defense that’s desperate for its first win of the season. The entire defensive tackle room (B+): After two weeks of criticism, the entire defensive tackle room made their presence felt. Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark looked like their old selves, and Otito Ogbonnia, along with Jonathan Bullard, were really good against the run. Derrick Henry did have his wins against Dallas’ front, but the Cowboys tackles were just as important on the fourth-down stops as Jaishawn Barham. One positive to pull from the loss is the much improved run defense. C grades: Von Miller/Donovan Ezeiruaku (C): The Cowboys just need more from their outside rushers. Von Miller got some key pressures against Lamar Jackson, but like Donovan Ezeiruaku, no one could finish or get close to bringing down the Baltimore quarterback. Miller said he was able to roll out of bed and get eight sacks this year, but maybe the expectations were too high considering he didn’t have an entire offseason with the Cowboys. Even for a future Hall of Fame player like himself, it could take a few weeks to knock off the rust. If the Cowboys’ outside linebackers are going to break out of their funk, this weekend is their chance to do it against a weaker Houston offensive line. D grades: Rashan Gary (D): The Cowboys hoped for a solid edge player when they traded for Rashan Gary, but he’s provided no juice on the outside as a rusher and got caught a few times not setting an edge in the Baltimore game. Since last season, Gary has failed to record a sack or tackle for loss in 13 consecutive games. For a player who had such a hot start to his 2025 season, it’s crazy to see how far he’s fallen off from what he was. Sure, he’s a great leader in the locker room and for the young players, but Dallas needs more production from someone who’s supposed to be a starting defender. Rashan Gary has failed to record a sack or tackle for loss in 13 consecutive games. https://t.co/oEKwYxBSXd — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) September 29, 2026 Markquese Bell (D): When the Cowboys moved Markquese Bell to linebacker in 2023 out of necessity, he looked like a different player. Sure, he was playing out of position, and it was unsustainable in the playoffs, but during the regular season, Bell played with confidence. The player who took the field against the Ravens is a shell of what he’s shown he can do in the past. Bell is a nice special teams player, but he’s shown he’s unreliable as a defender.…
