title: Week 4 is time to get Ashton Jeanty going
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 35-27 Week 3 win at the New Orleans Saints and what to look for Sunday at home against the Kansas City Chiefs: Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick played a season high 84 percent of the offensive […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 35-27 Week 3 win at the New Orleans Saints and what to look for Sunday at home against the Kansas City Chiefs: Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick played a season high 84 percent of the offensive snaps in Week 3. He didn’t produce much for the second straight game. Jeanty had 56 rushing yards on 19 carries and he had three catches for 37 yards. Jeanty is averaging 3.3 yards per carry this season after a strong Week 1. He isn’t getting great run blocking in the past two weeks. This needs to improve. Jack Bech: The second-round pick played 11 snaps before fracturing his forearm. He will be out an extended period of time. He has five catches for 48 yards on six targets this season. This is a disappointing situation for a player who needed to develop in his second season Darien Porter: He returned from missing Week 2 because of a foot injury, but Porter lost his starting job to rookie Zeke Masses. Porter didn’t play on defense and played 19 snaps on special teams against the Saints. It will be interesting to see if he plays any on defense against the Chiefs. Caleb Rogers: The third-round pick played five snaps at right guard when Jackson Powers-Johnson went out late with a groin injury. If Powers-Johnson can’t play Sunday, Rogers could play some. Charles Grant: The offensive lineman, taken in the third round, but didn’t play on offense, but logged five snaps on special teams. Dont’e Thornton: The wide receiver, taken in the fourth round, will be on the injured reserve for, at least, another week. Tonka Hemingway: The fourth-round pick played 53 percent of the defensive snaps, still it was the most of any defensive tackle in the game for the Raiders. He had three tackles. JJ Pegues: The defensive tackle, taken in the sixth round, has been inactive every game this season. He was active in nine of 17 games as a rookie. Cody Lindenberg: The seventh-round pick played 17 snaps on special teams.

title: Raiders-Chiefs Week 4: coaching is key matchup to watch
summary: Andy Reid vs Rob Leonard For the last 13 years, the Raiders have been tormented by the offense and play calling of Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid. Reid and the Chiefs have been to the Super Bowl five times, winning three. Making them the team of the late 2o-teens and early 2020’s. Additionally, […]
full_text: Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Andy Reid vs Rob Leonard For the last 13 years, the Raiders have been tormented by the offense and play calling of Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid. Reid and the Chiefs have been to the Super Bowl five times, winning three. Making them the team of the late 2o-teens and early 2020’s. Additionally, winning nine straight division crowns. Reid has been game-planning his players for career days for nearly 30 years. We’ve seen shovel passes, ring around the rosie, fly sweeps and screens. All kinds of disrespectful plays that show a lack of regard for the rules of defenses. He’s had to do some of his best work lately with less talented players and aging stars on the roster. This week, Reid will need to be at his very best if he hopes to avoid getting shut out in the clutch, like Kellen Moore did on Sunday. Rob Leonard has done amazing things in a short amount of time for the Raiders defense. He’s devised ways to engineer turnovers, attack offenses with proper timing and out-coach opposing offenses. Designing schemes to place players in positions to do what they do best when called on. Through three games, his defense has yet to surrender a fourth-quarter point, often making offenses look foolish. The mighty Raiders defense is ranked first in pressure rate (50%), turnovers (9), forced fumbles (10) and interceptions (4). They are tied for fourth with 10 sacks, ranked fifth with 41 total pressures all while blitzing only 25% of pass plays. Leonard’s unit is playing team defense; communicating, doing things the Raiders haven’t seen in decades, if ever. Spags vs Klint Steve Spagnuolo, Chiefs defensive coordinator, has been a premier defensive mind with his exotic blitz packages for decades. He has developed elite-level talents and his defenses have, in fact, won championships in multiple locations. For the seven years he has coordinated defense in Kansas City, he has left Raiders’ offenses seeing red. Screwing up pre-snap reads with disguised alignments, soft-shoeing receivers (playing man coverage at zone depths), and bringing blitzes from the second and third levels. These were just a few of the many tricks used to completely ground opposing passing games. Rushing attacks have been rendered stationary with run blitzes and the fundamentals he coaches up. and and too much laughing at the Raiders futility. That stops this year. Klint Kubiak, the Raiders head coach and play caller, isn’t accepting flowers after three weeks. Winning isn’t foreign to Kubiak; last season he and the Seattle Seahawks offense won the Super Bowl with Sam Darnold under center. Kubiak has proven to be one heck of a play caller and an even better play designer. His attention to detail, game plan preparation and in-game adjustments have the Raiders offense ranked seventh in scoring offense and EPA per play. Kubiak has been getting it done the old-fashioned way, with multiple tight end sets, a fullback and a run-heavy approach. Impressively, he is getting production from practice squad players in the red zone, stacking up 29.3 points per game and looking unbeatable with maximum efficiency. Doing it with the steely reserve of someone who has been there before. When adversity struck in a hostile environment, down 11 points, his team proceeded to score 19 straight points through the end of the third quarter until it was all over.

title: Raiders injury news: Jackson Powers-Johnson not practicing Wednesday
summary: As the Las Vegas Raiders begin the practice week for their biggest game since the 2021 season, they will do so without starting right guard Jackson Powers-Johnson. Las Vegas coach Klint Kubiak said Wednesday that Powers-Johnson will be out Wednesday because of a groin injury that cost his the five final plays at New Orleans […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images As the Las Vegas Raiders begin the practice week for their biggest game since the 2021 season, they will do so without starting right guard Jackson Powers-Johnson. Las Vegas coach Klint Kubiak said Wednesday that Powers-Johnson will be out Wednesday because of a groin injury that cost his the five final plays at New Orleans on Sunday. Kubiak did say, though, that the team is hopeful Powers-Johnson can practice at some point this week to give him a chance to play. 2025 third-round pick Caleb Rogers spelled Powers-Johnson on Sunday and would be in line to start if Powers-Johnson can’t play. Meanwhile, as expected, Kubiak said rookie starting safety Treydan Stukes will practice fully Wednesday after he cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol. He missed the Saints game. He will be needed Sunday as the 3-0 Raiders host the 3-0 Kansas City Chiefs in a huge early-season game. Kubiak said No. 3 quarterback Aidan O’Connell is still away from the team. He has been gone for 13 days dealing with the death of his father. Kubiak said the team is hopeful O’Connell will return later this week.
author: Bill Williamson

title: Tough stretch will define Raiders’ schedule
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are one of the stories of the early portion of the NFL season as they are a surprising 3-0. However, after beating teams with a 1-5 record in their games not against the Raiders, Las Vegas’ schedule is getting tougher. This upcoming stretch was always considered the teeth of teeth Raiders’ […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are one of the stories of the early portion of the NFL season as they are a surprising 3-0. However, after beating teams with a 1-5 record in their games not against the Raiders, Las Vegas’ schedule is getting tougher. This upcoming stretch was always considered the teeth of teeth Raiders’ schedule and now with a perfect record, this is a crucial stretch that could have serious post-season implications. Let’s dive in: Week 4, Kansas City Chiefs at home: The Raiders and Chiefs are two of three unbeaten teams in the AFC and this game is one of the biggest in the NFL as October foorball hits. The Chiefs look solid as usual and this going to be a tough test. Week 5, at New England Patriots The Patriots are 1-2 after going to the Super Bowl last year. This game may not be as difficult as it seemed it was going to be before the season started. Quarterback Drake Maye has been a turnover machine and that could a bad matchup against the Raiders’ defense, which leads the NFL with nine takeaways. While the Patriots are struggling, this won’t be a sure thing for the Raiders. There is talent in New England and that’s a long road trip. Week 6, Buffalo Bills at home: The Bills is the other 3-0 AFC team. This will be a tough, tough test and a wild atmosphere. Bills Mafia travels well and this will be Buffalo’s first game in Las Vegas with fans allowed in Allegiant Stadium. Week 7, Los Angeles Rams at home: The Rams are a disappointing 1-2, but they’re still the Rams. This will be a massive test for the Raiders. Week 8, at New York Jets: The Jets are 1-2 but they actually are competitive and former Raiders’ quarterback Geno Smith is actually playing decently. This will be one of the Raiders’ easiest games in this stretch, but it may not be an automatic win. Week 9, at San Francisco 49ers: The 49ers are 3-0 and are playing well. The only thing that can get in San Francisco’s way is its health as usual. But this game, a candidate to be finalized to Sunday Night Football, will be a challenge for Klint Kubiak’s team as he coaches against his brother, 49ers’ offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak. Week 10, Seattle Seahawks at home: The defending Super Bowl champions are 2-1 and are still who they are. Kubiak’s former team will be ready for him. Week 11, at Denver Broncos: The Raiders’ first game against Denver ends this stretch. The Broncos are 2-1 and looks capable of making the playoffs again. Conclusion: Again, the next eight games was never going to be easy. But, at least, the Raiders have built a 3-0 cushion heading into it. Plus, they have the confidence that they know how to finish games.
author: Bill Williamson

Bowers had 10 catches for 116 yards and a touchdown as the Raiders improved to 3-0 in a 35-27 win at the New Orleans Saints on Sunday. It was the first such award for Bowers, a 2024 first-round draft pick. Bowers missed the first two games of the season after having knee surgery. title: Assessing the Vikings Offense
summary: It’s been an ugly start to the season for the Minnesota Vikings’ offense, at least from a total yards perspective, but most major efficiency metrics as well. The season began with high hopes for a more productive offense led by a proven veteran in Kyler Murray, who’s ranged between an average to near top ten […]
full_text: Sep 27, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell speaks with quarterback Kyler Murray (1) prior to the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It’s been an ugly start to the season for the Minnesota Vikings’ offense, at least from a total yards perspective, but most major efficiency metrics as well. The season began with high hopes for a more productive offense led by a proven veteran in Kyler Murray, who’s ranged between an average to near top ten quarterback since he entered the league by most major metrics; and a more dynamic running game designed by new assistant head coach and de facto run game coordinator Frank Smith. But the results so far have been disappointing across the board. Here are some metrics and the Vikings ranking: Total Yards (32nd) Passing Attempts (32nd) Passing Yards (32nd) Net Yards per Passing Attempt (31st) Yards per Rushing Attempt (27th) First Downs (32nd) Average Plays per Drive (32nd) Average Yards per Drive (32nd) 3rd Down Conversion Percentage (31st) Team Passer Rating (23rd) Offensive DVOA (30th) Passing DVOA (31st) Rushing DVOA (19th) Red Zone TD Percentage (4th) It’s that last statistic that has helped the Vikings to a middle-of-the-pack 16th ranking in points scored, although that is helped by special teams and defensive takeaways as well. The Vikings offense has only two turnovers as well after three games, which ranks 5th best. But overall the metrics confirm what has been apparent to most observers, including the Vikings coaching staff: the Vikings’ offense is anemic. So why such a poor start to the season? Let’s examine in more detail. Passing Game The season had hardly started when Kyler Murray got knocked out of the game with a concussion, which caused him to miss the second game of the season as well. That led to Carson Wentz taking over for the first two games and playing at a competent, reliable, replacement-level of production that we expect from a healthy Carson Wentz at this stage of his career. He averaged 22 pass attempts per game over his two games as the Vikings pursued a run-heavy approach. He also averaged just 130 net passing yards per game, which is about 90 yards or 40% below average across the league so far this season, and his own average last season. His passer rating and ANY/A are higher this year, however, as he’s taken fewer sack yards with no interceptions and a higher rate of TD passes from a year ago. But overall, it seems that part of the game plan with Wentz as the starter was to run more and take more off of Wentz’s plate and hope that the running game, defense, and special teams would be enough to prevail. But once Murray returned last weekend, net passing yards didn’t improve much, going from the 130 Wentz averaged to just 152 against Tampa Bay. There was always likely to be an acclimation period over the first part of the season for the newcomer Murray as he gets used to the new scheme and players around him in a real game setting, but his essentially missing the first two games with a concussion has delayed that as the Bucs game was essentially his first. And even then after the first drive Justin Jefferson exited the game with an ankle injury, which doubtless upended the game plan- at least the passing game plan- as Kevin O’Connell likes to run the passing game through Jefferson. Murray had a few explosive completions to Jordan Addison in Jefferson’s absence, but he also looked tentative in the pocket. But there were misfires as well. He was a bit off on a couple throws to Addison and one to Hockenson and was out of sync with Hockenson as well on a seam route in which Hockenson held up a bit expecting the pass but Murray threw it expecting Hockenson to continue down the field, resulting in an overthrow. There were also a couple instances where if Murray was just a split second faster in his processing/decision-making, he might have been able to hit on a few other pass attempts as well. These are all issues that are likely to improve with more reps, time on task, and by building more rapport with receivers- and the offensive line. Murray’s average time to throw against the Bucs was 3.34” according to PFF- a little over a half second longer than his 2.80” career average. That suggests a little bit of tentativeness in his first full game in nearly a year, in a new system and with new receivers. Overall, Murray’s adjusted completion percentage (accuracy) was just 66.7% – below his career average of 75.8% meaning he was off on about 3 more passes than usual. It wouldn’t be unusual if that was due to being rusty after not playing for a year and/or not being quite in sync with his new receivers yet. It’s probably underappreciated how losing Jefferson early on, but after a week of game planning and practicing with him expected to play the whole game, creates problems in the passing game plan given that it runs through Jefferson by design. The coaching staff is forced to improvise with plays not practiced during the week and/or different receivers running the routes. Having a new quarterback limits the catalog. Kevin O’Connell said in his Wednesday press conference that he could have done more to adapt to Jefferson’s absence and they will be more prepared on Sunday in the event Jefferson doesn’t play on Sunday. But it’s also fair to say that Jauan Jennings has been a disappointing non-factor in the passing game over the first three games (he missed one of them) and T.J. Hockenson has lost a lot as a route runner. He functions mostly as a stop route runner and checkdown although he had a couple decent receptions on screen passes. Tai Felton also didn’t make much of the extended reps he had with Jefferson out most of the Bucs game. Overall, beyond Jefferson and Addison, the Vikings need a reliable third receiver with some juice. Getting Jennings going on underneath routes seems like the easiest solution- which presumably was why he was signed along with his blocking ability. It would also be nice if a back emerged as a weapon in the passing game. Running Game After a certain amount of buzz about their revamped running game during the off season and training camp- the Vikings running game looks… not much different. It certainly hasn’t been more productive, averaging almost a full yard less per carry than last season. I’m not seeing much, if any, of the more innovative features of the Dolphins running game under Frank Smith and Mike McDaniel, and not that much more push/attention to detail from the offensive line that was an emphasis this offseason for new offensive line coach Keith Carter. That view may reflect more of the recent performance against the Bucs, which have a very stout defensive front and head coach Todd Bowles has always been focused on stopping the run, but I really haven’t noticed all that much change. Hopefully that will be coming soon. Of course like the passing game, some of the disappointment in the running game comes from injuries. In this case, to Jordan Mason. He was the more effective back for the Vikings last season and looked to be even more so this season as he slimmed down a bit and looked a bit more dynamic. But he went on IR after the Packers game and has been missed. God bless Aaron Jones for holding up as the bell cow against the Bears and doing the best he could against the Bucs stout front as well, but he’s not going to last long averaging 20 carries a game like he has the last two. But neither DeeJay Dallas nor Demond Claiborne has shown much as a rusher to earn more reps at this point. And with Jordan Mason out until after the bye-week, the Vikings just added Devin Neal to the running back room- but he averaged just 3.6 yards per carry last year with the Saints. From his scouting reports, Neal is a good fit as a zone-scheme back with good ball security and receiving ability. Not terrible as a pass protector either.…

Minnesota Vikings Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Jordan Mason* RB Thumb DNP IR-OUT Justin Jefferson* WR Ankle DNP Brett Thorson* P Hamstring DNP Aaron Jones* RB NIR-Rest LP Blake Cashman* LB Elbow LP Miami Dolphins Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation De’Von Achane* RB Knee DNP DNP DNP IR-OUT Kenneth Grant DT Lower Leg DNP DNP DNP IR-OUT Rob Beal Jr. EDGE Hamstring DNP Caleb Douglas WR Ankle DNP Tucker Addington LS Shoulder LP Chris Bell* WR Knee LP Storm Duck CB Knee LP Jaylen Wright RB Foot LP Zeek Biggers DL Ankle FP JuJu Brents* CB Knee/Heel FP Aaron Brewer* C Hand FP Dante Trader S Groin FP Seydou Traore TE Thumb FP Josh Uche* EDGE Foot FP Injury Report Terms and Glossary FP = Full participant in practice. LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. NIR = Not injury related. PUP = Physically unable to participate list. IR = Injured reserve. Note: only starters on IR are listed. Player Name* = Starter. Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. Notes on Injured Players For the Vikings, a shorter list but all of them are starters. The key injured player is Justin Jefferson, who missed most of the Bucs game with an ankle sprain. The outlook is that if things go well this week, he’ll play on Sunday. Jordan Mason remains out and Aaron Jones is taking a well-earned rest day. Blake Cashman’s injury seems more like something he’ll work through rather than something that keeps him out of Sunday’s game. And if Brett Thorson can’t go, the Vikings have Johnny Hekker on the practice squad and could elevate him if need be. For the Dolphins, a longer list but mostly either non-starters or minor injuries that are unlikely to keep the players out of Sunday’s game. The key loss for the Dolphins this past weekend was running back De’Von Achane, their best player on offense, who suffered an ACL tear last weekend and is on IR for the rest of the season. Storm Duck- is that a real name? – is officially on the PUP list but could return for Sunday’s game. Backup cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. is also on the PUP list and could return this week as well. We”ll see how the week goes for Justin Jefferson and provide further updates on Thursday and Friday. Stay tuned. Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford

title: Minnesota Vikings News and Links: Onward And Upward!
summary: The JJ McCarthy trade was a shock. I mean, some folks thought it would happen but it is still a shock when it does. It is sad too. Sad for the Vikings team and for JJ. The team really wanted him to be the long term answer and injuries just kept getting in the way […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings passes in the first half against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images The JJ McCarthy trade was a shock. I mean, some folks thought it would happen but it is still a shock when it does. It is sad too. Sad for the Vikings team and for JJ. The team really wanted him to be the long term answer and injuries just kept getting in the way of putting game reps on tape. To me, it is as simple as that. The head coach and GM spoke about the trade and Teasley said one line that resonated with me. “Contracts are not infinite”. If the Vikings kept JJ through the season then trading him in 2027 could be harder especially if he would not have received any game action. The Vikings saved about $4.66 million in total cash and cap space across the remaining portion of the 2026 season ($885,294) and the full 2027 season ($3,775,200). The Vikings will have to absorb $3,178,599 in remaining dead cap for 2027 due to his prorated rookie signing bonus. That extra 3.775M could come in handy. I am not really upset about this situation even though it is a wasted draft pick (Brock Bowers would have been nice. Real nice!). The draft is a crap shoot and failed first round picks are not uncommon. The truth is that you miss every shot you do not take. There is a lot of discussion about the team and specifically KOC letting JJ down or not developing him enough. It is a mystery how or why folks think this but what can you do? If the dude is unable to take real game reps, how can he be developed? Time was running out too. Next year is the last year of his rookie contract and picking up his 5th year option was not going to happen and still wont happen. I am not sure what more KOC could have done. I am certain that JJ would not trade his time at Michigan and the National Championship for anything. But, did Harbuagh develop him enough for the NFL? He attempted 713 passes in college and 243 passes in the NFL regular season, for a combined total of 956 regular season pass attempts. Bo Nix attempted 1,988 in college and 1,272 in the NFL for a total of 3,260 attempts. Is 713 pass attempts enough in college? Others have done it (data from AI) … FEWER THAN 600 ATTEMPTS: Cam Newton (292 attempts): Played only one full season at Auburn before going No. 1 overall. Trey Lance (318 attempts): Started only one full season at North Dakota State before being drafted 3rd overall. Michael Vick (343 attempts): Played just two seasons at Virginia Tech in a highly run-heavy option offense. Anthony Richardson (393 attempts): Started only 13 games at Florida before being taken 4th overall. Mitch Trubisky (572 attempts): Was a one-year starter at North Carolina before being drafted 2nd overall. CLOSE TO J.J. MCCARTHY (600 – 850 ATTEMPTS): Mac Jones (638 attempts): Served as the full-time starter for just one season at Alabama. J.J. McCarthy (713 attempts): Handled a low volume across 28 starts in a run-heavy Michigan offense. Kyler Murray (754 attempts): Only had one full year of starting attempts at Oklahoma. C.J. Stroud (830 attempts): Only started two seasons at Ohio State before departing for the NFL. Hmmmm … maybe it is not the number of pass attempts? Hard to say but he is gone now and the train keeps on keeping on! Onward and Upward! Minnesota Vikings News and Links Prisco’s NFL Week 4 Power Rankings: Bills claim No. 1 status while Vikings continue to climb https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/2026-nfl-power-rankings-week-4-bills-vikings/ Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores is a madman when it comes to calling defense. The philosophy is simple, really: Blitz, blitz, and blitz some more. He has taken defense and made it truly fun to watch. The Vikings are blitzing at a rate of 73-78% of passing plays, depending on the site giving out the data. That is by far the highest percentage in the league — and it’s not close. They are a zone-blitz unit that shows a ton of looks that confuse offensive lines and quarterbacks to the point that the passers are often left seeing ghosts even when the pressure isn’t there. It’s why the Vikings lead the league in sacks with 14 and are quickly becoming a team opposing quarterbacks fear. They registered six sacks of Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield in their 23-16 victory Sunday, a game in which they made the Tampa Bay offensive line look bad. They also ran through backs and tight ends in pass protection, and Mayfield was jumpy all day. It looked like Minnesota was playing with 13 players on defense all day long. The Vikings are 3-0 because of that defense. Their quarterbacks haven’t thrown for over 168 yards in a game because they haven’t needed it, thanks to that dominant defense. Minnesota is up to No. 4 in my Power Rankings as Flores continues to show off his impressive defensive mind. If the offense, with Kyler Murray back under center, can get some flow in the passing game, this is going to be a tough team to beat week in and week out. It’s also going to make for tough weeks for opponents to recover after playing them, since they beat you up on defense. 4 Vikings 3-0-0 If only they had a better offense. They might just be considered the best team in football. Brian Flores and the defense have led them to a 3-0 record. NFL Power Rankings, Week 4: 49ers claim No. 1 spot! I also know Minnesota’s defense is special and the reason these Vikes are 3-0. That’s enough for me to move them into the top 10 for the first time this season, even if I still can’t trust Kyler Murray. NFL Power Rankings: Vikings Surge Continues with 3-0 Start https://www.vikings.com/news/nfl-power-rankings-surge-continues-with-3-0-start No. 6 (up 5 spots): Brent Sobleski – Bleacher Report The Minnesota Vikings understand the exact blueprint for them to be successful, even if it’s not pretty. Brian Flores is going to bring more pressure than any other defensive play-caller and dictate games. The approach is simple yet effective. Kyler Murray’s return to the lineup didn’t exactly jumpstart Minnesota’s offense. The Vikings 230 yards were fewer than the team managed during the previous two weeks with Carson Wentz at the helm. Maybe Murray shows more once he gets comfortable in Kevin O’Connell’s offense. As for now, Minnesota will blitz, blitz and blitz some more to ensure they’re in a position to win every game possible. If QB Kyler Murray settles in without trying to do too much − good job on that front Sunday in Tampa − this team should be really dangerous. ‘New Set of Eyes,’ ‘Fresh Start’ — Ex-Vikings Star Adam Thielen Sees Giants Giving J.J. McCarthy a Baker Mayfield, Sam Darnold-Like Revival Path https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/set-eyes-fresh-start-ex-144059832.html But Thielen, who spent nearly a decade with the Vikings after coming on as an undrafted free agent, isn’t ready to give up on him just yet.Speaking on the “Airing It Out’ radio show on SiriusXM, he explained his stance. “J.J. gets a fresh start. He gets an opportunity to prove who he is and who he thinks he is,” Thielen hoped, after having shared a locker room with McCarthy during the 2025 season before he requested a release. “It’s not a surprising thing,” Thielen added. “The longer you’ve been around this league and in this league and seen all the stuff that’s happened over the years, like, it’s not surprising. I’m very excited for J.J. to get that fresh start, to get a new set of eyes on him, for people to kind of judge him for who…

full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: Johnny Hekker #5 of the Minnesota Vikings punts the ball against the Baltimore Ravens during the third quarter of the preseason game at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Wednesday, the Minnesota Vikings announced another group of practice squad signings. A couple of them came as part of the group that we brought you yesterday , but we’ll give you the full group that they announced today right here. First off, the Vikings brought punter Johnny Hekker back to the practice squad. He’ll serve as insurance once again in the event that Brett Thorson has any further injury issues. Running back Devin Neal, who we brought you news of yesterday, was also announced as a practice squad signing today by the team. The three other players who were announced by the team were running back Audric Estime, outside linebacker Keshawn Banks, and offensive lineman Josh Priebe. Estime is probably the most familiar name of that group. He was drafted by the Denver Broncos in the fifth round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of Notre Dame. He spent his rookie year with the Broncos and was waived following training camp in 2025. After a short stint on the Philadelphia Eagles’ practice squad, he signed with the New Orleans Saints and stayed with them through the rest of the season. He was with the Saints to start this season as well, but was waived by them with an injury settlement a week ago. For his career, he has 122 carries for 508 yards and three touchdowns, and has also caught 17 passes for an additional 130 yards. Banks originally signed with the Green Bay Packers as an undrafted free agent out of San Diego State in 2023. He spent the season on their practice squad before being elevated to the main roster for their wild card playoff game that year. In 2024, he made a brief stop with the Michigan Panthers of the UFL but was then let go so he could sign with the New England Patriots. He appeared in three games for them, got released, signed with the Arizona Cardinals practice squad for the remainder of the season, and then went back to the Panthers in 2025. In 2026, he was selected by the Orlando Storm in the 2026 UFL Draft, then went through training camp with the Atlanta Falcons, and now finds himself in Minnesota. That’s quite the resume. Priebe spent the entire 2025 season on the Miami Dolphins’ practice squad. He was elevated to the main roster once but did not appear in the game he was elevated for. He was waived by the Dolphins on the last day of August. With that, based on the roster page on the Vikings’ main website, the team’s practice squad now looks like this: CB Da’Veawn Armstead OLB Keshawn Banks S Maceo Beard (IPPP exception) WR Dillon Bell WR Michael Briscoe G Henry Byrd OLB Kenny Dyson RB Audric Estime TE Cam Grandy P Johnny Hekker LB Bangally Kamara RB Devin Neal OL Jack Nelson G Josh Priebe DL Jahvaree Ritzie S Tavierre Thomas OLB Jihad Ward If the Vikings make any more moves, we will bring them to you as soon as we have them.

title: Myles Price Named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week
summary: For the second consecutive week, a member of the Minnesota Vikings has been recognized for his play in what’s commonly referred to as the “third phase” of the NFL game. Myles Price has been recognized as the NFC’s Special Teams Player of the Week for Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season. This comes on […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Myles Price #4 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates his punt return for a touchdown against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half at Raymond James Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the second consecutive week, a member of the Minnesota Vikings has been recognized for his play in what’s commonly referred to as the “third phase” of the NFL game. Myles Price has been recognized as the NFC’s Special Teams Player of the Week for Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season. This comes on the heels of Isaiah Rodgers receiving the same award last week. Price had 132 kick return yards and 106 punt return yards in the Vikings’ 23-16 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on Sunday, with the big blow coming on his 86-yard punt return for a touchdown in the first quarter. The score snapped a drought that spanned a decade for the Vikings, as it was the team’s first punt return for a score since Marcus Sherels got one against the Houston Texans in Week 5 of the 2016 season at U.S. Bank Stadium. It’s the only punt return touchdown in the NFL through the first three weeks of the season. Price is loose… Price TOUCHDOWN‼️ @KFAN1003 @PAOnTheMic pic.twitter.com/Uk4jJ90Xf1 — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) September 29, 2026 The 238 return yards by Price are also the most by a player in a game in Vikings’ franchise history, and the most by any player in the NFL since Nyhiem Hines had 241 in Week 18 of the 2023 season. Through the first three weeks of this NFL season, Price leads the NFL in the following categories: Punt return yards (130) Punt return touchdowns (1) Yards per punt return (21.7) Kickoff return yards (353) All-purpose yards (483) This is the 20th time the Vikings have won a weekly player award in the Kevin O’Connell era, including the seventh Special Teams Player of the Week Award. This is also the third time in that stretch that the Vikings have gotten back-to-back weekly player awards. They also accomplished the feat in Weeks 15 and 16 of the 2022 season (Kirk Cousins on offense and Greg Joseph on special teams) and Weeks 6 and 7 of the 2023 season (Jordan Hicks and Camryn Bynum, both on defense). Congratulations to Myles Price on being named the NFC’s Special Teams Player of the Month for Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season!

title: Patriots won’t make sweeping changes after latest O-line injury
summary: The New England Patriots are about to play their fourth game of the season on Sunday, and it will be their third starting a different player at right guard. The ever-reliable Mike Onwenu entered the season locked into the starting role at the position, but suffered a fractured ankle in Week 2 versus Pittsburgh and […]
full_text: The New England Patriots are about to play their fourth game of the season on Sunday, and it will be their third starting a different player at right guard. The ever-reliable Mike Onwenu entered the season locked into the starting role at the position, but suffered a fractured ankle in Week 2 versus Pittsburgh and will miss most if not all of 2026 as a result. His replacement, Greg Van Roten, lasted only one game: the veteran started last week’s loss in Jacksonville but departed the game in the second quarter with a thigh injury. With Van Roten since placed on injured reserve , the Patriots will now start right guard No. 3 against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday. Who will it be? For head coach Mike Vrabel, it comes down to two players. “Walter [Rouse] and Ben [Brown] will work in there today and tomorrow, and we’ll kind of see where that goes for the week,” Vrabel explained on Wednesday. Rouse entered the Jaguars game after Van Roten’s injury and ended up playing the final 41 offensive snaps in the Patriots’ 35-6 defeat. His debut with the team and at this particular position was a challenge for the late-August trade pickup. And yet, the team decided to go with him over the more experienced Ben Brown. The latter backing up the left guard and center positions was the main reason for that, but with the change in circumstances could bring another change in lineup again. Whatever that change will be, it won’t involve players from other positions. One speculated candidate to fill the now-vacant spot, starting left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker, will not factor into the right guard mix according to Vrabel. “The vision that I have for AVT and Will [Campbell], you’re starting to see a little bit of that,” the reigning NFL Coach of the Year said. “I want to continue that.”

title: Drake Maye, Mike Vrabel push back on reported rift among Patriots
summary: As New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel took the podium Wednesday, he was asked about a recent report from WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show regarding himself and quarterback Drake Maye. “Unnamed sources,” Vrabel said sarcastically. “My favorite.” The report, citing those unnamed sources, stated that there were issues between the coach and quarterback dating […]
full_text: As New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel took the podium Wednesday, he was asked about a recent report from WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show regarding himself and quarterback Drake Maye. “Unnamed sources,” Vrabel said sarcastically. “My favorite.” The report, citing those unnamed sources, stated that there were issues between the coach and quarterback dating back to Maye not being “[Vrabel’s] guy.” Vrabel, however, pushed back on that notion. “Let me just tell you why I’m here. I’m here because Drake was the quarterback,” Vrabel said. “Believe it or not, I had choices as to where I wanted to coach. I wanted to coach here because Drake was the quarterback. So, I don’t have really much other to add to that about a comment from an unnamed source. But I’ll just tell you what I’ve told numerous people if they want to ask me why I’m here.” As for Maye, the quarterback feels similarly. “Coach Vrabel’s been one of the best football coaches I’ve had in my life,” Maye said later in the afternoon. “One of the biggest things why this has been so enjoyable for me is playing for Coach. I think we all feel that way now in the locker room. He pushes us hard. I love playing for him, and it’s not going to change, it hasn’t changed, and it won’t change. The way he pushes me and coaches the quarterback in a way that I really respect, and I’m looking forward to getting going and proving to Coach that I can lead this football team and play good football.” The Patriots have gotten off to a 1-2 start, with Maye being perhaps the biggest reason for their struggles after turning the football over seven times. The losing has brought with it the usual negativity, something the Patriots will look to put behind them in Week 4 against the Buffalo Bills. In order to do so, they’ll need a better version of Maye — something Vrabel is trying to bring out of him, along with the rest of the team, this week. “The same thing I’ve been doing: just trying to coach the football team, trying to coach him,” Vrabel said. “I’m not going to coach him the X’s and O’s. I mean, I can show him the defense and say, ‘Hey, this is what these guys may like to try to do.’ But it’s just about the urgency that we have, how we operate and how we get in and out of the huddle and the command of the huddle. The quarterback is a conduit to Josh [McDaniels] and the play caller. I firmly believe that the way that they tell the players that they’re playing with, like, ‘Hey, this is what we’re going to do. This play is going to work not because it’s some great scheme, it’s going to work because we’re going to execute it, or we’re going to make it work.’ “And you get them to believe that whatever he calls is going to be successful. Now, will every one be? No, that’s not how it goes. But that’s what I try to teach them each and every day.”

title: The Number Crunch: What went wrong for the Patriots against Jacksonville
summary: Everything that could have gone wrong for the New England Patriots against the Jacksonville Jaguars came to fruition on Sunday. The fundamentals and execution were poor, ultimately leading to a dreadful defeat by a score of 35-6. The underlying numbers really tell a story of just how bad this game went for Patriots in every […]
full_text: Everything that could have gone wrong for the New England Patriots against the Jacksonville Jaguars came to fruition on Sunday. The fundamentals and execution were poor, ultimately leading to a dreadful defeat by a score of 35-6. The underlying numbers really tell a story of just how bad this game went for Patriots in every which way. Let’s therefore take a look at some key stats that led to this disappointing outcome. Red zone The red zone has been an area where the Patriots have struggled all season long, and it was quite apparent in Jacksonville. Their own offense went 0-for-3 when it got within 20 yards of the end zone. This is a main reason why New England is tied for last in the NFL in points scored per game (12.0). When the Patriots do get in a position to punch it into the end zone, they rarely cash in, ranking 32nd in scoring percentage (23.3%). Meanwhile, the Jaguars were as effective as it gets, going a perfect 5-for-5 in their own red zone opportunities. Middle of the field Jacksonville dominated the Patriots over the middle of the field the entire game. Every passing touchdown thrown by Trevor Lawrence was in this area, and he went a combined 12-of-15 targeting that part of the field. Drake Maye, meanwhile, did not have any success up the middle throughout the game and attempted just seven passes of which he completed for for 38 yards. Jacksonville did a phenomenal job forcing Maye to look on the outside, where he made multiple mistakes and threw both of his interceptions — most notably the one along the left sideline to Kyle Williams, where the route was easily overran by cornerback Jarrian Jones. Run game Of course, the attention flocks to the play of the quarterback, and rightfully so. But maybe if the running game was more productive, Drake Maye would not have had to force as many throws as he did. On Sunday, New England rushed for just 3.2 yards per carry. Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels often elects to run the ball on first down, with the team passing 2.2% below expectation on 1st-and-10. The plan did not work against Jacksonville, and really hasn’t at all up to this point in the season. The Patriots have run the ball on first down just under 57% of the time this season, which is the ninth-highest rate in the NFL. On designed runs on first down in Week 3, a combination of Treveyon Henderson, Rhamondre Stevenson, and Corey Kiner ran 13 times for 41 yards, equating to 3.15 yards per carry. Seven of these runs went for 2 yards or less, and none of them went for a first down. These runs getting stuffed are leading to second-and-long or third-and-long situations, in which Maye is forced to throw the ball. This, in turn, sets the stage for some of his bad decisions. Penalties While this game wasn’t the cleanest on either side, it felt as if the Patriots’ mistakes snowballed and were a big reason for why they couldn’t gain any momentum. New England committed nine penalties for 68 yards, whereas Jacksonville only had seven for 56. The Pats jumped into the neutral zone three times in the game. Combined with the efficiency of the Jaguars offense, the penalties only added to the feeling that the Jaguars were unbeatable on Sunday. A false start by Cameron Latu in the second half made the number of pre-snap penalties by the Patriots a total of four. Morgan Moses also had a detrimental holding call that took a 21-yard run for a touchdown by Maye off the board. The Patriots were not ready to go in Florida. Whether it was the run game, the pass game, the penalties, or even the kicking game, there was not much to write home about in this one. New England has to clean these details up if they want a shot against the Buffalo Bills next week, who are undefeated.

title: Patriots confident in bounce-back skills heading into Bills matchup
summary: The New England Patriots had their proverbial doors blown off in Week 3 by the Jacksonville Jaguars, and are now heading into a pivotal division battle with the Buffalo Bills facing more questions than answers. Standing above all of them is a simple one: how will they respond? Despite now being 1-2 and coming off […]
full_text: The New England Patriots had their proverbial doors blown off in Week 3 by the Jacksonville Jaguars, and are now heading into a pivotal division battle with the Buffalo Bills facing more questions than answers. Standing above all of them is a simple one: how will they respond? Despite now being 1-2 and coming off the worst loss of the Mike Vrabel era, there is optimism for a bounce-back. “I have a lot of faith and confidence in everybody that is here. That is why they’re here,” said Vrabel himself when talking to the media on Monday. “We have to continue to prepare and work with one another. The answers are here. The answers are in this building. We just have to do it much more consistently and continue to find ways to do it together.” The biggest issue for the Patriots through three weeks has been their inability to finish drives, with Drake Maye the main culprit. The third-year quarterback has thrown six interceptions to just one touchdown and also lost a fumble. Getting Maye back on track has to be the team’s top priority right now. However, the pressure will not just be on him, but the rest of the team as well come Sunday. The 35-6 defeat in Jacksonville, after all, was a comprehensive one: offense, defense and special teams all failed to play up to their capabilities. “It’s definitely a bounce-back week when it comes down to it,” said cornerback and team captain Marcus Jones. “It definitely challenges the situation of our leadership, captains and everything. We know what we have in the locker room and when it comes down to it, we have to stick together. We all know that. So, we are going to get back to practice, do the things that we need to do, and then go from there.” Doing all that is easier said than done, especially with a game against the unbeaten Bills coming up. However, hope, or in this case a belief in the program, dies last in the New England locker room. “I love this group,” added linebacker Christian Elliss. “We have a lot of playmakers. We have a lot of guys that have been in this position before. We’ll see. At the end of the day, you have to lace them up again and see what happens. But I know we’re going to respond.”

title: Patriots vs. Bills preview for NFL Week 4
summary: The New England Patriots are entering the fourth week of the 2026 NFL season off the worst defeat of the Mike Vrabel era, a 35-6 blowout at the hands of the Jacksonville Jaguars. Now at 1-2 and facing significant questions at quarterback and several other positions on and off the field, the team is in […]
full_text: The New England Patriots are entering the fourth week of the 2026 NFL season off the worst defeat of the Mike Vrabel era, a 35-6 blowout at the hands of the Jacksonville Jaguars. Now at 1-2 and facing significant questions at quarterback and several other positions on and off the field, the team is in dire need of a rebound and some success to start righting the ship again. Unfortunately, the next opportunity to do so will see the Patriots go up against one of the best teams in the NFL. The Buffalo Bills have won all three of their games so far and despite being led by a rookie head coach appear well-positioned to regain the AFC East crown they saw move to New England last season. Ahead of the two rivals’ Week 4 meeting, let’s take a closer look at the Bills and what to expect from them on Sunday. Bills key stats When you start a season with three straight wins, you obviously are doing something right. In the Bills’ case it is playing offensive football. The unit led by former league MVP Josh Allen at quarterback has been one of the best in football no matter how you want to look at it. New England will need to bring its A-game in order to slow down the Bills, especially in the run game: whereas the Patriots have been uneven defending the run, their upcoming opponent has been as good as any team in the league in that area. As for Buffalo’s defense, it hasn’t performed on quite the same level. While still good enough to help the team start 3-0, it doesn’t stand out in any particular metric. For a Patriots offense all out of sorts so far this season, this is an opportunity to build some much-needed momentum. Bills 2026 season As noted above, the Bills started the year with three straight victories. The first one came on the road against Houston, followed by wins over the Lions and Chargers to move the team to 3-0 and the current second place in the AFC playoff picture. Week 1: 36-31 win at Houston Texans (1-0) Week 2: 41-31 win vs. Detroit Lions (2-0) Week 3: 24-16 win vs. Los Angeles Chargers (3-0) The Bills have certainly been impressive this year, but their opponents have all struggled as well. The Texans, Lions and Chargers are a combined 2-4 in their other games this year; both of those wins have come courtesy of the Lions. Possibly the best quarterback in the NFL, he is again off to a hot start. In three games so far, Allen has completed 56 of 86 pass attempt (65.1%) for 786 yards with five touchdowns and two interceptions. In addition, he has gained 119 rushing yards and scored a league-leading six touchdowns on 23 non-kneel-down carries. Add his effective rushing performance — 5.2 yards per carry — to his passing success and you get a quarterback currently ranked fourth in the NFL in EPA per play (0.355). For comparison, his Patriots counterpart Drake Maye is ranked 28th (-0.070). For as much of a cheat-code he can be, Allen cannot sustainably carry the Bills offense by himself. Luckily, his supporting cast has been top-notch as well, especially two players: running back James Cook, who has 346 rushing yards, two touchdowns, and a league-best 6.0 yards per carry to his name, and tight end Dalton Kincaid, catcher of a team-best 14 passes for 263 yards and a score. Cook and Kincaid are two of the best players on an offense also heavily featuring the likes of D.J. Moore (11-167-1), Khalil Shakir (8-94-0) and Keon Coleman (8-101-0). Meanwhile, Joshua Palmer has scored on both of his receptions for a combined 77 yards. The skill positions are complemented by a stout offensive line whose starters have all been with the team last year as well and who have played plenty of football together. That chemistry in combination with creative play designs and well-timed calls has allowed Buffalo to control the line of scrimmage in all three of its games thus far. Defensively, Gregory Rousseau is the name to watch and somebody capable of giving the right side of the Patriots line all sort of problems. His six sacks are the most in the NFL so far this season, as are his three forced fumbles. The Bills’ defensive line is a pick-your-poison unit up front, with Rousseau complemented by Bradley Chubb and a talented interior pairing in Ed Oliver and Deone Walker. If the top dog commands extra attention, the others are more than capable of winning 1-on-1s elsewhere. Behind the talented front four, the Bills are again led by starting linebackers Terrel Bernard and Dorian Williams; despite the team’s extensive coaching changes, the two have remained in place as the top two at the position. Consistency in general has been a common theme for the Bills in multiple areas across their roster. One exception is the secondary, where two starters — safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson and nickel CB Dee Alford — only joined the team through free agency in March. Both have performed well this year, with Gardner-Johnson notching the team’s only interception so far. On the outside, Christian Benford and Maxwell Hairston are a solid pairing. Speaking of solid, Tyler Bass has gone 4-for-4 on field goals and 11-of-12 on extra points so far this year. Greg Dortch is averaging 9.0 yards per punt return. title: Examining the roster ties between Patriots, Bills ahead of Week 4
summary: The connections between the coaching staffs range from Bo Hardegree and Trace McSorley to Doug Marrone, Todd Downing and Scott Booker. But there’s additional familiarity to account for on the field. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, two former New England Patriots and six former Buffalo Bills find themselves in the fold […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WA - SEPTEMBER 09: Reggie Gilliam #44 of the New England Patriots runs off of the field at half time during an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The connections between the coaching staffs range from Bo Hardegree and Trace McSorley to Doug Marrone, Todd Downing and Scott Booker. But there’s additional familiarity to account for on the field. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, two former New England Patriots and six former Buffalo Bills find themselves in the fold for the AFC East opener. Here’s a glance through those ties ahead of Sunday’s 1 p.m. ET kickoff at Highmark Stadium. BUFFALO Brock Lampe, fullback — Lampe joined the practice squad in Orchard Park midway through September. That was the next move after reverting to injured reserve and reaching an injury settlement with the Seattle Seahawks in the preseason. The 23-year-old fullback out of Northern Illinois originally entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2025. He did so in Foxborough. After spending his rookie season on injured reserve due to a leg injury, Lampe was waived by the Patriots heading into training camp in July. Trent Sherfield Sr., wide receiver — Sherfield signed to New England’s practice squad leading up the divisional round last January. After being released on the eve of the AFC title game, he re-signed ahead of Super Bowl LX. The 30-year-old wide receiver was not retained on a futures contract in February. But Sherfield stayed in the division with the Bills and subsequently joined the practice squad at its formation. Since going undrafted in 2018, the Vanderbilt alum has handled 2,684 snaps on offense and 1,804 snaps on special teams. His career stretches 124 games, including 14 starts, along with 89 receptions for 1,034 yards and six touchdowns. The veteran has also spent time with the Arizona Cardinals, San Francisco 49ers, Miami Dolphins, Minnesota Vikings and Denver Broncos. NEW ENGLAND Reggie Gilliam, fullback — As the new league year opened in March, the Patriots closed in on a three-year deal with Gilliam. The 29-year-old fullback has since notched one reception and two starts for New England while splitting his snaps between the offense and the kicking game. Buffalo marked the first NFL stop for Gilliam. Signed as an undrafted free agent in 2020, the former second-team All-MAC selection out of Toledo went on to appear in 94 games and make a dozen starts during his Bills tenure. Gilliam had a hand in 153 yards and two touchdowns from scrimmage across 25 touches. He also had a hand in 29 tackles, two forced fumbles, one fumble recovery and AFC Special Teams Player of the Week honors. Mack Hollins, wide receiver — The Patriots signed Holins to a two-year contract in 2025 and altered the incentives in the agreement entering 2026. The 33-year-old wide receiver has made 15 starts for New England in the regular season along with 58 catches for 706 yards and two touchdowns. Before arriving at Gillette Stadium, he started 13 games as a member of the Bills in 2024. Hollins’ lone campaign with the previous AFC East champions included a team-high five touchdown receptions. Entering the NFL in the fourth round of the 2017 draft at No. 118 overall, the North Carolina Tar Heel earned a Super Bowl LII ring as a rookie with the Philadelphia Eagles and has also been a Miami Dolphin, Las Vegas Raider and Atlanta Falcon. He finds himself 130 games, 220 catches, 2,775 yards and 17 touchdowns in. Greg Van Roten, guard — After visiting Foxborough in August, the 36-year-old Van Roten returned to sign a one-year deal following the preseason opener. He started at right guard last week with incumbent Mike Onwenu on injured reserve due to a broken ankle, yet exited with a thigh injury before halftime and has since landed on IR, as well. A veteran of 147 games, including 106 starts, the former All-Ivy League selection out of Penn began his career as an undrafted rookie in 2012. Van Roten has since made stops with nine different NFL organizations, plus the CFL, in a career approaching 7,000 offensive downs. For the 2022 Bills, he appeared in 16 games and got the nod for four starts. Da’Metrius Weatherspoon, guard — New England added Weatherspoon to the practice squad on Wednesday. The 23-year-old offensive lineman had entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent in May. And with Buffalo. The Bills waived Weatherspoon at the 53-man roster deadline in August after a rookie preseason that included 67 snaps between left and right tackle. A former HBCU All-American at Howard, Weatherspoon transferred to Syracuse for the 2024 and 2025 campaigns and made 22 starts for the Orange while playing both tackle spots as well as left guard. DaQuan Jones, defensive tackle — The Patriots signed Jones to the 53-man roster in September after the 34-year-old defensive tackle was hosted on a visit in August. On a one-year deal now, he had spent the previous four campaigns in the fold for the Bills. Standing 169 games into a career that got underway in the fourth round of the 2014 NFL draft at No. 112 overall, the Penn State product has started 161. His run in the league spans 374 tackles, 20 sacks, four forced fumbles, three fumble recoveries, one interception and one touchdown. Prior to finding his first AFC East home as a free agent in 2022, Jones made stops with the Tennessee Titans and Carolina Panthers. Mitch Wishnowsky, punter — New England promoted Wishnowsky to the 53-man roster after he served as a standard elevation twice in as many weeks to begin the regular season. The 34-year-old joined the initial practice squad as Patriots punter and holder Bryce Baringer landed on injured reserve in August. Before then, Wishnowsky had spent the majority of 2025 with Buffalo and was released at the cutdown deadline following the preseason. The former Ray Guy Award winner by way of Australia, Santa Barbara City College and the University of Utah originally entered the NFL with the 49ers in the fourth round of the 2019 class at No. 110 overall. Through 108 games, he has amassed 358 punts for 16,288 yards and a long of 74, good for an average of 45.5 yards per and 40.9 net yards per.

title: Vikings sign two former Saints running backs ahead of their Week 5 matchup
summary: The New Orleans Saints’ roster has already been plagued by some unfortunate injuries just four weeks into the season. In Sunday’s loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, running back Travis Etienne Jr. suffered a hamstring injury that could sideline him for some time. With Etienne potentially out, the Saints could now be looking for another […]
full_text: Dec 28, 2025; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; New Orleans Saints running back Audric Estime (30) runs with the ball against the Tennessee Titans during the second half at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New Orleans Saints’ roster has already been plagued by some unfortunate injuries just four weeks into the season. In Sunday’s loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, running back Travis Etienne Jr. suffered a hamstring injury that could sideline him for some time. With Etienne potentially out, the Saints could now be looking for another running back to help fill his role in the offense. And in what you could call the worst possible timing for New Orleans, the Minnesota Vikings have signed two former Saints running backs, Devin Neal and Audric Estime, to their practice squad. Both Neal and Estime were with the Saints earlier this season before injuries led to their departures. Neal was selected by New Orleans in the sixth round of the 2025 NFL Draft after a productive career at Kansas. As a rookie, he appeared in 10 games for the Saints, rushing 57 times for 206 yards and two touchdowns while adding 17 receptions for 104 yards. Neal entered his second year with an opportunity to compete for a larger role in the backfield but was hampered by a hamstring injury. He was placed on injured reserve during final roster cuts before the Saints reached an injury settlement with him Sept. 3. A fifth-round pick by the Denver Broncos in 2024, Estime joined the Saints during the 2025 season and appeared in seven games for New Orleans, rushing for 198 yards and a touchdown on 46 carries. He scored a touchdown in the Saints’ 2026 preseason opener before suffering a thigh injury. Estime was eventually placed on injured reserve Sept. 12 and waived with an injury settlement last week. Now both backs have landed in Minnesota while the Saints suddenly find themselves needing additional help in the backfield. Adding another layer to the timing, the Saints will host the Vikings in Week 5, meaning Neal and Estime could be playing against New Orleans not long after joining their new team.

title: Saints vs. Raiders Game MVP: Who stood out in Week 3?
summary: With the game against the Las Vegas Raiders ending the way it did, it can be easy to overlook some of the positives that came from the matchup. This was a game that the New Orleans Saints can learn a lot from, especially when it comes to closing out games. However, one player showed up […]
full_text: With the game against the Las Vegas Raiders ending the way it did, it can be easy to overlook some of the positives that came from the matchup. This was a game that the New Orleans Saints can learn a lot from, especially when it comes to closing out games. However, one player showed up and performed exceptionally well throughout the entire game. Had it not been for his performance, the Saints might not have even been able to take the lead. First and foremost, let’s acknowledge the fans. It was the home opener of the season, and the Dome was rocking. The fans remained locked in through all the emotions of the game and kept the pressure on the Raiders. It was beautiful to see the Dome back in action on Sunday. Game MVP: Chris Olave Chris Olave was the unquestioned MVP of this game. Through three weeks, Olave is making his case to be the best receiver in the league. Olave was targeted 13 times, caught nine passes, and finished with 107 receiving yards. He averaged 11.9 yards per reception, and some of those catches were difficult and contested. So far this season, Olave has 27 receptions, which is tied for first in the NFL; 375 receiving yards, which ranks second in the league; and 36 targets, which is also tied for first. He is averaging 125 receiving yards per game, ranking second in the NFL. Olave also has 20 receptions that have resulted in first downs, which ranks among the league leaders. He currently has a PFF grade of 90.2, and every week, he continues to prove that his new contract is well worth it. If the Saints can begin to complement his play with better performances across the team, and Olave can maintain this pace, he will certainly put himself in a position to earn some hardware at the end of the season. Who do you think was the MVP of the game? How do you feel about the team after the first three games?

title: A look back at the history between the Saints and Falcons
summary: In Week 4, the New Orleans Saints will face their first NFC South opponent of the season when they host the Atlanta Falcons for a Monday Night Football showdown on Oct. 5 in the Caesars Superdome. The Saints-Falcons rivalry dates back to Nov. 26, 1967, when New Orleans defeated Atlanta 27-24 at Tulane Stadium during […]
full_text: Football: New Orleans Saints Steve Gleason (37) in action after blocking punt vs Atlanta Falcons Michael Koenen (9) at Louisiana Superdome. First game in Superdome since Hurricane Katrina. New Orleans, LA 9/25/2006 CREDIT: Bob Rosato (Photo by Bob Rosato /Sports Illustrated via Getty Images) (Set Number: X76696 TK1 R9 F0 ) In Week 4, the New Orleans Saints will face their first NFC South opponent of the season when they host the Atlanta Falcons for a Monday Night Football showdown on Oct. 5 in the Caesars Superdome. The Saints-Falcons rivalry dates back to Nov. 26, 1967, when New Orleans defeated Atlanta 27-24 at Tulane Stadium during the Saints’ inaugural season. Monday night will mark the 114th meeting between the two franchises, including one postseason matchup, with Atlanta holding a slim 58-56 edge in the all-time series. Despite the long history between these two teams, they have faced each other just once in the playoffs. That meeting came on Dec. 28, 1991, when the Falcons defeated the Saints 27-20 in an NFC Wild Card matchup at the Louisiana Superdome. New Orleans entered the fourth quarter with a 20-17 lead, but Atlanta responded with 10 unanswered points, highlighted by a 61-yard touchdown pass from Chris Miller to Michael Haynes with 2:41 remaining to seal the victory. While the 1991 playoff meeting remains the only postseason game between the two teams, there have been plenty of memorable moments throughout the rivalry. None, however, were more significant than the “Domecoming” game on Sept. 25, 2006. The Monday night matchup marked the Saints’ return to the Superdome following Hurricane Katrina and became one of the most iconic nights in franchise history. Steve Gleason’s blocked punt, recovered by Curtis Deloatch in the end zone for a touchdown, provided one of the defining moments of the night as the Saints went on to defeat the Falcons 23-3. Twenty years later, these longtime rivals will meet again under the bright lights of the Superdome as the NFL and New Orleans commemorates the anniversary of a game that meant far more than just football to the city and its fans. Kickoff is at 7:15 p.m. CT and the game will be broadcast on ESPN with Joe Buck (play-by-play), Troy Aikman (color analyst) and Laura Rutledge and Lisa Salters (sideline)

full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - SEPTEMBER 27: Noah Fant #87 of the New Orleans Saints scores a touchdown during the second quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders at Caesars Superdome on September 27, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints hoped the signing of Noah Fant could provide another reliable option in the passing game. Through three games, Fant is beginning to show just how valuable he can be to this offense. Fant delivered his best performance of the season in Sunday’s 35-27 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, finishing with four receptions for 33 yards and two touchdowns. According to Pro Football Focus, Fant earned an impressive 89.3 overall offensive grade, while his 90.1 receiving grade was a team-high. Fant may not receive the most attention in the Saints’ passing game, but his ability to make plays when his number is called gives the offense another weapon to work with. He has the athleticism and experience to create mismatches, particularly in the red zone, and Sunday’s performance provided a glimpse of what that could look like in New Orleans. One strong game does not necessarily signal that this will be the usual, but Fant is showing signs that he can become a meaningful part of the Saints’ offense. If he can continue producing at a similar level, New Orleans could have another reliable weapon emerging at tight end just when the offense needs it most. Because after Sunday, it looks like the Saints could have one of the top TE tandems in the league with Juwan Johnson and Fant.

title: NY Giants’ QB Jameis Winston faces questions despite Sunday’s victory
summary: The New York Giants are 1-0 with Jameis Winston as their starting quarterback. At least they are under John Harbaugh in 2026. But somehow it doesn’t feel as though the Giants won on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans. The opening odd for the Giants in Week 4 were as 1.5-point favorites at home against the […]
full_text: New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston throws the ball. | Getty Images The New York Giants are 1-0 with Jameis Winston as their starting quarterback. At least they are under John Harbaugh in 2026. But somehow it doesn’t feel as though the Giants won on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans. The opening odd for the Giants in Week 4 were as 1.5-point favorites at home against the Arizona Cardinals. Since then, the line has flipped and now the Cardinals are favorites on the road against the Winston-led Giants. The media, it seems, is disappointed in the Giants with Winston at quarterback. Yeah, they won… But where were the fireworks on a soggy Sunday? “I feel like – that a lot of people are surprised that we can win a game in the manner that we did,” Winston said. “Because everyone’s so used to me throwing for 500 yards and throwing interceptions. Right? If we were having a conversation about me throwing interceptions and throwing for 300 yards, y’all wouldn’t be asking me a question.” Winston has long been known as a gunslinger in the NFL. His reputation is as the guy who always wants to throw the ball and doesn’t much care whether it’s to the team wearing the same helmet as him. So it was jarring, in a way, when Winston attempted just 22 passes and completed 14 for 118 yards. “When God allows me to manage a football game, now it’s, does he still have it? But, I mean, I done seen a lot of quarterbacks go 62% for less than 150 yards and win a football game, but it’s not a question.” That’s been the question since the Giants beat the Titans. Why didn’t Winston throw more? He did enough to win, sure, and a number of veterans have said since that the Giants would have lost that game a year ago. But still … Why didn’t Jameis throw for more? Does he still have it? “I get it, the identity, right? Like, what y’all used to,” He said. “And that’s why assumptions maker, right?” Winston affirmed, he hasn’t transformed into a milquetoast game manager who’s happy to just be on an NFL field. He wants to throw and he wants to score. But more importantly, he adds, he wants to win . “So, again, my desire is to score some touchdowns this game,” Winston said. “You know? And that’s what my focus (is) on, man. I’ll tell you, playing this position, man, I want to score touchdowns. Like, it’s required. It really – I’m so encouraged because we were inside the 5-yard line twice. Right? And that’s what I talk about, building on the positives and eliminating the negatives. We’re not going to win a lot of games moving backwards. Right? So, we want to make sure that we finish drives with six.” The veterans of the 2025 season are almost unanimous in their assessment of the Giants win over the Titans. To paraphrase, they don’t win that game last year. The Giants managed to claw their way through the adversity of a short week, a nor’easter, and a change in quarterback. They managed to get the win, now’s the time to get better. And that’s what Winston is focused on. “I feel challenged to get better every single day,” he said. “I just think that’s the makeup of who I am as a person, always looking for ways to build on the positives and eliminate the negatives. You hear me say this a lot, no matter the circumstances, conditions, or facts, my mind is on what my heart desires, and that’s to be a Super Bowl winning quarterback.” “I don’t remember who won Super Bowl V,” Winston said. But I want to be remembered for winning Super Bowl 61. Or at least one of them throughout my career.” Super Bowl 61, of course, is the one that will be played on February 14th, 2027. In other words, Winston wants to with the Super Bowl with the Giants. “I know what I’m capable of, but also I know what’s required of me.” he said. “I can make all the throws. I can do anything I put my mind to. I’m blessed to that point. But at the same time, my job is to give the team the best chance to win.” Of course, the Giants brought in another quarterback this week, trading for former 10th overall pick JJ McCarthy. “I think he’s a good kid, and I’m happy to have anyone that’s my teammate,” Winston said of the young man who some think may take his job. “Obviously, we share [that] we won the national championship. We share (that) he got coached by a Harbaugh. I’m getting coached by a Harbaugh right now. We share that – those similarities. But he’s curious. He wants to be great. I think anybody that gets the opportunity to come to a new organization with a fresh start wants to make an impact.” Nobody knows what the future holds. Perhaps McCarthy will get the chance to make an impact as the Giants’ starting quarterback. But for now, Winston is the starter. And he says that he understands the assignment: Put the team in position to win. “I have to play well regardless. It doesn’t matter who’s in the building,” Winston said. “When you’re the quarterback for the New York Football Giants, you have to give your team a chance to win, and that’s just the business that we’re in.”

full_text: Jihad Ward is coming back to the Giants. | Getty Images The New York Giants are bringing veteran edge defender Jihad Ward back to East Rutherford, N.J., per multiple reports. Ward is being signed off the Minnesota Vikings’ practice squad. The Giants, of course, needed depth at the edge position after Brian Burns was lost for the season to a torn ACL. The 32-year-old Ward is an 11-year veteran. He played for the Giants in 2022 and 2023, recording eight sacks over two seasons. Ward, 6-foot-5, 285 pounds, spent last season with the Tennessee Titans, where current Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson was in that role for Tennessee. Ward had five sacks, tying the career-high he set with the Giants in 2023. Ward is also familiar with Giants head coach John Harbaugh. He played for Harbaugh with the Ravens in 2019 and 2020. Ward has played in 136 regular-season game, starting 49. He had 24 career sacks. The Giants terminated the contract of veteran defensive tackle Josh Tupou to make room for Ward. Tupou played in one game for the Giants this season, and could land back on the practice squad.
