title: Why did NY Giants cut Odell Beckham? ‘It just wasn’t working,’ says John Harbaugh
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The New York Giants released franchise icon and fan favorite Odell Beckham Jr. this week, ending a comeback by the veteran wide receiver that had captivated many in the fan base. “We just weren’t getting enough. It just wasn’t working for us. I told him I wanted to be able to […]
full_text: Odell Beckham | Getty Images EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The New York Giants released franchise icon and fan favorite Odell Beckham Jr. this week, ending a comeback by the veteran wide receiver that had captivated many in the fan base. “We just weren’t getting enough. It just wasn’t working for us. I told him I wanted to be able to get more. I wanted to be able to do more, get him on the field more. Whatever the reason, we weren’t able to do it. Put it on us. We weren’t able to get it done, but at this point in time, that’s kind of where we were, and we needed to move on.” Beckham, 34, made the roster after being out of football in 2025. He had just one target and no receptions over three games while playing just 20 offensive snaps. Beckham played for Harbaugh with the Baltimore Ravens in 2023, and the coach has tremendous respect for the player. He admitted it was “tough” to tell him the Giants were moving on. “I did hope he would get more chances, and he didn’t,” Harbaugh said. “That’s where we stood, so I felt like that being the case, we’re not going to be able to get it done roster spot-wise. We need more out of that spot, and that’s what we’re going to do. Nothing about Odell, nothing that he could do in that sense. “It’s just we weren’t able to get it done, make it fit, make it work, whatever you want to call it, and I was hoping we could, and we didn’t.” The Giants’ use a lot of heavy formations with multiple tight ends and fullback Patrick Ricard. Only three receivers — Malik Nabers, Malachi Fields, and Darnell Mooney — are getting consistent snaps. “It just wasn’t the best thing for our offense, as it turned out, when they’re putting the game plan together, as plays are getting called in the game,” Harbaugh said. “If it doesn’t feel like to the coaches that it’s the best thing, then it’s not working. It doesn’t have to be one or two reasons. It just isn’t happening, and that’s the reason. That’s where it stops. “We didn’t think it would make us better or we’d of had him on the field.“We didn’t think it would make us better or we’d of had him on the field. That’s really the end of the conversation. That’s it. “I hope he lands somewhere. I mean, he’s a great friend.I love the guy and, you know, I hope he lands somewhere. He gets a shot … It just wasn’t working here and that’s really, that’s all that needs to be said.” Harbaugh said moving on from Beckham was “what’s best for the team.” “That’s it. And if you think it’s anything else, then you don’t know me and you don’t know what we’re doing here. It’s nothing more than that,” Harbaugh said. “It’s not doing enough for our offense. It’s not doing enough for our team. So, we need to make a change and he’s not thrilled with it either. He wants to play. “So, there’s no deep conversation. There’s no conspiracy theory. It’s just, we’re trying to win games.We’re trying to put the best 48 and best 53 out there for us, for our team right now and that’s it. So, any speculation about all that, that’s just noise. Nobody cares about that. It’s the last thing I care about. So, that’s it. I told you what it is and that’s what it is. “I’m not kidding. I’m not hiding anything. It’s not Watergate.”

McCarthy was acquired in a trade with the Minnesota Vikings for a fifth-round pick earlier this week, giving the Giants another signal caller to help them after losing Jaxson Dart to a season-ending knee injury. Likely spoke about how the Giants are bringing him up to speed. “Really just trying to reiterate the things that I’m talking about with Jameis to him, whether it’s on the field, in the film room, or just walking around in the hallway. Just making sure that whatever quarterback is out there, making sure that I’m on the same page as them. Just trying to get – be 1-0 that week,” Likely said.

title: NY Giants vs. Arizona Cardinals: 6 storylines for Week 4
summary: Things are happening fast around the 2026 New York Giants. Here are some of the storylines to follow in Week 4 as the Giants host the Arizona Cardinals at MetLife Stadium. Kickoff is at 1 p.m. ET. Still ridin’ with Jameis All the chatter this week is around the Giants’ acquisition of J.J. McCarthy. Understandable, […]
full_text: Jameis Winston | Getty Images Things are happening fast around the 2026 New York Giants. Here are some of the storylines to follow in Week 4 as the Giants host the Arizona Cardinals at MetLife Stadium. Kickoff is at 1 p.m. ET. Still ridin’ with Jameis All the chatter this week is around the Giants’ acquisition of J.J. McCarthy. Understandable, since McCarthy is a 23-year-old former first-round pick the Giants heavily considered selecting in the 2024 NFL Draft. Still, Jameis Winston is the starting quarterback. The story really needs to be about how the Giants can help Winston raise his level of play. Winston is 25 of 49 (51%) for 229 yards with no touchdowns, one interception, a passer rating of just 55.6, a league worst QBR of 22.9, and an EPA per play of -0.31, 34th of 36 graded quarterbacks. Week 2, the thought was that a Jaxson Dart-centric game plan did not favor Winston’s strengths. Week 3, wet, blustery conditions weren’t conducive to high-flying offense. Still, there have been too many throws that it was surprising to see the strong-armed Winston miss. They will need more to win games going forward, and Winston will need to do more to keep McCarthy on the sideline. It is certainly possible that if he plays well going forward and the Giants win a decent number of games that Winston will do exactly that. You’ll need a scorecard No Jaxson Dart. No Brian Burns. No Odell Beckham Jr. J.J. McCarthy, Braxton Berries, Charlie Jones in. Perhaps more roster changes coming before Sunday’s 1 p.m. kickoff against the Cardinals. This Giants roster is changing quickly, partially due to injury and partially due to John Harbaugh’s meritocracy. I give Harbaugh credit for moving on from Beckham. There is a ton of respect between the two, and it has been clear cutting Beckham was never a position Harbaugh wanted to be in. He put what he felt was best for the team ahead of his relationship with Beckham, though, and he deserves “Kudos” for that. Super celebration The Giants will be honoring the 40th anniversary of the 1986 Super Bowl team on Sunday. There a pre-game walk-in by players from that team and a halftime ceremony , among other things. Touchdowns, please Rookie placekicker Dominic Zvada has been excellent, but the object on offense is to get seven points, not three. The Giants’ 18 points the last two weeks have all come via field goals. The Giants are 0 for 4 in the red zone over the past two weeks. Questionable play-calling in a couple of situations hasn’t helped. Penalties at key times have been a problem. After putting up 28 points Week 1, the Giants are now averaging 15.3 points per game, 28th in the league. Offensive coordinator Matt Nagy has two powerful running backs at his disposal in Cam Skattebo and Najee Harris. He has Malik Nabers. He has big receiving targets like Isaiah Likely, Malachi Fields, and Theo Johnson. It has become clear that the Giants are not going to be able to rely on consistently generating explosive plays. They have to figure out how to get touchdowns when they have the opportunity. Will the pass rush join the party? I discussed the paucity of the pass rush earlier, so I won’t belabor it. The Giants, though, have got to begin finding ways to make quarterbacks uncomfortable. That needs to start with Jacoby Brissett of Arizona. First place on the line How about that little nugget. If the Giants win, they will at least share first place in the NFC East a quarter of the way through the season. I’m not sure anyone realistically saw that coming.

title: NY Giants’ pass rush must be better, but that is easier said than done
summary: The New York Giants have one quarterback sack in three games, 31st in the NFL. Their 1% sack rate and 25.7% quarterback pressure rate are also 31st. Thank goodness for the Miami Dolphins, the only team below them in all of those categories. The pass rush, led by edge defenders Brian Burns, Abdul Carter, and […]
full_text: Abdul Carter | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants have one quarterback sack in three games, 31st in the NFL. Their 1% sack rate and 25.7% quarterback pressure rate are also 31st. Thank goodness for the Miami Dolphins, the only team below them in all of those categories. The pass rush, led by edge defenders Brian Burns, Abdul Carter, and Kayvon Thibodeaux, and supplemented by athletic inside linebackers as well as defensive backs capable of blitzing, was supposed to be the strength of the Giants’ defense. Especially with the creativity expected from new defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson, creativity he showed throughout the summer. Obviously, that has yet to be the case. The Giants are eighth in the league in points allowed per game (18.3), something they have accomplished despite the lack of pass rush. A ball-control offense, tremendous special teams play, good enough run defense, and five takeaways — tied for fifth in the league — have helped that number. The pass rush has not. Giants head coach John Harbaugh knows that has to change. “What we just need to do is get on track up front in terms of the pass rush. I mean, I think they’re doing a really good job. All those guys have done a very good job against the run,” Harbaugh said. “We’ve been pretty darn consistent against the run. We’ve had a few runs against us in the second half of the last two games that we aren’t happy about. But generally, we’ve been a good run defense. And we want to keep building on that. But we need to get to the quarterback more.” Per NFL Pro, the opponents’ time to throw against the Giants is 2.70, fifth-fastest in the league. So, the ball is being thrown quickly. Giants’ rushers, meanwhile, have the worst “get-off” in the league at .93 seconds to cross the line of scrimmage. Harbaugh knows the Giants have to come up with an answer. “Some of that’s – yeah, some of that, the ball comes out quick. Sometimes they’re chipping. They’re doing a lot of things to offset our pass rush,” Harbaugh said. “But they’re having a little too much success offsetting it right now. So, we’ve got to keep finding ways to get the quarterback on the ground. “The biggest issue probably is the way we’re being attacked. But we’ve got to find a way to overcome those, like I mentioned just in the last answer. So, for us, we’ve got to find a way to overcome those things. It’s always a chess game. It’s always kind of an evolution, back and forth. And we’ve got to find our next move. We’ve got to find our next couple moves to get ourselves to the quarterback. We’ll be working really hard, and we have been, but we’ve got to find – we’ve got to make it happen. And that’s what we’ll be working to do.” Without Burns, who had 16.5 sacks last season and had at 7.5 sacks, in each of his first seven seasons, much of the pass-rush burden will fall to Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux. Carter has the Giants’ only sack and eight pressures, but has yet to showcase the game-wrecking productivity that got him selected No. 3 overall in the 2025 NFL Draft. Carter’s 92 pass rush snaps is fourth-most among edge defenders, but he is tied for 23rd in pressures. There are 27 edge defenders with 50 or more pass rush attempts. Carter’s 8.7% pressure rate is 31st. The Giants need to find ways to get Carter favorable matchups and free him up from the inevitable double teams that will increasingly come his way without Burns. Thibodeaux, who has no sacks, four pressures, and just one quarterback hit in 56 pass rush snaps thus far, is going to play much more with Burns down. He is going to have to step up. “I’ve just got to play my game. I’ve got to command, and I’ve got to make my presence known,” Thibodeaux said during a Tuesday conference call with New York media. Thibodeaux had a career-high 11.5 sacks in 2023, the only double-digit sack season of his four-year career. In his last 25 games, he has just eight. The Giants will need him to be more impactful. The answer, though, is a lot more complicated than “Carter and Thibodeaux need to do better.” Here are a few thoughts: The answer isn’t “blitz more.” To me, and I am not a defensive coordinator, one of the answers has to be “disguise more.” Too often, I think it is clear by defensive formation who is coming on the pass rush, and where they are coming from. That is making life too easy on offensive lines. I would like to see a better job of hiding their intentions, putting doubt into the minds of the quarterback and offensive linemen about who needs to be accounted for. The run defense has, statistically, been OK. Still, it needs to be better. Second-and-5 allows quick game, or another run. Second-and-10 does not. The offense needs to be better. The Giants have scored 18 points the past two weeks. Convert a couple of those red zone opportunities against the Tennessee Titans into touchdowns, and you have a big lead that forces the Titans out of quick game and turns the pass rush loose. However, they do it, the Giants know the pass rush has to actually begin looking like a pass rush.

title: NY Giants news: OBJ released, J.J. McCarthy fit, more
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to as the Giants prepare to stay atop of the NFC East. Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 4 | ESPN.com I think … J.J. McCarthy will save neither himself nor the Giants. In New York, McCarthy will get more spread looks […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to as the Giants prepare to stay atop of the NFC East. Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 4 | ESPN.com I think … J.J. McCarthy will save neither himself nor the Giants. In New York, McCarthy will get more spread looks and RPOs from the gun. Does he have the poise, field vision and accuracy to create explosive plays in that passing game? I’m dubious … but I am interested. The offensive line in New York is far better than the banged-up line the Vikings had for McCarthy in 2025. McCarthy is a slippery mover who should be involved in the option running game, though he needs to protect himself from hits, as he has collected far too many knocks over his short time in the league. I can see Matt Nagy and Greg Roman, the two primary offensive designers in New York, coming up with good, risk-averse game plans that dramatically lower McCarthy’s time to throw (3.22 seconds last season, 14th longest for a QB since 2010) and minimize his opportunities for post-snap decisions. The Vikings were finished with J.J. McCarthy. So why did the Giants want him? | The Athletic A bevy of injuries prevented him from staying on the field enough to develop further. Wonky footwork didn’t allow him to pass the ball with enough accuracy to move the Vikings offense. Off the field, his day-to-day habits, even inside the Vikings’ building, made it difficult for the staff to know what type of mindset they’d be coaching each week. Even though McCarthy played in a pro-style system at Michigan, he often seemed more comfortable flowing out of the pocket. The Vikings worked hard to ingrain him within their complex rhythm-and-timing-based system. During the back half of last season, McCarthy found success, saying that he stopped fixating on the fundamentals and processes and played free. Maybe Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy’s offense, which contains some simpler RPO-style concepts that were a part of the game plan with Dart, will allow McCarthy to think less and let his athleticism take over. Giants Trade For J.J. McCarthy: What Does It Mean For Present, Future Of QB Room? | FOX Sports Make no mistake, this is Dart’s team. The Giants love him and his potential. Even Harbaugh, who wasn’t around when the Giants traded back into the first round to get him in 2025, fell in love with Dart quickly. He made it clear that Dart was a big selling point when he took the Giants job. There are almost no scenarios where he doesn’t enter camp with his old starting job. Once McCarthy is up to speed on the playbook, probably in a couple of weeks, Winston will have to watch his back. His hold on the job could very much be week-to-week. Some of that is because of how one team source described the Giants’ interest in McCarthy: “He’s just a better fit for what we want to do. He’s athletic. He’s much more like Dart than Winston is. He may not be better, but he’s a better fit.” Giants ’ J.J. McCarthy gamble shows they’re not giving up after Jaxson Dart’s injury | SNY.tv Schoen and Harbaugh could easily stick to their guns. Ride through with Winston no matter what. McCarthy seems to be an admission that they misvalued Winston’s worth. If they didn’t trust Jake Haener, elevated from the practice squad, as a backup, there were options in free agency (Jimmy Garoppolo) or practice squads (Josh Johnson) who were more than capable of riding out a game. This aggression for McCarthy (the Vikings would not accept a sixth-round pick in compensation) is a two-fold covering: Both if Winston goes down, or if they’ve seen enough of the 32-year-old and believe they need a switch. The expectation, talking to league sources, is that the Giants do not give up a fifth-round pick unless they plan to play McCarthy in the near future. #BaldyBreakdown of Arvell Reese "From the opening drive of the game, Arvell Reese was a factor" pic.twitter.com/m3AshxlDvh — New York Giants (@Giants) September 29, 2026 Arvell Reese nominated for Pepsi Rookie of the Week | Giants.com Arvell Reese has been nominated for Pepsi Rookie of the Week following the Giants’ 12-7 victory over the Titans in Week 3. The linebacker was everywhere against Tennessee as he finished with a game-high 13 tackles (10 solo), including one tackle for loss, and a pass defensed. The rookie linebacker also performed well in coverage, according to Pro Football Focus. Reese surrendered just three receptions for 14 yards against the Titans, which earned him a passer rating against of just 79.2. In addition to his dominant performance on defense, Reese also made an open-field tackle on Jordan Stout’s 74-yard punt. Yannick Ngakoue says he’s ‘ willing and able ’ if Giants come calling | USAToday.com Veteran pass rusher Yannick Ngakoue has attempted to put himself on the New York Giants’ radar days after Brian Burns suffered a season-ending torn ACL in Sunday’s win over the Tennessee Titans. When a Giants fan suggested the team call the free agent and loop in head coach John Harbaugh, Ngakoue answered with three words: Willing and able. After another fan asked whether he and Harbaugh were on good enough terms to make the call, Ngakoue wrote that “coach is my guy.” From Big Blue View Giants add 2 WRs to roster after releasing Odell Beckham, putting Brian Burns on IR Film shows lots of good … and bad with new Giants QB J.J. title: Scouting Jets offensive lineman Jordan Meredith
summary: The Jets recently acquired former Raiders offensive lineman Jordan Meredith via trade. Today, we break Meredith down in detail. The 28-year old Meredith is listed at 6’2” and 300 pounds and was undrafted out of Western Kentucky in 2021. He has started 20 games in his NFL career, all of them with the Las Vegas […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - SEPTEMBER 27: New York Jets center Jordan Meredith (67) looks down as he walks off of the field at the conclusion of a regular season NFL football game between the New York Jets and the Detroit Lions on September 27, 2026 at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Jets recently acquired former Raiders offensive lineman Jordan Meredith via trade. Today, we break Meredith down in detail. The 28-year old Meredith is listed at 6’2” and 300 pounds and was undrafted out of Western Kentucky in 2021. He has started 20 games in his NFL career, all of them with the Las Vegas Raiders. He played on special teams with the Jets in the first two games of this season, but saw extensive action on offense in the fourth quarter of the Lions game due to an injury. Background Meredith was a two-star high school recruit, who headed to Western Kentucky in 2016 and redshirted his first season before serving as a backup in 2017. From 2018 through 2020, he started all 37 games earning an all-Conference USA honorable mention in 2019 and second-team recognition in 2020. His NFL career began as an undrafted free agent with the Rams, for whom he did not make the roster or practice squad in 2021. Meredith spent most of the 2022 season on the Raiders’ practice squad, although he was also briefly on the Browns’ practice squad as well. He ended up making his NFL debut with Las Vegas, albeit only seeing action on special teams. Over the past three seasons, his role increased. He played in every game and made his first NFL start in 2023, then began the season as a reserve but ultimately started eight games in 2024. At the start of the 2025 season, he was named as the starting center and he started the first nine games there before moving back to guard for two games and then landing on injured reserve. The Jets acquired Meredith at the end of preseason, in exchange for a future year pick swap. Let’s move onto some more in-depth analysis of what Meredith brings to the table, based on in-depth research and film study. Measurables/Athleticism Meredith lacks ideal size and has poor length, which is perhaps why the Raiders were keen to try him at the center position, even moving their previous starting center out to guard to accommodate this. His workout numbers were really good, with a 5.11 in the 40-yard dash, 25 bench press reps and good agility and explosiveness numbers. Usage In college, Meredith only played right guard other than one snap which saw him listed at left tackle. At the NFL level he had some preseason experience at center before the Raiders moved him permanently ahead of the 2025 season. He has otherwise seen plenty of action at both guard spots, and indeed moved back to guard for a couple of games in 2025 before landing on injured reserve. Pass Blocking Meredith’s individual pass protection numbers have been solid throughout most of his college and pro careers. He has a low pressure rate and doesn’t give up many sacks. In 2018 and 2020, he only gave up one sack. However, 2019 may have been his best season for pass protection even though he alllowed three sacks. He only gave up four other pressures all year and his pass protection grade according to Pro Football Focus led the nation. His numbers were solid with the Raiders too, as he only gave up two sacks in his first 18 starts. He did give up three sacks in his final two starts of last season, but that was right before he went on injured reserve, so he may have been limited at the time. Also, those were the two games after he moved from center back to guard, which may have been a factor. The Raiders gave up 10 sacks in one of those games, as the Browns created constant pressure with stunts. Meredith has good feet and is capable of mirroring to stay in front of his man and a good sense of how to direct his man to prevent leverage advantages. He can anchor against a bull rush but if he loses leverage, he may lack the physical tools to recover. Run Blocking Meredith doesn’t necessarily bring power and drive as a run blocker, but he’s athletic enough to make blocks on the move and is good at finding a target in space and angling his man off. In addition, he is also a good pulling option with the athleticism to make reach blocks on the move. As noted, he’s not consistently powerful at the point of attack. However, he does work well on combo blocks. Short Yardage The Raiders’ record at the goal line with Meredith at center was not good last year. In fact, they only had three rushing touchdowns of less than 50 yards all season, from three, three and four yards. However, he did a decent job on this play. They fared slightly better in that category in 2024 when he was at guard, rushing for three one-yard touchdowns, including a quarterback sneak, in his eight starts. Screen Blocking Meredith clearly has the athleticism to get out in front of a screen pass and has impressed with his ability to block in space. Footwork/Technique Meredith moves his feet well to stay in front of rushers and has a decent punch and anchor, although he perhaps over-compensates for his lack of size by over-extending himself at times in the drive phase. His arms were measured at just 31 inches which would be in the bottom 10 for offensive line scouting combine measurements over the past 27 years. This doesn’t tend to affect him once he’s locked onto a block because can extend his arms and lock his elbows to keep his man at bay. He also resets his hands constantly in pass protection. However, he can be slow to get those hands up at times. This also affected him when he was at the center position, because by the time he had snapped the ball and got his hands up, his man was often too quick for him. Penalties Meredith showed a good improvement in terms of his on-field discipline during his college career, reducing his offensive penalty count from eight, to six and then four over the course of his three years as a starter. Penalties haven’t been a major issue during his NFL career either, as he has only been called for seven. Only one of these was a holding call and none were personal fouls. Special Teams Meredith’s only special teams role at the NFL level has been as a blocker on the placekicking unit. This was also the case in college, apart from four plays where he was on the punt protection unit. He had one special teams penalty in college. Instincts/Intelligence Meredith has displayed versatility at the NFL level and is considered to have good awareness and football IQ. He is also regarded as a good communicator. However, at times last year, the Raiders line was in chaos, as they really struggled to pick up stunts. Prior to that, Meredith had shown that he can pick up a basic stunt effectively while at the guard position, so he may not have been the main culprit in that. Meredith is definitely not immune to mental errors, though. On this short yardage play, he clearly expected everyone else to downblock and the nose tackle was able to capitalize on him moving out of the way. He has had three pre-snap penalties at the NFL level, all of them on false starts. He was also called three times for being an illegal man downfield on a pass. Attitude Meredith apparently has some nastiness to his game and a killer instinct in terms of his finishing and aggressiveness. By moving around so much, he has displayed adaptability and a team-first attitude, and his resilience to establish himself with the Raiders having been released five times at the NFL level has been impressive. Injuries Meredith has had some ankle issues during his career, which led to him being placed on injured reserve last season. He had also been limited by an ankle issue during the 2024 season at times. Scheme Fit The Jets have clearly brought Meredith in to be their fourth interior lineman as it seems likely he would be the first man off the bench at all three interior positions. The team’s…

title: New York Jets News: Geno Smith is Having a Historic 2nd Act
summary: The New York Jets are 1-2, and that stinks, but I have something to cheer you up. Geno Smith is delivering a level of quarterback play that we have literally never seen before. It probably isn’t getting attention from the rest of the NFL because of the Jets’ not-so-great record, but it totally deserves more […]
full_text: Sep 27, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (7) runs with the ball aginst Detroit Lions linebacker Derrick Barnes (55) at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Jets are 1-2, and that stinks, but I have something to cheer you up. Geno Smith is delivering a level of quarterback play that we have literally never seen before. It probably isn’t getting attention from the rest of the NFL because of the Jets’ not-so-great record, but it totally deserves more love from anyone who watches the sport. “As far as I can tell, Geno Smith is the first Jets QB to EVER open the first three games of a season with 700+ passing yards 4+ TDs 0 interceptions 70% completions,” Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic wrote. Smith currently leads the league in completion percentage (75.5%) and is top-five in quarterback rating this season. It’s a shame that we’re 1-2 because no one could have predicted that we’d get this insane Smith renaissance season in 2026. Smith has been efficient, has been protective of the football (only one turnover through three games), and is starting to click with his array of playmakers. Jets fans, we are freaking scoring points. The rushing attack admittedly leaves much to be desired right now, which is super disappointing, BUT the Jets are 13th in offensive yards per game, 11th in passing yards per game, and 17th in scoring. The good news is it should only continue to get better. There are several players on offense that we’re waiting to return to the lineup, and as this unit plays more together, they will continue to gel. Appreciate it, Jets fans; we don’t get this every year, that’s for sure. J-E-T-S! Take the game-day conversation with you! title: Eagles Injury Report: DeVonta Smith among 6 players listed under did not practice
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles issued their first official injury report of the week on Wednesday in advance of their Week 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams. Note that this report is an estimation because the team held a walkthrough in lieu of a normal practice. The Eagles listed six players under DID NOT PARTICIPATE: DeVonta […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: DeVonta Smith #6 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on against the Washington Commanders during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles issued their first official injury report of the week on Wednesday in advance of their Week 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams. Note that this report is an estimation because the team held a walkthrough in lieu of a normal practice. The Eagles listed six players under DID NOT PARTICIPATE: DeVonta Smith, Zack Baun, Dallas Goedert, Will Shipley, Hollywood Brown, and Fred Johnson. Smith did not practice on Thursday last week before ramping up to limited on Friday and full go on Saturday before playing against the Chicago Bears. Perhaps he’ll follow a similar path this week as the Eagles look to manage his hamstring injury. If Smith can’t play, well, that’s a big problem. Baun is a new addition to the report with a concussion. He’ll have to be cleared before he can return to the field. If Baun can’t suit up, look for Jeremiah Trotter Jr. to start in his place. Goedert was always expected to miss multiple games, so, the Eagles will probably be without their top tight end again this weekend. Perhaps we’ll see Zach Ertz’s playing time increase in his second game back with the Birds. Shipley is dealing with a foot injury that caused him to miss last Thursday’s practice before being limited on Friday and Saturday. He was able to play against the Bears. We’ll see if he’s able to ramp up in practice over the next two days. Brown and Johnson were unexpectedly added to the injury report after apparently getting banged up in practice last week. Until they return, one must assume they might not be able to suit up. The Eagles listed three players under LIMITED PARTICIPATION: Moro Ojomo, Jordan Davis, and Jihaad Campbell. All three players are new additions to the report. Ojomo is listed with calf and elbow injuries. Davis is dealing with a calf injury. Campbell is dealing with a knee injury. Being listed as limited is better than being listed under DNP. These guys might be able to play against the Rams. The Eagles listed five players under FULL PARTICIPATION: Jonathan Greenard, Jalen Carter, Darius Cooper, Tank Bigsby, and Byron Young. Good to see Greenard was full go once again, just like he was on Saturday before playing on Monday. The Eagles need him to be able to handle a bigger workload … and soon. title: Eagles-Bears Film Review: Rough game for Vic Fangio
summary: The Eagles’ defense had a rough night against the Bears. Ben Johnson had an excellent read on what Vic Fangio wanted to do, and he kept finding ways to turn the Eagles’ aggression against them. The result was a 27-7 loss in which Case Keenum completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards, two touchdowns […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - JANUARY 07: Miami Dolphins defensive coordinator Vic Fangio enters the field prior to a game against the Buffalo Bills at Hard Rock Stadium on January 07, 2024 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles’ defense had a rough night against the Bears. Ben Johnson had an excellent read on what Vic Fangio wanted to do, and he kept finding ways to turn the Eagles’ aggression against them. The result was a 27-7 loss in which Case Keenum completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions. The Eagles did not sack him once. I want to separate the run defense from everything else. The Bears ran 35 times and controlled the ball for nearly 37 minutes, but they only averaged 3.7 yards per carry. I don’t think the Eagles got destroyed by the run. But I think they were terrified after last year. They got hurt because their commitment to stopping it left them vulnerable to play action, and because their pass rush and coverage could not get on the same page. The tackling and communication concern me more than the rushing yards given up. There were still individual performances worth appreciating, and I haven’t lost faith in Fangio after three weeks. But this was bad. I’m hopeful he will work it out. At least we don’t play Ben Johnson every week. He’s becoming Fangio’s kryptonite. Defense Ben Johnson seemed to understand exactly how the Eagles would react after last year’s game. Watch the linebackers and safeties commit to the run action, then look at the space that opens behind them. This wasn’t a case of Keenum repeatedly fitting impossible throws into tight windows. The Bears used the Eagles’ determination to stop the run to make the passing game easier. Fangio got worked over on this one. One issue with starting with a split-safety look is that defenders have to come aggressively downhill. It’s sort of part of the structure. Eagles' Defense All22 vs Bears. 1) Ben Johnson had such a good read on the Eagles' defense all game. He knew they would be aggressive against the run because of last year, and he used that aggressiveness against the Eagles. The Bears were incredibly effective with play action,… pic.twitter.com/RGu480hRjd — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 30, 2026 Last week, I wrote about the Eagles’ inability to rally to the football and tackle consistently. A BGN commenter described this defense as a little soft. I wasn’t ready to use that word then, and I still don’t want to label the whole unit after one clip. But this is a poor look. The Bears push the Eagles into the end zone, and the defense offers too little resistance when it should be fighting for every inch. Whatever scheme you are playing, good defense still requires effort, leverage, and finishing hard. That part has to improve. This defense normally excels at the fundamentals of good defense, but it hasn’t this season. It’s odd to see. 2) I said last week I can't remember an Eagles' defense being so bad at rallying to the football and tackling. I had a great comment on my BGN article that the defense feels a touch soft this year. I'm not ready to say they are weak, but they were pushed into the end zone here,… pic.twitter.com/JVPq375sBX — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 30, 2026 That said, let’s give the run defense some credit. This is a really good Bears rushing attack, and the Eagles made plenty of individual stops. Michael Carter II comes from depth here, reads the play, and makes an excellent tackle. I wouldn’t be surprised if we see more of him if the players ahead of him keep struggling. The run game was part of Johnson’s plan, but the Eagles’ run fits weren’t the main reason they lost. 3) I know the Bears ran the ball a lot and had some success, but I don't think the Eagles defended the run that poorly. This is an excellent run game, and I don't think it was their run defense that cost them. This was an excellent play from depth by Michael Carter, who might… pic.twitter.com/RorgoVoFe4 — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 30, 2026 How often do you see Fangio send a cornerback? The Eagles were looking for pressure because their normal rush wasn’t getting home. This call finally makes Keenum uncomfortable, but it still ends with a completely open completion. That’s the maddening part of this game, and it was frustrating to watch. Even when the front gave the secondary a chance, the coverage broke down. The Bears repeatedly used motion and switch releases, where receivers exchange positions immediately after the snap, to test the Eagles’ communication in match coverage. Here Zack Baun and Cooper DeJean both head toward the flat and end up covering the same receiver. The middle of the field is abandoned. You can see them communicating before the snap. Match coverage is all about communication. The Eagles made so many errors this week. 4) Fangio is clearly annoyed with the pass rush, because we don't see a cornerback blitz very often! This was one of the only times that the Eagles made Case Keenum uncomfortable, but he still ended up with a totally wide-open completion because the Eagles' communication is… pic.twitter.com/tFb6Xif58S — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 30, 2026 I criticized the lack of fight earlier, so I should also mention the first-half goal-line stand. The Eagles made several big plays with their backs against the wall. Jalen Carter made this one without using his right hand. That is impressive, but it also shows the problem. He clearly can’t play right now, and the Eagles desperately need him to be a disruptive player again. He recorded no pressures on 33 pass-rush snaps. The Eagles are paying him a lot of money and can’t rush the quarterback. It’s a big issue. 5) I mentioned a bit of a lack of fight earlier, so it's only fair to point out that the Eagles did have a fantastic goal line stand in the first half. They made some big plays repeatedly at the goal line and did show some fight after the poor TD they gave up earlier. This is… pic.twitter.com/ZSA7Xz90yL — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 30, 2026 Jonathan Greenard did flash in limited snaps, and he gets after Keenum here. The Eagles badly need him healthy and contributing as a pass rusher. But then of course, Andrew Mukuba flies downhill toward the run action, and the receiver runs straight past him. Keenum deserves credit for a terrific throw under pressure, but Johnson has caught the defense out of position again. Mukuba is moving so aggressively toward the line that recovering when the ball goes behind him becomes extremely difficult. 6) Finally, an Eagles pass rusher wins, and Greenard ends up getting pressure. However, look at how aggressively Mukuba comes downhill. He's so focused on the run that the receiver runs right by him for a big gain. There just feels like a lack of awareness with the Eagles defense… pic.twitter.com/9ewcOV903S — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 30, 2026 This in-breaking route is another play where I wanted Mukuba to arrive sooner. Fangio often asks his safeties to come across and cut off crossers, though, and without knowing his precise assignment, I won’t declare this entirely his fault. What I can say with confidence is that Keenum has far too comfortable a pocket. If the quarterback can stand there and wait for a route to develop, every uncertainty in the coverage becomes harder to survive. The Eagles had no quick pressure for long stretches of this game. Keenum played well, but I’m convinced if the Eagles had got pressure on him early and hit him a few times, they could have forced him out of rhythm. When you don’t lay a hand on the quarterback, it’s easy for them to get comfortable back there. Any quarterback in this league can win when he is kept upright and trusts what he is seeing. Keenum was never under any real pressure. 7) The broadcast pointed out this one, and it feels like Mukuba should be getting downhill quicker on this in breaking route. However, we do know…

title: NFL Power Rankings: Week 4 Edition
summary: Now that Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season is in the books, it’s time for an incredibly meaningful and serious exercise: NFL Power Rankings! What differentiates these rankings from all others is that they’re THE only truly accurate ones in the entire universe. Hard to believe, I know. But it’s true. Let’s take a […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during the third quarter of the NFL game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Now that Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season is in the books, it’s time for an incredibly meaningful and serious exercise: NFL Power Rankings ! What differentiates these rankings from all others is that they’re THE only truly accurate ones in the entire universe. Hard to believe, I know. But it’s true. Let’s take a look at how all 32 teams stack up. BLG’S WEEK 4 NFL POWER RANKINGS 1 – Kansas City Chiefs (Last Week: 2) – The Chiefs took care of business by comfortably defeating the worst team in the NFL. 2 – Buffalo Bills (LW: 3) – Josh Allen turned the ball over three times after having zero giveaways in the Bills’ first two games. But he also had two touchdowns to give him a league-leading 11 total on the season as the Bills are off to a 3-0 start. 3 – San Francisco 49ers (LW: 4) – Brock Purdy currently has the second-shortest NFL MVP odds. The Niners are rolling early on. 4 – Seattle Seahawks (LW: 1) – Strange to see this staunch Seahawks defense get carved up by Marcus Mariota. Seattle ran into a more desperate team in Week 3. They’ll probably bounce back and be fine. 5 – Baltimore Ravens (LW: 6) – The Ravens took advantage of the Cowboys’ incompetence to steal a win in regulation. This offense, which ranks fourth in points scored, has looked pretty good in two of their three games thus far. Seems like hiring Ben Johnson assistant Declan Doyle was a good call. 6 – Minnesota Vikings (LW: 9) – Brian Flores is a huge reason why the Vikings are undefeated through three games. Minny’s defense has allowed the second-fewest points in the NFL. 7 – Chicago Bears (LW: 10) – Despite being down to third-string quarterback Case Keenum, the Bears bullied the Eagles on Monday night. Chicago clearly outcoached Nick Sirianni and his staff in that game. 8 – Los Angeles Rams (LW: 5) – Now is not the time to declare the Rams dead. Week 1 was a weird situation and they were done dirty by a bad call late in Week 3. They haven’t hit the ground running but they’re still going to be good. They outgained Denver by 225 yards in a loss on Sunday. 9 – Detroit Lions (LW: 14) – The Lions’ offense is often going to give them a chance to win. Their defense continues to be a major concern, however. 10 – Cincinnati Bengals (LW: 8) – The Bengals’ defense was looking to be improved … and then they gave up nearly 300 yards and three touchdowns to 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers. 11 – Philadelphia Eagles (LW: 7) – Maybe the Eagles just aren’t very good. With all the winning they’ve done in recent years, they certainly deserve some benefit of the doubt. It’s possible they’ll turn things around. So far, though, they just haven’t been a very good football team. How the Eagles compare to other teams in terms of EPA through 3 games (via RBDSM) pic.twitter.com/sF400ohVPG — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) September 30, 2026 Entering Week 4, the Eagles rank 20th in point differential 20th in offensive EPA/play 20th in defensive success rate 22nd in DVOA 24th in defensive EPA/play 28th in offensive success rate — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) September 30, 2026 12 – Dallas Cowboys (LW: 12) – The Cowboys snatched defeat from the jaws of victory. Their defense still looks bad. 13 – Denver Broncos (LW: 16) – It wasn’t pretty but the Broncos picked up a big win against a tough opponent to stay in competition for the top spot in a very competitive AFC West. 14 – Jacksonville Jaguars (LW: 17) – The Jags have the second-best point differential in the NFL. They’re only two points behind the 49ers in the top spot. 15 – Las Vegas Raiders (LW: 18) – The Raiders are fun! Will be very interesting to see how they fare against the Chiefs in a matchup of two 3-0 teams. 16 – New Orleans Saints (LW: 15) – The Saints were outdone by the Raiders in a battle of two teams that seem to be on the rise. 17 – New England Patriots (LW: 11) – Woof. Drake Maye has seven times as many giveaways as he does touchdown passes this season. Less than ideal. 18 – Pittsburgh Steelers (LW: 21) – The Stillers are inevitably competent. 19 – New York Giants (LW: 20) – It’s hard to see the Giants winning a lot of games with Jameis Winston struggling. But credit to them for not totally folding after Jaxson Dart’s injury. 20 – Indianapolis Colts (LW: 24) – The Colts are on the board after a much-needed win to avoid starting 0-3. Still alive. 21 – Washington Commanders (LW: 26) – Marcus Mariota > Jayden Daniels? Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota have each started nine games since 2025. pic.twitter.com/wAWV6jcfiR — Jimmy Kempski (@JimmyKempski) September 27, 2026 22 – Houston Texans (LW: 13) – The Texans are 0-3 and they have the Cowboys up next. Could very well be 0-4. 23 – Green Bay Packers (LW: 19) – The Packers are in desperate need of offensive line help, as evidenced by their flurry of roster moves up front. Not a great spot to be in. 24 – Carolina Panthers (LW: 22) – Losing to the Browns isn’t very serious behavior. 25 – Atlanta Falcons (LW: 31) – Well, Michael Penix Jr. gives the Falcons more of a chance to win than Cooper Rush does. They’ve gone from one of the very worst teams to merely bad instead. 26 – Cleveland Browns (LW: 30) – If the Browns are tanking, they’re not exactly doing it right. 27 – Tampa Bay Buccaneers (LW: 23) – Disaster start to the season for the Bucs. Interested to see if Jalon Daniels gives them a spark? 28 – New York Jets (LW: 28) – The Jets have lost their last two but they were both one-score games. Not looking totally incompetent. 29 – Arizona Cardinals (LW: 27) – It’s not in the Cards for this team this year. Arizona has the toughest remaining schedule in the NFL. 30 – Los Angeles Chargers (LW: 25) – Only two teams have a worse point differential than the Chargers this year. More losing is probably on the way with the Seahawks, Broncos, Chiefs, and Rams up next. It’s simply never gonna happen for this team. 31 – Tennessee Titans (LW: 29) – Cam Ward couldn’t build on some of the promise he showed in Week 2. Very bad interception to end the Titans’ chances in North Jersey. 32 – Miami Dolphins (LW: 32) – No team looks like they want the No. 1 overall pick the 2027 NFL Draft more.

title: Eagles News: An undesirable new franchise record
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Zero takeaways through three games. Not great! In fairness, the Birds have forced a couple fumbles that were recovered by the offense. So, some bad luck there. And with luck being an element in the turnover equation, the Eagles are probably […]
full_text: Jun 10, 2026; Philadelphia, PA, USA; Philadelphia Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio during minicamp at Jefferson Health Training Complex. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Zero takeaways through three games. Not great! In fairness, the Birds have forced a couple fumbles that were recovered by the offense. So, some bad luck there. And with luck being an element in the turnover equation, the Eagles are probably due for some moving forward. That’s the optimistic spin. The less rosy view of this situation is that the Eagles might not have enough playmakers to come up with these takeaways. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Here’s this week’s Roob’s Eagles Stats: Proceed at your own risk – NBCSP How is it possible to play three entire football games without forcing a turnover? That’s where the Eagles are. This is the first time in franchise history the Eagles have opened a season without a takeaway in their first three games. They’re only the 16th NFL team to ever achieve that dubious distinction. Of the first 15, only two reached the playoffs – the 1979 Broncos and 2004 Rams. There have been four previous seasons where the Eagles only forced one turnover through Week 3 – 1996, 1998, 2020 and 2021. This is also only the fourth time the Eagles haven’t intercepted a pass through Week 3. That also happened in 1998, 2020 and 2021. The Eagles have now gone 13 consecutive games without multiple interceptions, the 6th-longest streak in franchise history and the 4th-longest current streak in the NFL. They haven’t had a three-interception game since 2022, and their streak of 65 consecutive games without more than two INTs is by far the longest in franchise history. The next-longest streak is 34 games over the 2019 through 2021 seasons. The 65-game streak is 13th-longest in NFL history. Last time the Eagles picked off three passes in a game was Week 6 of the 2022 season, when C.J. Gardner-Johnson had two and Slay had one off Cooper Rush in a 26-17 win over the Cowboys at the Linc. The Eagles are 1-27-1 in their last 29 games when they’re minus-three or worse in turnover differential. The Eagles are also only the fifth team with no takeaways and three or fewer sacks through Week 3 since sacks became an official stat in 1982. The four others: The 2002 Bengals, 2013 Steelers, 2019 Broncos and 2023 Giants. None of them made the playoffs. Trying to Decipher How Bad This Eagles Defense is – Crossing Broad It brings me no joy to say this, but I think what we saw on Monday night is closer to what this defensive unit actually is, and the elite Week 1 and Week 2 numbers are the fluke. The smoking gun for this theory is how bad Washington and Tennessee’s offenses are. The Commanders are 27th in pass offense and the Titans are 30th in scoring, 31st in total offense, and 30th in pass offense. Those are two bad teams, which is why the Eagles looked nice against them. But when facing Chicago’s actually-good offense — which ranks 3rd in total yards (408.0 YPG) and 1st in rushing (184.3 YPG) — the Eagles got exposed. They had no pass rush, they couldn’t create turnovers, and they allowed Case Keenum of all people to sling the ball wherever he wanted. And sadly, these seem like foundational issues to me. Through three weeks, the Eagles have no takeaways. They have 3 sacks. No need to overcomplicate it. That’s a bad defense. Eagles Film Review: This team looks like they are running two separate offenses – BGN This was a deeply disappointing offensive performance. There were positives on film, and I do not want to ignore them. However, those positives existed within an offense that still doesn’t fit together. Right now, the Eagles look like they are running two separate offenses. They have a shotgun passing game and an under center running game. Those two worlds barely connect. The Eagles ran for 107 yards on 19 attempts, but that success didn’t produce the explosive play-action passes it should. The numbers were ugly. The Eagles finished with 14 first downs and 248 net yards. They went 2-for-9 on third down, 0-for-5 on third-and-long, and 0-for-2 on fourth down. They reached the red zone twice and came away empty once. Andy Dalton’s interception was the single biggest win-probability swing of the game. We will get into that because I’m still angry… For me, the biggest problem was pass protection, particularly against pressure. I’m saying pass protection rather than offensive line play. Cam Jurgens had a poor game in pass protection, but the recurring free rushers were not simply five linemen losing individual blocks. The Eagles repeatedly looked confused about who they wanted to block and which defender they were prepared to leave free. That is a schematic and coaching problem first. Jalen Hurts was largely fine for three quarters before his play deteriorated once the Eagles fell behind by 20. The quarterback was not the main reason this offense failed. NFC East Mixtape Vol. 193: The Upside Down is here and so is JJ McCarthy – NFC East Mixtape Last week brought chaos to the NFC East as the Washington Commanders shocked the reigning champions to change everything we thought about them. Elsewhere in the division… the Dallas Cowboys collapsed against the Baltimore Ravens in Brazil. All the while the New York Giants took care of business against the Tennessee Titans… and then got a new quarterback in JJ McCarthy! Finally, the Philadelphia Eagles were expoed on Monday night by the Chicago Bears and Case Keenum of all people. Needless to say… RJ Ochoa and Brandon Lee Gowton have a lot to discuss! You can see that we have a BRAND NEW NFC East Mixtape YouTube Channel so make sure to subscribe as the show will live here exclusively in video format. AND you can also listen to the show! On Blogging The Boys and/or Bleeding Green Nation podcast feeds as well as the SB Nation NFL Show feed! NFC Hierarchy/Obituary: Week 4 edition – PhillyVoice So what the coaching staff essentially did there was trade an opportunity for three shots into the end zone for one bite at the apple on a type of play that (a) hadn’t worked all season, (b) didn’t really even work when they got a favorable look for it and finally executed it well, and (c) was a risky call that had a high likelihood of burning the rest of the clock if it failed. “We had 19 seconds,” Nick Sirianni said. “We had plenty of time to get it clocked or do what we did in that particular case. They were bringing a certain type of pressure there, and that screen was built into the call, and it worked out to be able to get the touchdown there. But with 19 seconds left you should be able to get another play off.” What?! They were flat out unable to get their next intended play off, which was a spike to stop the clock. They never would have been able to execute that in time, or even come close, and really, they came within hundredths of a second within getting the snap off on the impromptu sneak. If Smith had been tackled, at, saaay, the 3 yard line instead of the 1, there’s a pretty good chance that Hurts would not have made the split-second decision to sneak it from that far away, even if the result of the play showed that he got in easily from the 1. Like, what would that scenario have looked like? My guess is that Hurts’ best bet would have been to take the snap and try to run around hoping a receiver got open in some kind of back yard improv play. Honestly, I’m almost kind of bummed that we didn’t get to see it. Even though it ultimately worked, there is really no good argument for that screen call in that situation, and it’s alarming to me that any 12 year old playing Madden would also recognize that. Something or Nothing? – Iggles Blitz You can’t point to anything to get genuinely excited about. The offense is wildly inconsistent. The defense has underachieved. They only have 3 sacks…

title: We finally learned what makes Jalen Hurts really mad
summary: It was scary when Jalen Hurts took a late hit out of bounds on Monday night against the Bears, and the Eagles QB was forced to undergo a concussion evaluation as a result. He left the field annoyed, but with urgency to get it over with, and Hurts was seen growing increasingly angry the longer […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles takes the field against the Chicago Bears during the second quarter of the game at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was scary when Jalen Hurts took a late hit out of bounds on Monday night against the Bears, and the Eagles QB was forced to undergo a concussion evaluation as a result. He left the field annoyed, but with urgency to get it over with, and Hurts was seen growing increasingly angry the longer he was sidelined. In the moment, I appreciated the emotion from the quarterback, but more than anything, I just wanted him back out on the field. Doing what he does. Competing. What I missed in the moment, was just how much was being revealed by the situation. For years, people have complained about a lack of emotion from Jalen Hurts. They’ve tried to analyze his personality any number of ways, and used his baseline of calm and collected as evidence for both his successes and his failures. They’ve associated that personality with issues in the locker room, and used it as a scapegoat for poor chemistry among former friends. What we saw on Monday night, was the “it” factor. The one thing to make Hurts lose his composure in a fit of anger. They took him out of the game — off the field he’s so often called his most sacred place, and weren’t letting him back to compete alongside his brothers in their quest to win. And, to make things worse, he believed he was fine enough to be on the field, and they took too long to get him there. Instead, he had to watch Andy Dalton throw an interception in the back of the end zone while he waited for the doctors to give him the thumbs up he knew he’d get several minutes earlier. So, we finally saw it. Hurts was mad. He was yelling, cussing, and stomping around. And, it wasn’t because of a turnover, or in the final seconds of an ugly loss, it was when the game was taken away from him and he wasn’t given a chance to contribute. For anyone wondering what it would take to see the infamously even-keeled QB crack, it’s not letting him play football. Holy shit I’ve never seen Jalen this angry 😭 pic.twitter.com/rvIvPy22QP — dhwani (@dhwanisaraiya_) September 30, 2026
author: Alexis Chassen

title: Eagles-Bears snap counts
summary: The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 3 loss to the Chicago Bears are in. Let’s take a look and run through some analysis. OFFENSE DEFENSE SPECIAL TEAMS DID NOT PLAY ACTIVE: Mac McWilliams INACTIVE: Hollywood Brown, Tanner McKee, Cole Payton, A.J. Epenesa, Fred Johnson, Dallas Goedert
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 28: Andy Dalton #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles walks off the field after a preseason game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Lincoln Financial Field on August 28, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 3 loss to the Chicago Bears are in. Let’s take a look and run through some analysis. OFFENSE Only 50 snaps for the offense is low. So low that it tied their season-low for offensive snaps in a game last year, which came in a win over the Minnesota Vikings. Jalen Hurts was pulled from the game by the concussion spotter. Those four snaps he missed turned out to be pretty important since Andy Dalton came in and threw a terrible interception into the end zone for a touchback. Dontayvion Wicks was once again the clear WR2. He was second in wide receiver snaps and targets. Saquon Barkley looked pretty spry out there despite playing with a collar on after suffering a stinger injury last week. Good to see his playing time wasn’t really limited. Makai Lemon’s snap count percentage was a season-high, slightly up from the 63% mark he was at in each of the first two weeks. Johnny Mundt was the Eagles’ top tight end with Dallas Goedert out. Not really an ideal configuration. Zach Ertz was limited to a relatively small role in his first game back with the Eagles. He was still TE2 ahead of E.J. Jenkins, though, in terms of total playing time. Will Shipley was RB2 over Tank Bigsby, who fumbled on one of his two snaps played. That giveaway isn’t going to help Bigsby get more snaps. With Hollywood Brown inactive, Elijah Moore made his Eagles debut in this game. He was not targeted and he did not help out on special teams at all. Darius Cooper looked good in Week 2, including when he made the game-winning touchdown grab. His reward? The fifth-most playing time of any Eagles receiver (behind Moore, who was previously a healthy scratch behind six active receivers in each of the first two games) … and zero targets. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ Markel Bell made his NFL debut on offense in a six offensive linemen package. DEFENSE Cooper DeJean and Quinyon Mitchell are the only Eagles defenders to not miss a snap so far this season. Jalen Carter’s snap count percentage has dropped each week this season (94% to 77% to 71%) while he continues to play through a wrist injury that’s causing him to wear a cast. Jordan Davis logged his highest snap count percentage of the season. He was ahead of Moro Ojomo for the first time this year. Byron Young saw a lot more playing time than he usually does. Guess the Eagles are trying to use him more to help lighten the load of the players ahead of him. Ty Robinson also saw a bigger role than normal to have the Eagles significantly utilize five DTs. Marcus Epps and Michael Carter II rotated as at the safety next to Andrew Mukuba in nickel defense packages. When you have two safeties playing at one spot, you might just have none. Here’s a positive for the defense on what was otherwise a pretty bad night: Jonathan Greenard looked good in his debut. He logged two pressures (including one QB hit), a forced fumble, and a stop in just 18 snaps played. The Eagles need to hope he’s able to handle an increased workload sooner than later. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. saw a little action on defense for the first time this season. SPECIAL TEAMS Chance Campbell saw some special teams action in his Eagles debut and first regular season action since 2023. Quiet night for Jake Elliott, who did a single kickoff and a single extra point. Micah Morris played a single special teams snap in his first-ever NFL game. DID NOT PLAY ACTIVE: Mac McWilliams INACTIVE: Hollywood Brown, Tanner McKee, Cole Payton, A.J. Epenesa, Fred Johnson, Dallas Goedert McWilliams was active but did not play a snap for the first time this season. Goedert, Brown, and Johnson were ruled out due to injury. McKee was the emergency third quarterback once again. He should really be QB2. Dalton shouldn’t be on the team. With Greenard returning to the field, Epenesa was a healthy scratch as the fifth edge rusher.

title: Steelers Week 4 power rankings roundup
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers offense came to life on Sunday, as they defeated the Cincinnati Bengals 30-27 at Acrisure Stadium. The same offense that looked largely lifeless through the first two weeks, scoring only 16 points, showed great improvement. With rookie Max Iheanachor and veteran Brock Hoffman now starting on the right side of the offensive […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers offense came to life on Sunday, as they defeated the Cincinnati Bengals 30-27 at Acrisure Stadium. The same offense that looked largely lifeless through the first two weeks, scoring only 16 points, showed great improvement. With rookie Max Iheanachor and veteran Brock Hoffman now starting on the right side of the offensive line, the Steelers seem to have more freedom running the ball, and Aaron Rodgers seems to have more time to get rid of the ball to his receivers. Let’s take a look at various media outlets to see how much of a bump the Steelers got in the rankings after handing the Bengals their first loss of 2026. FOX Sports: No.14 (No. 21 Last Week) “Aaron Rodgers going throw-for-throw with Joe Burrow at his age, and after his ugly start to the season, wasn’t on anybody’s Bingo card. He even dusted off DK Metcalf, his forgotten No. 1 receiver, and RB Jaylen Warren had a big game with Rico Dowdle out. Beating the Bengals was huge, surprising (at least to me), and deserving of a big jump, even if none of this is exactly how head coach Mike McCarthy drew it up. It was the first sign of life from the Steelers’ stagnant offense. There are no defensive juggernauts in the next five weeks before their bye week, so they’ve got a chance to go on a run if they can keep the scoring up.” – Ralph Vacchiano The Athletic: No.14 (Last Week No.21) “It’s been a big season already for NFL lip-readers. Aaron Rodgers gave them a clip to dissect Sunday in which he was either very mad at Michael Pittman Jr. after a dropped pass, very mad about the overall state of the Steelers offense or just rehearsing material for his next appearance on “The Pat McAfee Show.” It’s tough to tell with Rodgers, who has Pittsburgh in a crowded race in the AFC North despite being beaten by six drops (the third most in the league). He hasn’t been great either, though. He’s 33rd in EPA per dropback (minus-0.26).“ – Chad Graff and Josh Kendall CBS Sports: No.13 (Last Week No. 22) “At 2-1, they are getting some good play from Aaron Rodgers. He looked like the old Rodgers in the victory over the Bengals.” – Pete Prisco Pro Football Talk: No.13 (Last Week No. 18) “There’s some magic left in the post-Tomlin Steelers.” – Mike Florio NFL.com: No.19 (Last Week No.26) “Pittsburgh’s offense woke up! It was refreshing to watch the Steelers finally produce with the approach (aggressively pushing the ball downfield) they’ve been trying to force this season. It wasn’t at all surprising that their defense was the one to finish the job, either. I won’t be taken for an easy sale, though; they’ll need to do it more than once offensively for me to emotionally invest.” – Nick Shook Yahoo! Sports: No.17 (Last Week No. 23) Maybe the Steelers stumbled upon a solution for their offense: Turn Jaylen Warren into a workhorse. Last season, he played 47.4% of the Steelers’ snaps, a lower percentage than Kenneth Gainwell. In Week 1, with Rico Dowdle having been added over the offseason, Warren was at 37.3% of snaps. Dowdle was injured in Week 2, and in Week 3 Warren had the backfield to himself. He had 127 rushing yards on 17 carries and 49 receiving yards on three catches. That opened up the Steelers’ offense, which hadn’t played that well through two weeks. Aaron Rodgers had a strong game with 292 yards and three touchdowns. – Frank Schwab USA Today: No.16 (Last Week No.27) “An unanticipated offensive breakthrough vaulted them back to a 2-1 record and a four-way tie atop (at the bottom?) of the AFC North.” – Nate Davis ESPN: No.17 (Last Week No. 25) “None of Pittsburgh’s skill position players was projected to be a significant fantasy contributor, but Metcalf (WR31 in ADP) largely underperformed through the first three weeks with multiple drops, 11 catches and 98 receiving yards. Metcalf, though, might be turning a corner with the rest of the Steelers’ offense after finally recording a touchdown catch against the Bengals. He put up 12.1 fantasy points in the win.” – Brooke Pryor The Steelers jumped up at least six spots, and as many as 11 spots in the rankings. Everyone is putting a lot of stock in just how good the offense looked against what looks to be a quality Bengals defense this season. Pittsburgh will have their work cut out for them on a short week as they travel to Cleveland to take on the Browns. The Steelers have not won a road game on Thursday Night Football since the 2007 season. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Steelers set to have quarterback advantage in next five games
summary: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers is still an elite decision-maker at the line of scrimmage and capable of deciphering defenses as well as anyone. There are some limitations that come with being a 42-year-old quarterback behind an offensive line lacking cohesion, but Rodgers can still outplay the opposition on any given day. The Steelers won’t […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers is still an elite decision-maker at the line of scrimmage and capable of deciphering defenses as well as anyone. There are some limitations that come with being a 42-year-old quarterback behind an offensive line lacking cohesion, but Rodgers can still outplay the opposition on any given day. The Steelers won’t often have the quarterback advantage this season, especially in a division with Joe Burrow (who they’ve already beaten) and Lamar Jackson, but the road ahead looks very promising. Leading into the bye week, the Steelers will play four quarterbacks over the next five games where the tale of the tape on paper goes to Pittsburgh. Mike McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers will take on Deshaun Watson (Browns) twice, Daniel Jones (Colts) at home, Jalon Daniels (Buccaneers), and Tyler Shough (Saints) in Paris. Baker Mayfield is going to miss three weeks and will currently keep him OUT of the Buccaneers-Steelers game on October 18. The next four quarterbacks the Steelers will face before the bye week: – Deshaun Watson (twice) – Daniel Jones – Jalon Daniels – Tyler Shough pic.twitter.com/6VM1emI7Tx — Austin Bechtold (@AustinRBechtold) September 28, 2026 Tampa Bay’s Pro Bowl quarterback Baker Mayfield is expected to miss at least the next three weeks with a thumb injury. It’s a significant development for the Steelers, who play in Tampa Bay on Sunday, September 18. Jalon Daniels, an undrafted rookie out of Kansas, is set to start for the Bucs moving forward. Daniels relieved Mayfield against Minnesota on the last drive and finished 0-for-3 with an interception on the final play. Shough may be the best of the bunch and is playing well for the Saints. The 2025 second-round pick owns nine total touchdowns and is averaging 305.7 passing yards per game. He’s also a threat on the ground, rushing for 67 yards through three games. Jones suffered a season-ending Achilles injury last December, but rehabbed quick enough to be ready for Week 1. He’s off to a tough start with three touchdown passes compared to five turnovers (three interceptions and two lost fumbles). Jones has recorded a 66.3 completion percentage and an 80.8 quarterback rating. But first up is Watson, who was booed by Cleveland fans in the preseason and experienced a rollercoaster ride of ups and downs to get here. That includes Browns owner Jimmy Haslam previously calling the trade a “big swing and a miss.” After an embarrassing afternoon against the Jacksonville Jaguars (34-10), Watson and the Browns bounced back with two consecutive wins and are tied with the big three in the AFC North. In his last two games, Watson is 40-for-60 passing for 388 yards, four touchdowns, and no turnovers. Rodgers owns a 58.4 completion percentage and has thrown four touchdowns in three games, but has played better than the stats indicate. He’s taken care of the football, with only two interceptions, and played one of his best games as a Steeler in the 30-27 victory over the Bengals. Rodgers threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns for Mike McCarthy and Rodgers’ 100th career win together. Joe Burrow, Jalen Hurts, Bo Nix, Trevor Lawrence, and Lamar Jackson (twice) are some of the quarterbacks after the bye that will flip the script, but the Steelers have an opportunity to take full advantage before the difficult stretch of their 2026 schedule. Anyone from the group could have a big day against the Steelers and mitigate this, but on paper, the Steelers are in good hands with Rodgers for the next five games.
