title: Steelers-Browns preview: What to expect from Cleveland’s offense, defense in Week 4
summary: The Steelers and Browns will meet on Thursday Night Football to open the NFL’s Week 4 — and who would’ve thought the winner will take the lead in the AFC North? Both Pittsburgh and Cleveland, with new head coaches, have endured some early-season struggles to emerge with a 2-1 record to open 2026. Now, it’s […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Cleveland Browns linebacker Carson Schwesinger (49) reacts after they beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the second half at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Steelers and Browns will meet on Thursday Night Football to open the NFL’s Week 4 — and who would’ve thought the winner will take the lead in the AFC North? Both Pittsburgh and Cleveland, with new head coaches, have endured some early-season struggles to emerge with a 2-1 record to open 2026. Now, it’s a short-week divisional game — both teams will be vying for yet another gritty win on Thursday night. What to expect from the Browns’ offense Rushing YPG: 87.7 (29th) Passing YPG: 178.3 (28th) PPG: 18 (24th) RB : The Browns offense, much like the team as a whole, is in a weird spot right now. Stuck with quarterback Deshaun Watson for another season and enduring a 34-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1, it looked like Cleveland’s season was over right about when it began. But although the overall metrics still aren’t great, Cleveland has managed to put together just enough offensive production to enjoy a two-game winning streak entering Week 4, with a 23-19 win over the Buccaneers and a 21-18 win over the Carolina Panthers in the last two weeks. The Browns are one of three AFC North teams to have a new head coach in 2026, with former Ravens offensive coordinator Todd Monken taking on the role while also being Cleveland’s play caller. Under Monken, Cleveland has used some of his signature heavy-personnel tendencies (tight formations, a healthy dose of fullback Michael Burton), but are a primarily 11 personnel operation. According to NFL Pro, Cleveland currently uses it 64.7% of the time, while Monken’s highest 11 personnel rate in Baltimore was 47.2% in 2023. Some of that willingness to use more receivers has come from the Browns retooling the position group in the draft with the additions of Texas A&M’s KC Concepcion and Washington’s Denzel Boston. Concepcion, playing primarily in the slot so far, certainly hasn’t been bad, but he and Watson have struggled to connect despite the rookie seeing a number of snaps and targets. But with incredible quickness and primary usage in the short game, he remains a yards after catch threat. Wide receivers with 20+ targets and <81 receiving yards through the first three weeks of the season, since 2000. KC Concepcion joining a distinguished line of Browns pass catchers. pic.twitter.com/1tSCq2D3WR — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) September 29, 2026 However, the budding star on the Browns offense to start the season is Boston, who has emerged as a legitimate Offensive Rookie of the Year candidate through three games with nine catches for 195 yards and two touchdowns. The big-bodied wideout is a smooth mover with great hands who has developed good chemistry with Watson in the intermediate passing game. Denzel Boston getting constant chunks already through 2 games as an NFL player. all the explosive reception leaders right now are strong pass catchers that can run through contact on intermediate throws. pic.twitter.com/qAgdtwiJEy — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) September 20, 2026 While the Browns are primarily a short passing game (Watson averages just 6.6 yards per attempt), Monken’s passing concepts emphasize in-breakers that find spots in zone, and motion before the snap and into the routes to give receivers some early momentum. That’s created some easy completions; per NFL Pro, the Browns’ 4.5 yards of separation per target is the best mark in the league. Cleveland’s 71 yards after the catch over expected is also the NFL’s seventh-best mark. Still, Watson hasn’t always been able to take full advantage of his talented group of pass catchers, which also includes young tight end Harold Fannin Jr. The Browns have SEPARATORS. KC, Boston, & Jerry completely dominated their defenders. Boston with the sudden snap down, KC stemming inside & winning with violent hands over top, & Jerry attacking leverage and getting the DB turned around with the rocker step. pic.twitter.com/mKN1sZX59V — Cam White (@RouteUniverse9) September 30, 2026 We have got to find a way to hit KC on this basic. Would have been a gigantic play. pic.twitter.com/zPMo8fQg5o — Cam White (@RouteUniverse9) September 30, 2026 While Watson has a 4-0 touchdown/interception ratio over the last two games, he had at least two almost-interceptions and a number of other misses against the Panthers in Week 3. Still, Watson hasn’t lost all the traits that used to make him a productive passer in the NFL. He can be a bit of a one-speed thrower but still possesses a powerful arm. He’s also been impressively mobile at times in 2026, even if his throwing off-platform comes with highs and lows. that's ✌️ scores on the day for Harold! #CARvsCLE on FOX pic.twitter.com/gYzHTbpmYR — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 27, 2026 Still, Watson has already amassed 105 rushing yards on the season. And according to NFL Pro, while he’s faced 12 unblocked pressures this season — good for third-most in the NFL — he has not been sacked on any of them. He’s done a good job of slipping by rushers in the pocket. Watson has had to scramble more because the Browns offensive line remains a work in progress. Through three weeks, Cleveland has allowed the eighth-highest pressure rate (39.4%) and the third-worst sack rate (9.8%). The running game has been similarly unsteady. Cleveland has the sixth-worst rushing success rate in football (33.3%), with the offensive line often looking uncoordinated, especially on the team’s zone concepts. Running backs Quinshon Judkins and Raheem Sanders are hard-nosed, downhill backs, but haven’t always been able to get a runway through three weeks. Like I said bad blocking on the perimeter You have to either seal or drive out the overhang in wide zone Fannin gets good pop but doesn’t replace his hands Howard takes a very slow left step & the double with Barber isn’t tight Front side is washed and no where to cut back pic.twitter.com/kMYag1yRe0 — Mac🦬 (@tha_buffalo) September 25, 2026 I wouldn’t expect those line troubles to be fixed on a short week ahead of Thursday Night Football. Tackle Tytus Howard (knee) and guard Teven Jenkins (back) were limited in Tuesday’s practice, while center Elgton Jenkins did not participate in concussion protocol. And while healthy, both guard Zion Johnson and rookie tackle Spencer Fano have been shaky at times early in the season. This is a flawed Browns offense, and Pittsburgh should be able to find some success if its pass rush can consistently win against a struggling Cleveland line and force mistakes from Watson. Still, Watson and the Browns’ developing group of offensive weapons have managed to get the job done in recent weeks, with Watson tossing a go-ahead touchdown in each of the team’s last two games to earn a win. Sure, “the Browns is the Browns,” but that doesn’t mean there aren’t some exciting players in this offense. What to expect from the Browns’ defense Rushing YPG Allowed: 120.3 (23rd) Passing YPG Allowed: 224.0 (18th) PPG Allowed: 23.7 (18th) RP : Much like the Steelers, the Browns defense has undergone some significant transformation since these teams last met. The headliner here, of course, is that the team traded away perennial All-Pro Myles Garrett during the offseason. But Cleveland also has a new coaching staff, which means this defense is no longer the blitz-happy unit it was for the past three seasons under Jim Schwartz. Instead, the Browns have a first-time coordinator in Mike Rutenberg. So far, Rutenberg and the Browns are blitzing far less. In the three seasons under Schwartz, the Browns’ blitz rate never dipped below 28.2% in any given year. In 2026, the Browns are blitzing at a 23.3% clip, the ninth-lowest figure in the NFL. And yet, the Browns appear to be having even greater success than they did just a year ago. Last season,…

title: Seahawks Week 4 injury report: Julian Love returns to practice, Ty Okada remains out
summary: The first Seattle Seahawks practice report of Week 4. The biggest name on the list is star safety Julian Love, who was limited in practice on Wednesday. This is welcome news as Love, who injured his calf in last week’s practice, missed Week 3 against the Washington Commanders. It is still unclear whether Love will […]
full_text: The first Seattle Seahawks practice report of Week 4. The biggest name on the list is star safety Julian Love, who was limited in practice on Wednesday. This is welcome news as Love, who injured his calf in last week’s practice , missed Week 3 against the Washington Commanders. It is still unclear whether Love will be cleared to play in week four against the Los Angeles Chargers. That being said, a limited participation is still good news. As for the other players, there was only one player who was unable to participate. Unfortunately that was Seattle’s other starting safety, Ty Okada, who has not practiced at all since the start of the regular season due to a hamstring injury. Running backs George Holani (rib), and Jadarian Price (chest) were also limited in practice today, as was left guard Grey Zabel (groin) and defensive tackle Jarran Reed (foot). It is still to be seen whether any of those injuries will linger later into the week. Defensive tackle Leonard Williams was a limited participant, however that appears to be simply for rest. Others who were full participants were safety Nick Emmanwori, defensive tackle Brandon Pili, and wide receiver Rashid Shaheed. This is all good news as Emmanwori is still slowly coming back from his ankle surgery this offseason, and with Pili returning from a neck injury that kept him out of week three against the Commanders. Not listed on the injury report is Zach Charbonnet. Since he is still on the PUP list (and his 21-day practice window has not been opened), Seattle does not need to list Charbonnet. That being said, when asked about his status, head coach Mike Macdonald stated that “there is a chance” that he can practice on Thursday .

title: Seahawks All-22 review: The good and bad from the rookies against the Commanders
summary: After two weeks of seeing Seattle Seahawks rookies gradually take on larger roles, Week 3 was a much different story. Jadarian Price remained the rookie with the biggest opportunity, but a costly fumble limited him to just 19 snaps, while Beau Stephens continued to rotate at right guard and played another 27 snaps. Julian Neal […]
full_text: After two weeks of seeing Seattle Seahawks rookies gradually take on larger roles, Week 3 was a much different story. Jadarian Price remained the rookie with the biggest opportunity, but a costly fumble limited him to just 19 snaps, while Beau Stephens continued to rotate at right guard and played another 27 snaps. Julian Neal did not play a defensive snap, while Bud Clark remains on injured reserve and Avery Smith was inactive. That makes this week’s rookie review a little shorter than the previous one. There is still plenty to discuss with Price and Stephens, especially with Price’s fumble leading to a significant reduction in his workload and Stephens continuing to get valuable NFL reps. title: Dante Fowler Jr isn’t getting much playing time in Seahawks edge rotation
summary: When the Seattle Seahawks did not re-sign Boye Mafe in free agency, it seemed logical to think that veteran Dante Fowler Jr would assume at least the bulk of Mafe’s snaps. Seattle didn’t draft an edge rusher, didn’t have anything going on with the UDFA market, and didn’t sign or trade for another pass rusher […]
full_text: When the Seattle Seahawks did not re-sign Boye Mafe in free agency , it seemed logical to think that veteran Dante Fowler Jr would assume at least the bulk of Mafe’s snaps. Seattle didn’t draft an edge rusher, didn’t have anything going on with the UDFA market, and didn’t sign or trade for another pass rusher throughout the offseason, so Fowler figured to be getting a healthy workload at a small fraction of the cost of Mafe’s $20 million/year contract. Well, Fowler is getting a small fraction of Mafe’s snaps. Dante Fowler is hardly playing Through three games of the 2026 regular season, Fowler has played a grand total of 39 defensive snaps (including no-plays due to penalties), barely 20 percent of the overall defensive snap count. For perspective, DeMarcus Lawrence played 45 snaps against the Washington Commanders, Derick Hall had 35, and Uchenna Nwosu had 36. Those three either exceeded or closely matched in one game what Fowler has played over three games. Seattle has repeatedly healthy scratched Connor O’Toole and has barely played Mike Morris, so the fourth edge rusher on the team is a distant one. If we go by NextGenStats, Fowler has three pressures on 19 pass rush snaps, good for a respectable 15.8% pressure rate, with both of his quick pressures coming against the Arizona Cardinals. He has yet to chart a pressure by winning on the outside. Dante Fowler Jr's three pressures through three Seahawks games, as charted through Next Gen Stats and All-22. pic.twitter.com/2SOBEMCw8q — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) September 30, 2026 When Fowler isn’t playing, it means more work for Messrs Hall, Lawrence, and Nwosu. Here’s what the snap percentage breakdown looked like for Seattle’s main quartet last season when they were on the field , so this leaves out all of the combined games missed due to injury or suspension. Seahawks pass rush rotation snap percentages in 2025 Derick Hall : 45.8% Boye Mafe : 50% Uchenna Nwosu : 55.7% DeMarcus Lawrence : 59% Keep in mind that Nwosu’s percentage is a little lower than expected because he just came back from injury and had a fairly low snap count in his first few games. Let’s take a look at a three-week sample size (vs. Cardinals, at Rams, at Titans) when all four were available and played a normal snap count (e.g. didn’t leave the game early due to injury). Derick Hall : 99 snaps (48.7%) Boye Mafe : 78 snaps (38.4%) Uchenna Nwosu : 120 snaps (59.1%) DeMarcus Lawrence : 136 snaps (67%) Mafe played the fewest snaps but still was touching 40 percent, so the Seahawks made sure they had a healthy rotation of four edge rushers. Here’s what the snap percentages look like through Week 3 for Hall, Nwosu, Lawrence, and Fowler. Seahawks pass rush rotation snap percentages in 2026 Derick Hall : 56.8% Uchenna Nwosu : 48.9% DeMarcus Lawrence : 61.6% Dante Fowler Jr : 20.5% We expect Hall to play more, in part, because he just got paid. Lawrence is on pace for a higher snap share than last season, while Chenna is down a bit. Fowler hasn’t had a snap share this low since the 2023 season with the Dallas Cowboys. Fowler has started the season as almost exclusively a situational edge. Twelve of Fowler’s 19 pass rush snaps have come on third down. When he’s been on the field for first- and second-down, he’s primarily been on running plays. Seattle is more or less playing a three-man edge rotation with an occasional cameo from Fowler, which is considerably different from last season. Nick Emmanwori has had some snaps at edge but he didn’t play Week 1 and scarcely played Week 2. Tyrice Knight, who had some edge looks in training camp and preseason, has had a grand total of one passing down rep in the regular season, and he was tasked with covering the flat. There is no “in the aggregate” replacement happening. As to why Fowler is playing so infrequently? I’m not sure. He hasn’t been bad in a limited sample size, but there must be something that is giving Mike Macdonald and the coaching staff pause. Unless that changes any time soon, the Seahawks will be putting the onus of their edge rush productivity on three players instead of four, one of whom already declared he’s retiring after this season . Without a true, standout, 10+ sack guy among Lawrence, Hall, and Nwosu, I don’t think that’s a promising proposition as the season progresses and the Seahawks play offenses much better than they’ve faced thus far.

(Photo by Bryan Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the second day in a row, the Seattle Seahawks have added a defensive player to their practice squad. Following Tuesday’s signing of defensive tackle Gary Smith III , the Seahawks have signed linebacker Jimmy Ciarlo to their practice squad, according to a report from KPRC 2 Houston’s Aaron Wilson . Seattle also had the exemption for wide receiver signing Malick Meiga lifted, so he now counts toward the 17-man practice squad limit. The Seahawks released veteran safety D’Anthony Bell and wide receiver Julian Hicks in corresponding moves. Ciarlo, a third-year pro out of Army, went undrafted following the 2024 NFL Draft and tore his ACL during his first preseason, then with the New York Jets. He has since spent time with the Buffalo Bills, Miami Dolphins, and Tennessee Titans. He was a part of Buffalo’s final cuts from 90 to 53 in August, and had a brief stint on the Titans’ practice squad earlier this month. Across Ciarlo’s three seasons, he’s made one regular-season appearance, playing exclusively on special teams for the Bills in a Week 5 loss to the New England Patriots last season. After a tour of most of the AFC East and a short cameo with Robert Saleh in Tennessee, the 25-year-old will now try to get on the field with the defending Super Bowl champions.

title: Seahawks Week 4 power rankings: A fall from the top after surprise loss to Commanders
summary: Entering Week 3, the Seattle Seahawks were widely considered the best team in the NFL. However, when you are on top of the mountain, there is only one way to go; down. After losing to the Washington Commanders last week, the Seahawks will very likely slip down the national media power rankings this week. However, […]
full_text: Entering Week 3, the Seattle Seahawks were widely considered the best team in the NFL . However, when you are on top of the mountain, there is only one way to go; down. After losing to the Washington Commanders last week, the Seahawks will very likely slip down the national media power rankings this week. However, how far will they slip? Let’s take a look at five national media sites (NFL.com, CBS Sports, Bleacher Report (B/R), Pro Football Talk (PFT), and ESPN) to see where they rank Seattle. Both NFL.com and B/R have dropped the Seahawks down to 4th. In their ranking, NFL.com noted that Seattle’s turnovers (two from Sam Darnold, and one from Jadarian Price) were the big differences against the Commanders . An interesting thing to note as well is that NFL.com ranks the San Francisco 49ers as the new number one team in the NFL. BR meanwhile brought up the Seahawks inability to run the ball effectively in Washington . Seattle ran for less than 50 yards and only 2.4 yards per carry in last week’s loss. ESPN was the only national media site last week to not rank the Seahawks first in the NFL. However, this week ESPN did not penalize the team too much, only dropping Seattle from 2nd to 4th . In their ranking, ESPN also discussed Price’s underwhelming start. Price ranks 47th in the NFL in fantasy points among running backs – although some of that can also be credited to Seattle deploying a timeshare in the backfield. Regardless, Price’s fumbling issues will likely not help with the timeshare problem. CBS dropped the Seahawks four spots, from first to fifth in the NFL. CBS noted that despite the interceptions from Darnold, he still “did some good things in his return” and that the Seahawks will be back after this surprising loss. CBS did not issue the biggest drop in power rankings. That honor belongs to PFT, who dropped the Seahawks from first all the way to sixth best in the league . PFT did not offer much analysis in their ranking other than “we’ll find out soon whether the loss at Washington was an aberration or a harbinger.” Overall, as can be expected after an upset loss to a team with a backup quarterback, the Seahawks dropped in the national media power rankings. Entering week three, the average power ranking between the five polled sites was 1.2. Entering week four, that average has dropped to 4.6. Despite the loss, the league is still high on the Seahawks. A loss this season was inevitable. Perhaps it is better to get it out of the way early against a non-NFC West team. The Seahawks next test will be in week four against the desperate Los Angeles Chargers. Let’s see if Seattle can get back on track, or if this time next week we are discussing why the team is slipping down the power rankings once again.

(Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The more I think about it, the more I see shades of Jalen Brunson in Brock Purdy’s game. Brunson plays a type of basketball that all of us can play, winning with intangibles like craftiness and toughness and smarts. Superior use of angles and footwork and timing and accuracy. It’s not as visceral of a dominance as someone like a Wemby dunking from the 3pt line, but that mental type of dominance is actually more important for winning games. I feel like every year Brunson’s played since his early Mavs days he’s gotten better and better, adding an element to his game, better understanding the game and being able to more quickly get to his spots. That journey of constant, continual improvement of a player who’s already so finesse / touch / “upstairs” oriented feels so familiar between the point guard and the quarterback. The tight-window throws on the run for Purdy and the crazy midrange stepbacks in the NBA Finals for Brunson seem like they’re just magically happening in a burst of glory, but they’re actually culminations of years of relentless practice, film study, and growth. title: Tom Brady makes Brock Purdy declaration following 3-0 start
summary: For a long time now, many have struggled with the idea of Brock Purdy being considered an elite quarterback. But, following Purdy’s red-hot start to 2026 for the 3-0 49ers, the man he beat in his first San Francisco start in 2022 has no problem putting him in that group. Speaking as part of a […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 6: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco shakes hands with Fox Sports commentator and former NFL quarterback Tom Brady prior to an NFL Football game against the Arizona Cardinals at Levi's Stadium on October 06, 2024 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images For a long time now, many have struggled with the idea of Brock Purdy being considered an elite quarterback. But, following Purdy’s red-hot start to 2026 for the 3-0 49ers, the man he beat in his first San Francisco start in 2022 has no problem putting him in that group. Speaking as part of a segment for Fox Sports in which he put the 49ers No. 1 in his power rankings, Tom Brady made it clear how highly he thinks of what Purdy has done so far this season, with the San Francisco signal-caller the best quarterback in the NFL by a plethora of different metrics . “Brock Purdy is playing as well as anybody,” Brady said. “[He] should be considered in the tier-one QB discussions; at least, he is in my eyes.” Pressed on if Purdy can now be deemed ‘elite’, the seven-time Super Bowl champion replied: “It sure looks like it. [He’s] playing within the system, throwing the ball accurately, no negative plays, getting his team in and out of the right plays. I love the way that he’s managing every single game.” It is a huge endorsement from the man regarded as the greatest quarterback to play the game, but Brady’s assessment may receive some scrutiny depending on how Purdy performs in the next two weeks. The 49ers face the vaunted Denver Broncos’ defense on Sunday before traveling to face the Seattle Seahawks and their fearsome defensive front in a game set to be called by Fox’s Kevin Burkhardt and Brady . If Purdy can continue to impress in those matchups amid a remarkable amount of injuries to his receiving weapons, then there will likely be many more ready to join Brady in giving Purdy the ‘elite’ tag.

San Francisco 49ers Vs Arizona Cardinals 2019 | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Dante Pettis was the first the 49ers wide receiver to seemingly end up in Kyle Shanahan’s ‘doghouse’, with a career with the team that once looked extremely promising coming to an end after fewer than three seasons. The 2018 second-round pick, who had five touchdowns as a rookie and a further two in 2019, was waived by the 49ers late in the 2020 campaign after his opportunities severely diminished. But, after Pettis’ return was confirmed on Wednesday with the wideout joining the practice squad, Shanahan rejected any of suggestion of any previous ill-feeling with the veteran, who is now in his eighth year. “There was no relationship issue,” Shanahan said. “That was just how it worked out, and I think people get confused sometimes with saying people are in the doghouse and things like that. People, I think, sometimes get that confused with just coaching.” Shanahan added that the 49ers tried to make a reunion happen earlier in the year when they were short on receiving depth. “But I’ve always loved Dante. Dante’s a great dude,” Shanahan continued. “He’s got a lot of ability, done some really good things, since we let him go, in other places. And so, we tried to bring him back during training camp, when we had some guys down, and tried again this time, and this time it worked out.” With Mike Evans dealing with a rib injury and KhaDarel Hodge missing Wednesday’s practice with a knee issue, the sheer scale of the 49ers’ injuries at receiver could press Pettis into immediate action against the Denver Broncos on Sunday. Nearly six years on from the end of his first spell with the team, Shanahan sounds more than ready to rely on Pettis again if needed.

title: NFL Insiders share the price tag for the 49ers to trade for Mac Jones
summary: As long as it’s still a topic of discussion, we’ll talk about the potential outcome of the San Francisco 49ers trading for Mac Jones. The more you think it through and look at the NFL landscape, the less likely it feels that a trade will happen. But the NFL is a fickle beast, and if […]
full_text: (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images As long as it’s still a topic of discussion, we’ll talk about the potential outcome of the San Francisco 49ers trading for Mac Jones. The more you think it through and look at the NFL landscape, the less likely it feels that a trade will happen. But the NFL is a fickle beast, and if any team knows how injuries can arise out of nowhere, it’s the Niners. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano had a true-or-false section where they went back and forth debating whether J.J. McCarthy would be the only quarterback traded ahead of the deadline. Here’s what was said when the discussion turned to Jones: And the big one is probably Mac Jones . The 49ers have said they aren’t interested in dealing him, and I believe it would take a lot to change their minds. But if someone gets desperate enough, who knows? Fowler: It would take real draft capital — perhaps a Day 2 pick — to get in the door on Jones. Brock Purdy is playing at an MVP level , but he also sat out seven games last season, with Jones filling in admirably. San Francisco could be there at the end if its aging roster holds up, so it makes little sense to deal Jones right now. For a team to part ways with a second- or third-round pick in this draft would mean they think they have a legitimate shot at making the playoffs this year. Brushing aside the 49ers’ injuries When asked which team’s injury issues were most concerning, the answer was the 49ers, but with an asterisk: “The easy answer is the 49ers, but they’re 3-0 and deal with this every year, so I don’t think it’s them.” Fowler added, “If San Francisco can survive the season with its core players remotely healthy, there’s no reason why it can’t be in the thick of the playoff race in January.” Let’s establish the core players: Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle, Trent Williams, Mike Evans, Nick Bosa, and Fred Warner. Williams, Evans, and Bosa are hurt. Williams is unlikely to miss a game, but he didn’t finish Week 3. I think it’s safe to say that the core players are already banged up and impacting how the 49ers can field a team. It hasn’t reflected on the scoreboard, but that doesn’t mean it’s taking its toll. The Nick Bosa effect was on full display in Week 3. The Rams ran 57 plays. The Dolphins ran 56. The Cardinals ran 81. Of course, Romello Height, James Thompson Jr., and CJ West weren’t playing, but Bosa, in the most literal sense, has single-handedly ended drives and gotten the defense off the field. The loss of Evans will be felt against the upper-echelon defenses, like Denver and Seattle. Purdy threw the ball to Evans on half his routes against the Cardinals. That’s Brock’s go-to target this season, and the results speak for themselves. Kyle Shanahan is a mastermind and will scheme players open, but at some point, your dudes have to be better than theirs. That’s who Evans is and why you sign him. To win on third down and in key situations against the Seahawks and Broncos of the world. We’ll see how the offense handles the loss of Evans, even if it’s for a game or two, but it shouldn’t be minimized because “they deal with this every year.”
author: Kyle Posey

title: How a motivated Deebo Samuel has quickly made an impact with the 49ers
summary: The San Francisco 49ers beat the Arizona Cardinals 36-30 over the weekend, improving to 3-0 on the season as they rode a strong performance from Brock Purdy and the offense to a victory. The game started with fireworks, as the 49ers successfully executed a hook-and-ladder for an 80-yard Deebo Samuel touchdown on their first possession […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Deebo Samuel Sr. #19 of the San Francisco 49ers on his knees to pray prior to the start of the game against the Arizona Cardinals at Levi's Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers beat the Arizona Cardinals 36-30 over the weekend, improving to 3-0 on the season as they rode a strong performance from Brock Purdy and the offense to a victory. The game started with fireworks, as the 49ers successfully executed a hook-and-ladder for an 80-yard Deebo Samuel touchdown on their first possession of the game to get an early 7-0 lead. That’s how Samuel ended with one of the most interesting stat lines you’ll ever see: zero catches, 80 yards, and one receiving touchdown. So far, through three games, Samuel has caught nine passes for 159 yards and two touchdowns, with his 17.7 yards-per-catch average being a top-10 mark in the NFL. Now, that latter figure has certainly been inflated by his 80-yard touchdown, but the 49ers have quickly begun to involve him in the offense, and he’s continued to see an uptick in snaps week-by-week. Heading into the season, many of his teammates noted that Deebo was coming into the season with a chip on his shoulder, given how his 2025 season with the Washington Commanders played out and how he went unsigned deep into the offseason before getting a deal with the 49ers. Well, Samuel got an early touchdown against the Los Angeles Rams and has already started to see a good amount of volume as a receiver and even a runner. Has head coach Kyle Shanahan seen that added motivation from Samuel so far? “Yeah, I totally get that [chip on his shoulder] because for us to get him back, for us to get him how we did, for him to be available this late and things like that, that’s definitely I think going to put a chip on his shoulder,” Shanahan said about Samuel. “When that stuff happens, people say you’re descending. So, I’m sure Deebo wants to prove that. “Quickly when we saw him, we watched him on tape, we didn’t feel like he was descending. When Deebo did get the ball and he was in certain situations, you can always see that talent. He had it at the beginning of camp here. I think you see it the most when that ball’s in his hand and he gets a chance to run. Deebo is as fast as anybody at his size that I’ve been around. And he still has that.” Samuel’s shape has been a question mark in years past, and some have also attributed that to his “decline”. But he’s looked quite fresh so far to start 2026, and has been the lone healthy member of the 49ers’ receiving core. “I think Deebo’s been in great shape a lot,” Shanahan added. “I think where Deebo’s gotten in trouble is when he’s gotten injured during the year and how hard it is to stay in shape when you’re injured like that. But, I’ve seen Deebo come in like this before a number of years. “But, I also don’t want to say they’re totally wrong in that. I think Deebo, just as all these guys as they get older too, it’s not just being in shape, but it’s also sleeping right, it’s eating right, it’s the type of conditioning you do on your own, not just on the football field and things like that. And I think Deebo, going into whatever year it is for him now, I think he has a very consistent routine. The more you have a consistent routine, I just believe the easier it is to stick with. I think that’s where I’d say that you would notice the maturing in that way the most.” The 49ers have seen a good start from Samuel here to open the 2026 season, and his role may continue to grow with the team dealing with injuries.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: 49ers in review: The offense is off to a historic start
summary: The San Francisco 49ers moved to 3-0 on the season and 2-0 in the NFC West with a 36-30 win over the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday.  At one point, it seemed the 49ers would run away with the game but instead played with their food a little bit, allowing the Cardinals to sneak back into […]
full_text: (Photo by Aaron M. Sprecher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers moved to 3-0 on the season and 2-0 in the NFC West with a 36-30 win over the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. At one point, it seemed the 49ers would run away with the game but instead played with their food a little bit, allowing the Cardinals to sneak back into the game late. San Francisco were able to stave off Arizona, securing a needed victory before the schedule gets tough with the Broncos and Seahawks on the horizon. But before we look too far ahead, let’s take one last look at Week 3 and review what we can learn going into Week 4 and beyond: Brock Purdy is the league MVP… through 3 games You can tell that Purdy is feeling himself when he’s trying a jump pass along the sideline. That was simply a heat check for the quarterback. But 49ers fans can also see that Purdy is playing out of his mind. With his four-touchdown performance in Week 3 against Arizona, Purdy closed one of the best three-game stretches. Sunday marked the third time in Purdy’s career where he’s gone a stretch of three games with nine or more passing touchdowns and one or fewer interceptions: Weeks 13-15, 2023: 10 touchdowns, 1 interception Weeks 13-16, 2025: 9 touchdowns, 1 interception Weeks 1-3, 2026: 9 touchdowns, 1 interception But what makes this stretch so impressive is how he’s doing it with such a hampered receiver room. After Mike Evans went out with an injury in the second quarter, Purdy was without his top four receivers (Evans, De’Zhaun Stribling, Ricky Pearsall, and Demarcus Robinson) and didn’t target Deebo Samuel once. Despite it all, Purdy completed 8-of-12 passes for 127 yards and a pair of touchdowns. It helps that George Kittle exists, but Purdy was moving downfield with Jordan Watkins, who was banished to the shadow realm just a week ago. Maybe it’s just a hot three games, and he settles a bit, but maybe this is who Brock Purdy is now. And if that’s the case, his MVP case will only get stronger as the season goes on. And the 49ers offense is having a historically good start because of Purdy Purdy’s hot start has worked wonders for the 49ers offense. They’ve not only produced the most points scored through three games under Kyle Shanahan, but with their 36 points on Sunday, the 49ers are up to 98 points this season, one of the hottest starts in franchise history : 1949 – 115 points 1998 – 112 points 1948 – 112 points 1983 – 107 points 1965 – 103 points 2026 – 98 points Maybe something to note: the 49ers have never won a Super Bowl in a season where they scored more than 100 points in its first three games. San Francisco has, however, won two Super Bowls (1984 and 1994) when scoring between 95-99 points in the first three games, so Shanahan might have found the sweet spot. But, look at some of the quarterbacks who led the offenses above: John Brodie in 1965, Joe Montana in 1983, and Steve Young in 1998. Some of the greatest in 49ers history. And now it’s Purdy who has led the 2026 offense to a historic start. Out of curiosity, I looked at how this start compares to when Shanahan led the Atlanta Falcons to a franchise-high 540 points in 2016 with an offense that featured the league MVP Matt Ryan, Julio Jones, and Devonta Freeman. That Falcons team scored 104 points through its first three games of that season. This 49ers team is just one touchdown behind that pace. This isn’t to say the 49ers are going to score 534 points through 17 games (the franchise record is 505 points, though), but just to put into context just how good of a start the San Francisco offense is. Is it sustainable? We’ll find out. But these three games are all we have to go off of, and so far, so good. Oh, and don’t forget the offensive line Purdy and the offense’s success can be tracked back to the most scrutinized position group entering the regular season: the offensive line. That success continued against the Cardinals on Sunday. I mean, where do you want to start? The fact that the 49ers are the only team to not allow a sack yet this season or the 49ers have only had four plays from scrimmage that resulted in negative yards (non-kneels)? Both of those can be traced back to the front five. Purdy has only been pressured on a quarter of his 90 dropbacks this season. When he is pressured, he’s only completed 43 percent of his passes, but he’s yet to make a mistake. But on the 75 percent of the dropbacks he’s been kept clean, Purdy has been nearly flawless, throwing all nine of his touchdowns with a passer rating of 142.8. It can only help the confidence that Purdy has been exuding, knowing that three-fourths of the time, he’s going to have time to find the open receiver he has seemingly on every play. But the offensive line is getting it done in the run game as well. The only four negative plays the 49ers offensive line has allowed this season are: a Christian McCaffrey run for a loss of three on Sunday a Kaelon Black run for a loss of two on Sunday a McCaffrey reception for a loss of one in Week 1 a Black run for a loss of one in Week 2 The offensive line has been as good as anybody could have asked through three weeks. It makes sense that the 49ers have scored on nearly 60 percent of their offensive drives this season, because the offensive line keeps the offense moving forward. Pass rushers needed Yes, Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams should be back within the next few weeks. Sure, the Matt Judon addition helps. But the 49ers are going to need more than that. Much, much more than that. For the 49ers fans here that pay attention to the San Francisco Giants, the 49ers pass rush reminds me of the 2026 Giants bullpen. Everybody knew the Giants bullpen needed help entering the season, but Buster Posey and the Giants front office didn’t do anything to address the need, and unsurprisingly, the Giants bullpen was bad. The same could be said for the 49ers pass rush. After a 20-sack season in 2025, all the 49ers did in the offseason was draft Romello Height and wait for Bosa to get healthy, and that was enough on the edges, banking on Bosa staying healthy. Sunday against Arizona, the Bosa-less pass rush pressured Jacoby Brissett 14 times on 54 dropbacks, sacking him twice. Even with Bosa, the 49ers pass rush wasn’t showing much, recording zero sacks in Week 1, and while the 49ers sacked Malik Willis four times in Week 2, two of those sacks were Willis running himself out of bounds behind the line of scrimmage. The talent gap needs to be significantly closer between Bosa and whoever you would have as the 49ers’ second pass rusher. Judon closes that gap a little bit, but Judon didn’t have a sack in 368 snaps for the Dolphins and Bills last season and hasn’t recorded a sack since Week 17 of the 2024 season. Maybe there’s a pass rusher out there, and let’s just choose a name at random here; let’s say the Chase Young skill range would help close that gap. John Lynch and company have until Tuesday, November 10, at 1 p.m. to find help on the edges.
author: Andrew Pasquini

title: Could the 49ers be a trade fit for former 1st round WR?
summary: Amidst their current injury situation, the San Francisco 49ers looked to bring in more bodies at wide receiver ahead of Week 4. Following a tryout, they signed former second-round pick Dante Pettis to the practice squad, making another change to a room that has seen a ton of movement so far. The 49ers have dealt […]
full_text: (Photo by David Rosenblum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Amidst their current injury situation, the San Francisco 49ers looked to bring in more bodies at wide receiver ahead of Week 4. Following a tryout, they signed former second-round pick Dante Pettis to the practice squad, making another change to a room that has seen a ton of movement so far. The 49ers have dealt with injuries to Ricky Pearsall, De’Zhaun Stribling, Demarcus Robinson, Christian Kirk, and Mike Evans so far this season, forcing them to sign Khadarel Hodge, Brandin Cooks, and now Pettis to either their active roster or the practice squad. It certainly isn’t an ideal situation for San Francisco, but the 49ers are 3-0 and humming on offense regardless. Pettis was one of nine players who worked out for the 49ers on Tuesday, and he comes to San Francisco after spending the 2025 season with the New Orleans Saints. Pettis played eight games in 2025, catching nine passes for 127 yards. He’ll be a depth fill-in piece for the time being. The 49ers are expected to have much of their receiver talent back at some point this season, set aside Pearsall, so making a major move at the position may not be their top priority. But there is an intriguing receiver candidate who could be had for cheap: former first-round pick Brian Thomas Jr. Thomas, drafted by the Jacksonville Jaguars in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft, has dealt with injury and inconsistency issues through his first three years. Through three games, he has just seven catches for 88 yards, while playing only 42 percent of the team’s offensive snaps, easily a career low. Thomas had a down sophomore campaign in 2025, catching only 48 passes for 707 yards and two touchdowns, as he posted a catch rate under 53 percent. But he was excellent as a rookie, catching 87 passes for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns, making the Pro Bowl. With Thomas’s snaps continuing to dwindle, he could be a trade candidate for the Jaguars, who reportedly listened to offers this offseason. And the 49ers could be a top fit, given their need for receiver talent and desire to stay on the younger side. The 49ers have needed that field-stretcher with their injuries. That role initially went to Ricky Pearsall, then De’Zhaun Stribling, then Demarcus Robinson, and now Khadarel Hodge. Having some consistency there by trading for Thomas could be a short-term, and maybe even long-term, solution. The cost to acquire the Jaguars receiver shouldn’t be too high at the moment, given his role is dwindling, but Thomas seems more and more likely to be dealt and fits what the 49ers want as a cost-controlled receiver who can play the role of their injured receivers.

summary: Brock Purdy has already earned my immense respect, and any accomplishment from here on out is gravy. Of all the things he has left to do before truly having a legacy… Super Bowl win, league MVP, other statistical accomplishments… he would become an actually immortal legend if he’s able to turn Dante Pettis into an […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brock Purdy has already earned my immense respect, and any accomplishment from here on out is gravy. Of all the things he has left to do before truly having a legacy… Super Bowl win, league MVP, other statistical accomplishments… he would become an actually immortal legend if he’s able to turn Dante Pettis into an NFL wide receiver. I’m really curious to see how Dante has adjusted and evolved since his first stint. I was a believer initially, and I hated to see it all turn out the way he did. Maybe he’s gained an edge after bouncing around the league for a while. 49ers reuniting with former second-round pick Dante Pettis “During the 2025 season with the Saints, Pettis appeared in eight games, recording nine receptions for 127 yards and averaging 14.1 yards per catch. His most recent receiving touchdown came in 2024 with New Orleans.” 49ers practice and media schedule ahead of Week 4 matchup vs. Broncos “ Wednesday, September 30: 12:35 p.m. – Kyle Shanahan press conference 1:30 p.m. – Practice Thursday, October 1: 12:30 p.m. – Practice After practice (approx. 2:20 p.m.) – Raheem Morris press conference Following Morris – Klay Kubiak press conference Following Kubiak – Brock Purdy press conference Friday, October 2: 12:35 p.m. – Practice After practice (approx. 1:35 p.m.) – Kyle Shanahan press conference.” Brock Purdy, the NFL’s most underappreciated player “Another trait that gets lost in the Purdy discussion is his aggressiveness. Shanahan gives Brock plenty of “easy outs,” like a six-yard pass to George Kittle or a swing pass out of the backfield to Deebo Samuel. But that’s just not how Purdy is wired. More often than not, he’ll forgo gimme completions for a tight-window throw 15 yards downfield. It happens every week. It happened on his first dropback of the game to Mike Evans. It happened later on a backside throw to Kittle. He’s not interested in first-level routes. Where Brock has grown the most, even since last year, is his ability to manipulate defenders. You can only do this if you know the offense inside and out. Purdy has shown a knack for getting to the second and third progressions in the blink of an eye, but he’s holding defenders with his eyes to create bigger throwing windows. What’s been prevalent for two weeks in a row is Purdy manufacturing chunk plays against the blitz. It’d be easy for Brock to check the ball down and be content with a five-yard gain against five- and six-man rushes. But again, that’s not how he’s wired. He’s a swing-for-the-fences kind of quarterback. You think you can get over on him by bringing extra rushers? He’ll make you pay at the intermediate level. The beauty is that the throws are on time and fit within the structure of the offense.” 49ers minutia minute: Fred Warner, Osa Odighizuwa weathered career highs in snaps (paywall) “ Odighizuwa’s 71 snaps set a career high and nearly matched the number of snaps he played in the first two games combined (77). His previous career high was 64 snaps in Week 12 of the 2024 season, when he was with the Dallas Cowboys. Among the newcomers asked to play bigger roles Sunday, perhaps the biggest standout was Kareem, who logged the third-most snaps and finished with two quarterback pressures and three solo tackles. Givens, meanwhile, had an impressive 22.2 percent pass rush win rate on his nine rushes. To put that in perspective, Aaron Donald’s win rate so far this season is 21.4 percent.” Inside George Kittle’s 243-day recovery from torn Achilles “Milligan told Kittle about an athlete who came back from the same injury but had a huge difference in the size of his legs because he didn’t properly strengthen both of them before returning to field work. That athlete tore the ACL on his other leg in his first year back. Kittle bought in immediately. Within minutes of getting his cast off, he was doing pointed toe flexes. Once he shed his walking boot, Milligan instructed him on which inserts to put in his shoes, starting with 3.5 centimeters. The inserts got smaller as he progressed, down to the 0.75 ones he still wears. ….Most importantly, Kittle never lost sight of the importance of strengthening both legs. Using numbers collected from the 49ers, Milligan and Rojas knew how strong Kittle was before the injury. To ensure the legs stayed within 10% strength of each other, Milligan tracked his calf girth and put him on a strain gauge to measure his raw toe-push force against a weight room floor plate. As Milligan emphasized, the goal wasn’t just to get Kittle back on the field. It was to get him back as close to his normal level of performance as possible. That meant continuing to do the boring single leg heel raises or marble pickups for about 90 minutes to two hours every day over the course of 10 weeks…..Since there are only so many exercises you can do on the Achilles — calf raises off a wedge while standing, seated, with bands or with isolation holds — Rojas tried to challenge Kittle by forcing him to do it all from different angles to best simulate some of the sudden football movements. Some days, Rojas threw Kittle tennis balls. Other days, they chatted about life, trying to find ways to break the boredom. All the while, Kittle was deploying his secret weapon: the BFR. A BFR is, essentially, a tourniquet that Kittle strapped to his thigh to cut off the blood flow into the muscles he was working. It tricks the brain into thinking it’s taking on heavier loads than it actually is. According to Kittle, it’s a better method to work to failure when you can’t bear weight on the leg. In any Achilles recovery, the BFR is a suggested tool used a couple of times a week. Kittle used it twice every day. He also used the BFR as a recovery method, inflating it to 100% and then laying down for a few minutes so when he deflated it, the blood rushed back into the leg. “It’s really hard,” Rojas said. “It makes the easiest thing really challenging. It enabled us to push him hard from a muscular standpoint without putting a ton of stress on the Achilles that was healing … Him really pushing through some of that boring stuff and pushing that calf to fatigue is why he was able to get back so fast.” 49ers overreactions: Does Brock Purdy’s talent neutralize defensive injuries? “Of this much we are certain: The 49ers eventually will move their team headquarters and practice facility from its current location in Santa Clara. The organization is in the process of scouting sites that have more acreage for practice fields and office space. And, at least for optics, it is a good bet there will not be an electrical substation looming in the background of every video shot from their future location.”

full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers runs against the Minnesota Vikings during the game at Raymond James Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Buccaneers opened preparations for their Week 4 matchup against the Green Bay Packers with several key players sidelined. Quarterback Baker Mayfield did not participate Wednesday due to dislocating his right thumb he suffered against Minnesota. Wide receiver Chris Godwin Jr. was also held out with an ankle injury, while outside linebackers Yaya Diaby (calf/shoulder) and Rueben Bain Jr. (groin/shoulder) were among seven Buccaneers who did not practice. Running back Bucky Irving was limited with a glute injury. Linebackers SirVocea Dennis (calf) and Josiah Trotter (shoulder), along with defensive back Keionte Scott (toe), were also limited. title: Three Burning Questions ahead of Week 4
summary: The Buccaneers are in dire straits right now sitting at 0-3 and now without their starting quarterback for at least a few weeks. The start of the season has been an absolute nightmare in more ways than one for this team so what now? There are certainly more questions than answers so let’s take a […]
full_text: The Buccaneers are in dire straits right now sitting at 0-3 and now without their starting quarterback for at least a few weeks. The start of the season has been an absolute nightmare in more ways than one for this team so what now? There are certainly more questions than answers so let’s take a look at them. What are realistic expectations for Jalon Daniels? With Baker Mayfield out a few weeks with a dislocated thumb, Tampa Bay will turn to undrafted rookie free agent quarterback Jalon Daniels. A star in the preseason, Daniels is now put in a position to try and help right the ship and it will be a tall task. In terms of expectations for the young signal caller, I would be cautiously optimistic but also ready for anything. The fact is Daniels was an undrafted free agent for a reason and while you could make an argument he should have been a draft pick, it still would have been a late round pick at best. This isn’t to say Daniels can’t provide a spark. He certainly could and the Packers have been struggling so far this season. However, if fans are expecting Daniels to come in and save the season and potentially keep Baker Mayfield on the bench even after he’s healthy, I wouldn’t hold your breath. Let’s see what he can bring to the table and keep an open mind about his success in these next few games. What is going on with the Bucs offensive line? I have no idea but it needs to be a lot better especially with an inexperienced rookie now behind them. Coming into this season, Tampa Bay’s offensive line was supposed to be a big strength of this team but instead it has been one of the biggest disappointments. Tampa Bay chalked up a lot of their offensive issues last season simply on the projected starting offensive line not playing a single snap together. This season so far, they have been completely healthy so what’s the issue? Perhaps it is taking guard Cody Mauch a bit longer to get back to normal after a major injury last season, maybe Ben Bredeson has come back down to earth a bit? Graham Barton continues to be hot and cold as he has had a solid season but is still taking way too many penalties. Tristan Wirfs has bounced back after a rough week one and Luke Goedeke has had his moments but it hasn’t been good enough. There are many issues with this offense, but the Bucs certainly didn’t expect the offensive line to be one of them. They need to figure it out and do it fast. How hot is Todd Bowles’ seat? I think the answer is a little complicated. In a long-term sense, his seat is probably getting pretty hot. This isn’t just a 0-3 start; it’s an extension of the collapse last season that saw a 6-2 record end at 8-9 and missing the playoffs. For the short term, it is unlikely that Bowles would be fired mid-season. The Glazer family really like Bowles and they have never fired a head coach mid-season and I don’t see that starting with Bowles. Fans are frustrated and rightfully so, but they may have to wait until the end of the season to get their wish of change. If the Bucs end up with a losing record and miss the playoffs for the second consecutive year, it is hard to imagine Bowles returning but I wouldn’t expect the Glazers to make any rash decisions before the year is over. Bucs fans may ultimately get what they want, but they’ll likely have to wait for it.

title: Who are the Titans going to start at RG in Week 3?
summary: The Tennessee Titans were hampered by the injury bug in their Week 3 loss to the New York Giants. Starting right guard Fernando Carmona quickly exited the defeat with an ankle injury. It’s since been reported by Jordan Schultz that Carmona will be sidelined on a week-to-week basis. At least it’s not a season-ending injury […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 13: Fernando Carmona Jr. #66 of the Tennessee Titans drops back to block during an NFL football game against the New York Jets at Nissan Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans were hampered by the injury bug in their Week 3 loss to the New York Giants . Starting right guard Fernando Carmona quickly exited the defeat with an ankle injury . It’s since been reported by Jordan Schultz that Carmona will be sidelined on a week-to-week basis. At least it’s not a season-ending injury for Carmona. The rookie right guard has been an early-season revelation. He was replaced by Jackson Slater, who performed serviceably. The issue? Head coach Robert Saleh revealed Slater suffered a “significant” foot injury, but played through it. The working expectation is Slater will be sidelined even longer than Carmona will. The Titans placed them both on IR earlier this week . So who do the Titans start at RG in Week 3 versus the Baltimore Ravens? OC Brian Daboll and OL Coach Carmen Bricillo have a few options to sort through. The straightforward option would be Atonio Mafi. Mafi was added to the Titans’ 53-man roster just recently as a waivers claim. The fifth-round pick from UCLA in the 2023 NFL Draft has started just seven career games. He’s been below-average when afforded opportunities to play. We’re not convinced Mafi will be the Titans’ choice. Garrett Dellinger was recently promoted to the active roster from the practice squad. Remember that Dellinger was the biggest surprise inclusion on the initial 53-man roster. He spent the entire offseason in this offense, and certainly knows the playbook better than Mafi does. Dellinger actually played really well throughout the preseason. The former LSU product didn’t allow single a pressure or sack and scored PFF grades of 74.8, 72.3, and 80.3 in pass protection. His overall run-blocking grade was 81.9. Is rookie Pat Coogan an alternative? He’s obviously far more comfortable at center than guard. The Titans will probably start Dellinger or Mafi versus the Ravens. Would they consider reuniting with Kevin Zeitler? We’re excited to analyze whichever decision is made.

From John Portis The Washington Commanders earned their first win of the season on Sunday against the Seahawks, and now travel across the pond to face the Indianapolis Colts in a “home” matchup in London. While the Commanders have had a difficult schedule, the Colts’ first few weeks have not been easy either. They opened with a home loss to the Ravens before losing again in Week 2 to the Chiefs in overtime at Kansas City. After narrowly defeating the Texans last Sunday, both teams — the Colts and Commanders — will arrive in London with a 1-2 record. One franchise will fly home all square with a .500 record, while the other will fall to 1-3 and the accompanying long odds of making the playoffs. Jayden Daniels made the trip to London after GM Adam Peters announced he wouldn’t have surgery. He has not been ruled out of Sunday’s game against Indianapolis , but the chances of No. 5 starting seem slim after Mariota appeared more than capable last Sunday. Still, Daniels was seen throwing at practice in London. Colts quarterback Daniel Jones is healthy, but so far it has been a lackluster start for the veteran, with a total QBR of 48.5 so far this season which included three turnovers versus the Texans. Indianapolis kicker Spencer Shrader was the hero of Sunday’s game; after injuring his groin in warmups, he battled through the injury and was a perfect 4 for 4 on field goal attempts versus the Texans—including a converted long of 58 yards, and the game-winning 53-yard field goal with just 16 seconds left in regulation. He was a full participant in practice Wednesday. All-Pro running back Johnathan Taylor is having a solid start to his season, and his matchup against a suddenly stout Commanders run defense should be one to watch. Popular offseason potential (but not actual) free agent target Alec Pierce was placed on injured reserve last week after signing a four-year, $114 million contract extension in the offseason, but wide receiver Josh Downs has stepped up along with 2025 first-round selection and Pro Bowl tight end Tyler Warren. title: Commanders film session: Washington’s offensive line answered the call against Seattle
summary: The Washington Commanders offensive line has been an easy target for fan frustration and local media criticism through the first three weeks of the season. But while the questions surrounding the unit remain valid, the players have continued to push back against those narratives with their play—and their performance against the Seattle Seahawks gave them […]
full_text: Sep 27, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; Washington Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota (8) huddles up the offense against the Seattle Seahawks in the first half at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Amber Searls-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Washington Commanders offensive line has been an easy target for fan frustration and local media criticism through the first three weeks of the season. But while the questions surrounding the unit remain valid, the players have continued to push back against those narratives with their play—and their performance against the Seattle Seahawks gave them another point in their favor. Washington will have to revisit the offensive line this offseason. Center remains a position they’ll upgrade, and the team will also have to decide what it wants from Brandon Coleman entering the final year of his rookie contract. Those are conversations for later. Right now, the offensive line deserves credit for what it accomplished against the defending Super Bowl champions. Washington entered Sunday’s matchup with its season unfortunately hanging in the balance. Jayden Daniels re-injured his elbow the week before, and the team was dealing with several key injuries. An 0-3 start would have put the Commanders in a difficult position this early in the year, but the offensive line helped give the team a chance to avoid that hole. The Commanders allowed just two sacks for seven yards against Seattle, but the offensive line’s impact went well beyond that statistic. Washington would not have won this game without the performance of its front five. From left to right tackle, the Commanders consistently won reps throughout the game. Washington used a combination of schematic answers and individual execution to slow down Seattle’s pass rush, including slide protections that ensured there were multiple blockers available against Leonard Williams, most importantly, but also other interior threats. But there were also plenty of snaps where the offensive line had to win 1-on-1. Against a Seattle defensive front capable of creating pressure with four rushers and excellent in their line games, Washington’s linemen had to be technically sound, physical, and aggressive—and for much of the afternoon, they were. It was the offensive line’s most complete performance of the early season, and it deserves more attention than simply looking at the number of sacks and pressures allowed. In the latest Trap or Dive film session, I break down how Washington’s offensive line attacked Seattle’s defensive front, the schematic adjustments that helped protect the quarterback, and the individual performances that allowed the Commanders to control the line of scrimmage. Comment and let us know your thoughts on the outlook of Commanders offensive line moving forward. Subscribe to the Trap or Dive Podcast.

title: Marcus Mariota voted FedEx Air Player of the Week after clutch performance
summary: Washington Commanders backup quarterback Marcus Mariota has officially been voted the FedEx Air Player of the Week following his stellar outing in relief of the injured Jayden Daniels. When Daniels went down in Week 2 vs the Cowboys, plenty of burgundy and gold faithful held their breath. While the timeline for Jayden’s return to the […]
full_text: Washington Commanders backup quarterback Marcus Mariota has officially been voted the FedEx Air Player of the Week following his stellar outing in relief of the injured Jayden Daniels. When Daniels went down in Week 2 vs the Cowboys, plenty of burgundy and gold faithful held their breath. While the timeline for Jayden’s return to the field remains uncertain, Mariota showed everyone why having a battle-tested veteran in the quarterback room is worth its weight in gold. He didn’t just keep the ship afloat—he steered the offense with complete command and poise from the opening drive to the final whistle against the Seahawks. MM8. pic.twitter.com/CH0cWUZAOO — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) September 30, 2026 Mariota delivered a crisp, ruthlessly efficient afternoon through the air, finishing with 19 completions for 183 yards, 3 touchdowns, and zero turnovers , good for an eye-popping 110.0 passer rating . He distributed the ball with rhythm, made smart reads, and protected possession against a defense eager to feast on a backup. Marcus Mariota with 3 Pass TD in a game for the first time since Week 8, 2022 pic.twitter.com/TT2jFvRoJQ — PFF (@PFF) September 27, 2026 Yet for all his sharp throws into the end zone, Mariota’s biggest moment of the afternoon came on the ground. Clinging to a tight lead late in the fourth quarter, Washington faced a key 3rd down with the game hanging in the balance. On a zone read play, Mariota trusted his legs; he kept the ball, diving between 2 defenders, each of whom had been blocked by TE John Bates, to convert the first down—effectively icing the victory. The value of that kind of veteran savvy and situational awareness is impossible to overstate. Marcus Mariota just called game! @SEAvsWAS on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/rsIGdzozr9 — NFL (@NFL) September 27, 2026 With the fan vote locked in, Mariota takes home an honor that Commanders fans are becoming happily accustomed to seeing in D.C. The last Washington player to take home FedEx Air Player of the Week honors was Jayden Daniels himself, who brought home the award three separate times during his electrifying rookie campaign in 2024. Congratulations to Marcus on a well-deserved recognition!

title: Future Hogs – Week 4: College football players who could help the Commanders
summary: It’s funny how quickly things can change in college football. Ole Miss took down top-10 ranked LSU in Week 3, but got thumped by Florida in Week 4 the Gators potential first-round running back Jaden Baugh. LSU needed win to keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive, and they got it over Texas A&M. The […]
full_text: COLUMBUS, OHIO - SEPTEMBER 19: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes lines up prior to a play during the first quarter of a game against the Kent State Golden Flashes at Ohio Stadium on September 19, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s funny how quickly things can change in college football. Ole Miss took down top-10 ranked LSU in Week 3, but got thumped by Florida in Week 4 the Gators potential first-round running back Jaden Baugh. LSU needed win to keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive, and they got it over Texas A&M. The Aggies, now with two losses in the conference, will need to be perfect and need a lot of teams to lose to even sniff the playoffs. Texas remains the top team in the country after a narrow victory over Tennessee. Oregon keeps their playoff chances alive by taking handing USC their first loss of the season. Iowa and Mississippi State also moved up in the AP Top 25 by beating ranked teams Michigan and Missouri respectively. Mississippi State, now ranked #16, will have a chance to keep moving up the rankings in Week 5 if they can beat #7 Alabama. #14 Iowa will look to do the same by taking down #5 Ohio State. #8 Florida will look to stay undefeated against #25 Missouri. Clemson has rebounded after getting blown out to start the season, but they will have possibly their toughest challenge against #4 Miami. Here are a few players who had a good week and might be able to help the Commanders. Let me know what you think about these prospects and feel free to comment with players that stood out to you. Davis Warren | QB | Senior | Stanford Marcus Mariota did exactly what a good backup quarterback is supposed to do: run the offense effectively and do enough for the team to win. With it looking more probable that Jayden Daniels will play through his elbow injury, the team needs to have quality backups including young QBs learning and growing in David Blough’s offense. Davis Warren is an intriguing candidate for developmental quarterback. After spending four seasons at Michigan, Warren transferred to Stanford to play for former Commanders’ QB coach Tavita Pritchard. Warren is not much of a runner, but he’s not a statue. He rolls out of the pocket scrambles effectively making accurate throws on the move. The arm strength is NFL-caliber, an attribute that was on display in the win over Georgia Tech. Where he can improve is with his ball placement. Passes are catchable, but some limit opportunities for yards after the catch. With Warren being an older prospect – he’ll be 25 on draft day – it’s a genuine question of how much he’ll improve. He’s 6’2” but only 200 pounds, so he may need to add size to his frame. Warren completed 22 of 36 passes for 396 yards and three touchdowns to beat Georgia Tech. CJ Baxter | RB | Senior | Kentucky The Seahawks have a great defense and it limited the Commanders’ run game. While Kaytron Allen figures to be the big back in the Commanders’ rotation, CJ Baxter is a talented back that could also play that role. A transfer from Texas, Baxter is 6’1”, 227 pounds. He tore ligaments in his knee in 2024, but looks to be fully healthy. Where Baxter is at his best is when he is patient and reads his blocks to gain yardage. Things like his ability to evade tacklers in the open field is hindered at his size, but he quick feet that allow him to find open space. With 40 career receptions, Baxter can contribute in the passing game. In a win over South Alabama, Baxter had 149 yards and a touchdown on 16 attempts. CJ Baxter has been infinitely more productive than I thought he would this season. He is starting to show some wiggle again, I believe he’s finally healthy and he’s starting to get comfortable getting hit again pic.twitter.com/0CL1azT96a — Monty Cats (@Monty4033) September 26, 2026 Jeremiah Smith | WR | Junior | Ohio State Terry McLaurin had his best game of the season in order for the Commanders to upset Seattle. He is 31. The next leading receiver, Stefon Diggs, is 32. While the Commanders have seen promise from Antonio Williams, the team still needs impactful young players at receiver. Jeremiah Smith could be the best player eligible for the NFL Draft in 2027. He’s only a true junior and Smith is the Buckeyes’ all-time leading receiver over Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Garrett Wilson, Chris Olave, Emeka Egbuka, even Chris Carter. With elite size at 6’4”, 222 pounds, and elite athleticism, Smith has drawn comparisons to Julio Jones and Andre Johnson. Even at that size, Smith quickness and fluidity during his routes is like that of a smaller receiver. He’s savvy running his routes using head and shoulder fakes to get defenders off balance then exploiting that weakness. Once the ball is in air, Smith uses ever bit of that frame and his sure hands to secure the pass. After the catch, Smith can run away from you or run through you. There are very few weaknesses to his game. He put up career highs in Ohio State’s win over Illinois with 12 catches for 217 yards and four touchdowns. Jeremiah Smith just settled ALL DEBATES, he is the GREATEST WR prospect ever. • 12 receptions (career-high) • 217 receiving yards (career-high) • 4 receiving TD’s (career-high) The Buckeyes WR was UNSTOPPABLE in the GREATEST game of his career 🤯🍿 pic.twitter.com/DhJLDREfJc — Rookie Watch (@RookieWatxh) September 26, 2026 Top 10 Fastest Max Speed | Week 4 T4 | 21.2 MPH Jeremiah Smith @Jermiah_Smith1 WR Ohio State IGA Score™ : 94.6 #ReelSpeed pic.twitter.com/Cq4dk3ZeVE — Reel Analytics (@RAanalytics) September 28, 2026 Jaleel Skinner | TE | Senior | Louisville The Commanders’ tight ends have been blocking well to start the season, but there hasn’t been much contribution from the group in the passing game. Getting Chig Okonkwo healthy should help, but a player like Jaleel Skinner could as well. At 6’5”, 230 pounds, Skinner is more of a lot like a big receiver. The big advantage Skinner has over defenders is his straight-line speed that he uses to get open against slower defenders. It also makes him effective running after the catch. Now, Skinner is a lighter tight end, but he’ll get on the line of scrimmage and block for the Cardinals’ productive running backs. Although Louisville was upset by Wake Forest, Skinner put up 84 yards and a touchdown on four catches in the loss. Harrison Moore | C | Junior | Florida The interior of Commanders’ offensive line is a group in flux. Nick Allegretti was moved to right guard with Sam Cosmi recovering from a concussion. Lucas Patrick was signed to play center, but is nursing an injury heading into next week. If he declares for the draft, Harrison Moore should be on the Commanders’ radar. After paving the way for Haynes King at Georgia Tech, Moore transferred to Florida. At 6’4”, 293 pounds, he’s a smaller center, but that helps Moore easily reach his landmarks as a blocker. He isn’t a people mover in the run game, but he latches onto his blocks to control them. His play in Florida’s zone-heavy run scheme is a big reason why Jaden Baugh looks like a Heisman favorite. In the pass game, Moore needs to get stronger. He mirrors defenders and stays in front of them, but he can be walked back into the quarterback. Being a younger prospect, the strength will come. Moore along with rest of the Gators’ offensive line help Florida gain almost 500 yards of offense and over 300 yards on the ground on the way to beating Ole Miss. Moore is #52 in the clip below. In the pass game they have generated pressure and even had a few hits on Sam Darnold. Colin Simmons…

title: Sonny Styles named NFC Defensive Player of the Week
summary: Washington Commanders rookie linebacker Sonny Styles has officially arrived on the national NFL radar. The league announced on Wednesday that Styles was named the NFC Defensive Player of the Week for his game-wrecking performance in Sunday’s 33-31 upset win over the previously unbeaten Seattle Seahawks. Curiously, while Styles was recognized by the NFL as the […]
full_text: Washington Commanders rookie linebacker Sonny Styles has officially arrived on the national NFL radar. The league announced on Wednesday that Styles was named the NFC Defensive Player of the Week for his game-wrecking performance in Sunday’s 33-31 upset win over the previously unbeaten Seattle Seahawks. Curiously, while Styles was recognized by the NFL as the absolute best defensive player in the entire conference in Week 3, he was not among the nominees for the Pepsi Zero Sugar Rookie of the Week award. How a rookie can outplay every veteran linebacker, edge rusher, and corner in the NFC yet not crack a rookie-only ballot is anyone’s guess, but Styles and Commanders fans will gladly take the more prestigious conference recognition. And Styles earned every bit of it against Seattle. Tasked with handling green-dot responsibilities following injury to Frankie Luvu, Styles was everywhere. He spearheaded Daronte Jones’ unit with 5 tackles, two passes defended, a forced fumble, a quarterback hit, and a heads-up interception that led to a Commanders touchdown. Thanks to his ability to diagnose plays and shoot interior gaps, the Seahawks’ offense struggled with the run game and turnovers, allowing Washington to score first, and prevent Seattle from ever taking the lead from start to finish. Sonny Styles was EVERYWHERE in Washington’s win over Seattle. 4 TKL, 1 INT, 2 PD, 1 FF, 1 QBH vs Seahawks The rookie came away with his first career interception and forced a fumble against the defending champs. https://t.co/UMG5nOAliR pic.twitter.com/H3zRDCHDxE — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) September 27, 2026 Sunday’s breakout wasn’t a fluke; it was the payoff of a rock-solid foundation built over the first two weeks. Facing tough divisional challenges in back-to-back games on the road against NFC East rivals Philadelphia and Dallas, Styles stepped right into heavy snap counts and looked like an old hand. In Week 1 against the Eagles, his sideline-to-sideline pursuit helped pace a run defense that surrendered zero rushing touchdowns. Even when things went sideways in Dallas in Week 2, Styles was consistently around the football, diagnosing concepts quickly and tackling with violence in space. The speed and instincts were obvious; Week 3 saw the production match the tape. It seems likely that the rookie will raise his own bar continually as he matures as an NFL player. Styles joins Champ Bailey, Chris Horton and Brian Orakpo as the only rookies in franchise history to earn NFC Defensive Player of the Week honors since the award’s inception in 1984. https://t.co/UUeWDEZLKv — Nicki Jhabvala (@NickiJhabvala) September 30, 2026 With this award, Styles joins some elite recent company in burgundy and gold. He is the first Washington defender to win NFC Defensive Player of the Week since Ryan Kerrigan took home the honor in Week 1 of the 2020 season. On the other side of the football, Jayden Daniels took home NFC Offensive Player of the Week for his Monday Night Football ‘coming out party’ against the Bengals in his sensational 2024 rookie run. If Styles keeps flying around the field like he did on Sunday, this won’t be the last time he collects league accolades—even if the Pepsi Rookie of the Week nominations committee needs a little more time to catch up.

Those are decent numbers, but an injury ended any hopes of the Virginia product making the Dallas Cowboys’ roster this summer. Now, the Commanders are giving him a chance. But there are concerns.
